# Vamana-purana

## Chapter 1. Dialogue between Pulastya and Narada

## \|\| 1.0 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam \|*  
*devīṃ sarasvatīṃ vyāsaṃ tato jayamudīrayet \|\| 0 \|\|*

0\. Jaya (Purana etc.) should be gone over when first salute to Narayana, the best man among all human beings, goddess Sarasvati and Vyasa.

## \|\| 1.1 \|\|

*trailokyarājyamākṣipya balerindrāya yo dadau \|*  
*śrīdharāya namastasmai chadmavāmanarūpiṇe \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Lord Visnu the husband of the goddess of wealth who once disguised himself as a dwarf (Vamana) under conceit and thus snatched the three-kingdom (the heaven of deities) is saluted.

## \|\| 1.2 \|\|

*pulastyamuṣimāsīnamāśrame vāgvidāṃ varam \|*  
*nāradaḥ paripapraccha purāṇaṃ vāmanāśrayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Once the very great scholar hermit Pulastya was seated at his hermitage. The divine hermit (Devarsi) Narada asked him the story related to the Vamana Purana.

## \|\| 1.3 \|\|

*kathaṃ bhagavatā brahman viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*vāmanatvaṃ dhṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Brahmana! Please bring to notice the query being raised by me to as how Lord Visnu had held dwarf body irrespective of his being so mighty?

## \|\| 1.4 \|\|

*kathaṃ ca vaiṣṇavano bhūtvā prahlādo daityasattamaḥ \|*  
*tridaśairyuyudhe sārthamatra mai saṃśayo mahān \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A doubt on the issue which intended Prahlada, the best demon devotee to Lord Visnu for fighting against deities, is looming large in my mind.

## \|\| 1.5 \|\|

*śrūyate ca dvijaśreṣṭha dakṣasya duhitā satī \|*  
*śaṅkarasya priyā bhāryā babhuva varavarṇinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O the great Dvija! It is heard that Sati, the most beautiful daughter of Prajapati Daksa, was married to Lord Sankara.

## \|\| 1.6-7 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ sā parityajya svarīraṃ varānanā \|*  
*jātā himavato gehe girīndrasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*punaśca devadevavasya patnītvamagamacchubhā \|*  
*etanme saṃśayaṃ chindhi sarvavit tvaṃ mato 'si me \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Why did that beautiful Sati abandon her life and was reborn as a daughter to the king mountain Himalaya? And she again had become wife of lord Mahadeva. I consider you duly know the facts of that episode. Hence, remove this doubt away from my mind.

## \|\| 1.8 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ caiva māhātmyaṃ dānānāṃ caiva sattama \|*  
*vratānāṃ vividhānāṃ ca vidhimācakṣva me dvija \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О the greatest saint! Let me further know the importance of holy places and the magnificence of donations as well as the procedure for observing the number of fasts prevalent as contemplated in the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.9 \|\|

*evabhukto nāradena pulastyo sunisattamaḥ \|*  
*provāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭho nāradaṃ tapaso nidhima \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The greatest orator and chief of hermits Pulastya, in reply to the query so raised, began to explain to Narada, the great ascetic.

## \|\| 1.10 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*purāṇaṃ vāmanaṃ vakṣye kramānnikhilamāditaḥ \|*  
*avadhānaṃ sthiraṃ kṛtvā śṛṇuṣva munisattma \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Pulastya said- "O great sage! listen attentively to Vamana Purana which I will explain from bottom to top in an orderly manner."

## \|\| 1.11 \|\|

*purā haimavatī devī mandarasthaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ dṛṣṭvā grīṣmakālamupasthitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Long long ago, goddess Haimvati (Sati) said to Mahesvara seated besides her on the mountain Mandara on the five entrance of the summer season.

## \|\| 1.12 \|\|

*grīṣmaḥ pravṛtto deveśa na ca te vidyate gṛham \|*  
*yatra vātātapau grīṣme sthitayornau gamiṣyataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O the Lord of gods! Summer has entered in yet there is lack of a suitable house which could enable us to face conveniently the stormy wind and the scorching heat, the companion of summer.

## \|\| 1.13 \|\|

*evamukto bhavānyā tu śaṅkaro vākyamabravīt \|*  
*nirāśrayo 'haṃ sudatī sadāraṇyacaraḥ śubhe \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Having heard this very statement, lord Sankara replied- "O beloved with beautiful teeth!" I am always homeless and a wanderer

## \|\| 1.14 \|\|

*ityuktā śaṅkareṇātha vṛkṣacchāyāsu nārada \|*  
*nidāghakālamanayat samaṃ śarveṇa sā satī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Narada, Sati passed the whole summer under the shade of trees with lord Sankara in compliance and under adaptation to the habit as explained by him.

## \|\| 1.15 \|\|

*nidāghānte samudrabhūto nirjanācarito 'dbhutaḥ \|*  
*ghanāndhakāritāśo vai prāvṛṭkāloṣatirāgavān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. An excellent rainy season ensued just after the summer was over. It was naturally tempting to excessive attachment. All the directions were sunk in dark due to the dense grip of clouds in the sky and it resisted the movement of common people.

## \|\| 1.16 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā dakṣatanujā prāvṛṭkālamupasthitam \|*  
*provāca vākyaṃ deveśaṃ satī sapraṇayaṃ tadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Afflicted by the presence of such a scenario created by that rainy season, Sati, the daughter of Daksa, requested Mahadeva courteously.

## \|\| 1.17 \|\|

*vivānti vātā hṛdayāvadāraṇā garjantyamī loyadharā maheśvara \|*  
*sphuranti nīlābhragaṇeṣu vidyuto vāśanti kekāravameva barhiṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Mahesvara, the winds are blowing in full swing, the clouds are thundering, the lightning is sparking in the blue clusters of clouds and the peacocks are cuckooing.

## \|\| 1.18 \|\|

*patanti dhārā gaganāt paricyutā bakā balākāśca saranti toyadān \|*  
*kadambasarjjārjunaketakīdrumāḥ puṣpāṇi muñcanti sumārutāhatāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Torrents lapsed from the sky are falling on the earth, heron and stork are racing to and fro like the clouds and the trees like Kadamba, Sarja, Arjuna and Ketakl are dropping their flowers down owing to the blowing of the strong wind.

## \|\| 1.19 \|\|

*śrutvaiva maghasya dṛḍhaṃ tu garjitaṃ tyajanti haṃsāśca sarāṃsi tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*yathāśrayān yogigaṇaḥ samantāt pravṛddhamūlānapi saṃtyajanti \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. As the recluse abandons the home irrespective of its being full of prosperity, the swans are leaving shelter of reservoirs immediately having heard the dreadful sound of clouds thundering.

## \|\| 1.20-22 \|\|

*imāni yūthāni vane mṛgāṇāṃ caranti dhāvanti ramanti śaṃbho \|*  
*tathācirābhāḥ sutarāṃ sphuranti paśyeha nīleṣu ghaneṣu deva \|*  
*nūnaṃ samṛddhiṃ salilasya dṛṣṭvā caranti śūrāstaruṇadrumeṣu \|\| 20 \|\|*

*udvattvegāḥ sahasaiva nimnagā jātāḥ śaśaṅkāṅkitacārumaile \|*  
*kimatra citraṃ yadanujjvalaṃ janaṃ niṣevya yoṣid bhavati tvaśīlā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nīlaiśca meghaiśca samāvṛtaṃ nabhaḥ puṣṣaiśca sarjjā mukulaiśca nīpāḥ \|*  
*phalaiśca bilvāḥ payasā tathāpagāḥ patraiḥ sapadmaiśca mahāsarāṃsi \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. О Sambhu! look at the herd of deer running to and fro happily and the skylark is sparkling in amazement in these dark clouds. It appears from the increased quantum of rain that the warriors are walking on the trees so as to escape themselves from getting wet. The rivers are flowing suddenly with galloping steps. О Candrasekhara! what scope there is for surprise if the wife of a corrupt man loses her chastity. The sky is covered by the blue clouds, Sarja tree by flowers, Kadamba with buds, bilva with fruits, rivers with water and reservoirs with the lotus petals.

## \|\| 1.23 \|\|

*kāle suraudre nanu te bravīmi \|*  
*gṛhaṃ kuruṣvātra mahācajalottame sunirvṛtā yena bhavāmi śaṃbho \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О Sankara! In such a strange, intolerable and dreadful phase of time, construct a house properly on this great and best mountain so that I could feel convenient and get rid of worry.

## \|\| 1.24-25 \|\|

*itthaṃ trinetraḥ śrutirāmaṇīyakaṃ śrutvā vaco vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe \|*  
*na me 'sti vittaṃ gṛhasaṃcayārthe mṛgāricarmāvaraṇaṃ mama priye \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mamopavītaṃ bhujageśvaraḥ śubhe karṇe 'pi padmaśca tathaiva piṅgalaḥ \|*  
*keyūramekaṃ mama kambalastvahirdvitīyamanyo bhujago dhanañjayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Having heard those humble words from Sati, lord Sankara (having tree eyes) replied- "O beloved! I have not sufficient wealth to construct a house. See that I have a mere tiger's hide on my body. О nice lady! King Cobra (the king of serpent) is my sacred thread. The two serpents i.e. Padma and Pingala are my ear-rings and Kambala and Dhananjaya serpents are my armlets (Bajubanda).

## \|\| 1.26 \|\|

*savyetare takṣaka uttare tathā \|*  
*nīlo 'pi nīlāñjanatulyavarṇaḥ śroṇītaṭe rājati supratiṣṭhaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The serpent Asvatara at right and Taksaka at left wrist are my two bangles (Kangana). The blue colour serpent (like Nilanjana) is around my waist.

## \|\| 1.27 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*iti vacanamathograṃ śaṅkarātsā mṛḍānī ṛtamapi tadasatyaṃ śrīmadākarṇya bhītā \|*  
*avanitasamavekṣya svāmino vāsakṛcchrāt parivadati saroṣaṃ lajjayocchvasya coṣm \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Pulastya said- "Having heard this hard but true and impressive yet appearing false statement from Mahadeva, Sati was caught in the grip of fright. She bent her eyes on earth, filled with anger and shame owing to the trouble of a lack of residence and began to say with a long expiration.

## \|\| 1.28 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ hi devadeveśa prāvaṭkālo gamiṣyati \|*  
*vṛkṣamūle sthitāyā me suduḥkhena vadāmyataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The goddess said- “O god of gods (Devadevesa)! how will this rainy season pass by living painfully under the shade of a tree? Hence, I pray you for the construction of a house.”

## \|\| 1.29 \|\|

*śaṅkara uvāca \|*  
*ghanāvasthitadehāyāḥ prāvṛdkālaḥ prayāsyati \|*  
*yathā'mbudhārā na tava nipativyanti vigrahe\|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. God Sankara said- О goddess! you will pass this rainy season by placing your body above the clouds and this will rescue your body from the torrents of heavy water drops.

## \|\| 1.30 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca*  
*tato harastadabanakhaṇḍamunrata- māruhya tasthau saha dakṣakanyayā \|*  
*tato'bhavannāma tadeścarasya jīmūtaketustviti viśrutaṃ divi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Pulastya said- "Lord Mahadeva then climbed upon the uprising cluster of clouds with Sati, the daughter of Daksa. He seated himself there calmly. Since then, he got popularity with the name in heaven as Jimutaketu.

## Chapter 2. Story of the birth of Nara and description of Destruction

## \|\| 2.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca*  
*tatastrinetrasya gataḥ prāvṛṭkālo ghanopari \|*  
*lokānndakarī ramyā śarat samabhavanmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Pulastya said- " Thus, the rainy season was passed by Mahadeva (trinetra) seated above the clouds. Then there began the pleasant Sarada (season), О sages!

## \|\| 2.2 \|\|

*tyajanti nīlāmbudharā nabhastalaṃ vṛkṣāṃśca kaṅkāḥ saritastaṭāni \|*  
*padmāḥ sugandhaṃ nilayāni vāyasā rururviṣāṇaṃ kaluṣaṃ jalāśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. (On commencement of Sarada) the blue clouds abandoned the sky, the herons abandoned the shelter of trees and the rivers abandoned their banks. Lotus flowers started releasing fragrance and the crows left the shelter of their nests. The antelope stage (Rurumrga) shed their horns and the reservoirs got clean and pure water.

## \|\| 2.3 \|\|

*vikāsamāyanti ta paṅkājāni candrāṃśavo bhānti latāḥ supuṣpāḥ \|*  
*nandanti hṛṣṭānyapi gokulāni santaśca saṃtoṣamanuvrajanti \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The lotus started blossoming, pure light began to spread everywhere, the creepers bore flowers, the cows became healthy and happy (owing to abundant grass) and the gentlemen got contentment.

## \|\| 2.4 \|\|

*sarassu padma gagane ca tārakā jalāśayeṣveva tathā payāṃsi \|*  
*satāṃ ca cittaṃ hi diśāṃ mukhaiḥ samaṃ vaimalyamāyānti śaśaṅkakāntayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The lotus in ponds, the stars in the sky, the water in the reservoirs, the directions and the heart of gentlemen as also the moonlight became all clean and holy.

## \|\| 2.5 \|\|

*etādṛśe haraḥ kāle maghapṛṣṭhādhivāsinīm \|*  
*satīmādāya śailendraṃ mandaraṃ samupāyayau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At this all-pleasing atmosphere, lord Sankara came down from his seat above the clouds and with Sati, he descended on the great Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 2.6 \|\|

*tato mandarapṛṣṭhe 'sau sthitaḥ samaśilātale \|*  
*rarāma śaṃbhurbhagavān satyā saha mahādyutiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He then engrossed himself in coition with Sati on a plane boulder at Mandaracala mountain.

## \|\| 2.7 \|\|

*tato vyatīte śaradi pratibuddhe ca keśave \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prajāpatiśreṣṭho yaṣṭumārabhata kratum \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When the Sarada (the season) was over and lord Kesava (Visnu) awakened, Prajapati Daksa commenced yajna (the offering).

## \|\| 2.8 \|\|

*dvādaśeva sa cādityāñ śakrādīṃś ca surottamān \|*  
*sakaśyapān samāmantrya sadasyān samacīkarat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He duly invited twelve Adityas and Kasyapa etc., sages along with Indra etc., eminent gods and made them participants to the yajna so arranged.

## \|\| 2.9-11 \|\|

*arundhatya ca sahitaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ śaṃsitavratam \|*  
*sahānasūyayātriṃ ca saha dhṛtyā ca kauśikam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ahalyayā gautamaṃ ca bharadvājamamāyayā \|*  
*candrayā sahitaṃ brahmannṛṣimaṅgīrasaṃ tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*āmantrya kṛtāvāndakṣaḥ sadasyān yajñasaṃsadi \|*  
*vidvān guṇasaṃpannān vedavedāḍgapāragān \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. О Brahmins! he thus, invited Arundhati with great resolute Vasistha, Anusuya with Atri, Dhrti with Kansika, Ahalya with Gautama, A may a with Bharadvaja and Candra with Angira for participating in that yajna. Daksa, after due invitation, nominated to that yajna all hermits as members who were meritorious, learned and conversant with the Vedas and all their parts.

## \|\| 2.12 \|\|

*dharmaṃ ca sa samāhūya bhāryayāhiṃsayā saha \|*  
*nimantrya yajñavāṭasya dvārapālatvamādiśat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He invited Dharma with his wife Ahimsa and appointed him as gatekeeper to the pavilion of that yajna.

## \|\| 2.14-15 \|\|

*ariṣṭaneminaṃ cakre idhmāharaṇakāriṇam \|*  
*bhṛguṃ ca mantrasaṃskāre samyag dakṣaṃ prayuktavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tathā candramasaṃ devaṃ rohiṇyā sahitaṃ śucim \|*  
*dhanānāmādhipatye ca yuktavān hi prajāpatiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Daksa assigned Aristanemi to the work of collecting the required fuel (Samidha) for yajna and appointed with due procedure, Bhrgu for the work of processing hymn (Mantra Samskara). And Prajapati Daksa appointed Candra with his wife Rohini as treasurer to that project.

## \|\| 2.16 \|\|

*jāmātṛduhitṛśvaiva dauhitrāṃśca prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*saśaṅkarāṃ satīṃ muktvā makhe sarvān nyamantrayat \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Prajapati invited all his son-in-laws, daughters and their children (Dauhitras) except Sati and Sankara in that yajna.

## \|\| 2.17 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kimarthaṃ lokapatinā dhanādhyakṣo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭho variṣṭho 'pi ādyo 'pi na nimantritaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Narada said- "Why did Daksa, the Prajapati, not invited Mahesvara in spite of being his senior, superior, principal, prime (Adya) and treasurer?"

## \|\| 2.18 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca*  
*jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭho variṣṭho 'pi ādyo 'pi bhagavāñśivaḥ \|*  
*kapālīli viditveśo dakṣeṇa na nimantritaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Pulastya replied- "He considered him a native of cremation ground (Kapali) in spite of being his senior, superior, principal, prime and treasurer. Hence, he did not invite him."

## \|\| 2.19 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kimarthaṃ devatāśreṣṭhaḥ śūlapāṇistrilocanaḥ kapālī bhagavāñjātaḥ karmaṇā kena śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The great god Narada said- "Why and owing to which act, did lord Sankara, three eyed and trident holder become Kapali (native of cremation ground)?

## \|\| 2.20 \|\|

*śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā kathāmetāṃ purātanīm \|*  
*proktamādipurāṇe ca brahmaṇāvyaktamūrttinā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Pulastya said- "Listen carefully to an ancient story being now told by me and which had been once told by lord Brahma, an intangible god and as contemplated in Adipurana."

## \|\| 2.21-22 \|\|

*purā tvekārṇavaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*naṣṭaṭandrārkanakṣatraṃ praṇaṣṭapavanānalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*apratarkyamavijñeyaṃ bhāvābhāvavivarjitam \|*  
*nimagnuparvatataru tamobhūtaṃ sudurdasam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. In the very distant past, this entire universe with its movable and immovable properties was only an ocean. There were nowhere any stars like the moon, the sun, all planets, wind and fire-like illuminating substances. The state of the then world was unknown, inaccessible to imagination and without presence or absence of anything. All mountains and trees were in the belly of the ocean and the entire universe was surrounded by darkness and in a pathetic condition.

## \|\| 2.23 \|\|

*tasmin sa śete bhagavān nidrāṃ varṣasahasrikīm \|*  
*rātryante sṛjate lokān rājasaṃ rūpāsthitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Lord Visnu sleeps for several thousand years in that oceanic stage of universe and he creates all worlds (lokas) under his Rajas formation when that prolong night is over.

## \|\| 2.24 \|\|

*rājasaḥ pañcavadano vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \|*  
*sraṣṭā carācarasyāsya jagato 'dbhutadarśanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. His Rajas form was the creator of this universe with its movable and immovable properties; it was strange in look, having its five mouths and it was fully conversant with the Vedas and their parts.

## \|\| 2.25 \|\|

*tamomayastathaivānyaḥ samudbhūtastrilocanaḥ \|*  
*śūlapāṇiḥ kaparddī ca akṣamālāṃ ca darśayan \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Similarly, one more Purusa (man) was bom at that time. He was with Tamas property, three-eyed, trident holder, leaper (kapardi) and a garland of Rudraksa was around his neck.

## \|\| 2.26 \|\|

*tato mahātmā hyasṛjadahaṅkāraṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*yenākrāntāv ubhau devau tāveva brahmaśaṅkarau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The supreme soul (Paramatma) then originated the fierce ego which gripped Brahma and Sankara, both the gods.

## \|\| 2.27 \|\|

*ahaṅkārāvṛto rudraḥ pratyuvāca pitāmaham \|*  
*ko bhavāniha saṃprāptaḥ kena sṛṣṭo 'si māṃ vada \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Sankara under the intoxication of ego said to Brahma- "Who are you to come to this place? Tell me who has created you?"

## \|\| 2.28 \|\|

*pitāmaho 'pyahaṅkārāt pratyuvācātha ko bhavān \|*  
*bhavato janakaḥ ko 'tra jananī vā taducyatām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Brahma too replied with ego- "First tell me who you are and who your parents are?"

## \|\| 2.29-30 \|\|

*ityanyonyaṃ purā tābhyāṃ brahmeśābhyāṃ kalipriya \|*  
*parivādo 'bhavat tatra utpattirbhavato 'bhavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhavānpyantarikṣaṃ hi jātamātrastadotpatat \|*  
*dhārayannatulāṃ vīṇāṃ kurvan kilakilādhvanim \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. О Narada, loved by Kali! thus, a dispute was arisen between lord Brahma and Sankara in the distant past. You yourself were also bom there. You also moved to the sky (space) above immediately after- birth. An excellent lyre was in your hands and a tremulous voice played on your lips.

## \|\| 2.31 \|\|

*tato vinirjitaḥ śaṃbhurmāninā padmayoninā \|*  
*tasthāvadhomukho dīno grahākrānto yathā śaśī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Lord Brahma (bom from the lotus) then defeated Sankara (the administrator of loka). He therefore put his head facing the ground like a frightened moon.

## \|\| 2.32-33 \|\|

*parājite lokapatau devena parameṣṣinā \|*  
*krodhāndhakāritaṃ rudraṃ pañcamo 'tha mukho 'brovīt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ahaṃ te pratijānāmi tamomūrto trilocana \|*  
*digvāsā vṛṣabhārūḍho lokakṣayakaro bhavān \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The fifth mouth of Lord Brahma subsequent to the defeat he had given to Sankara, burning in excess fury, said- О threeeyed and with Tamah property Purusa! I am familiar to you. You are naked (Digambara), Vrsarohi (bull rider) and destroyer of this entire universe.

## \|\| 2.34 \|\|

*ityuktāḥ śaṅkaraḥ kruddho vadanaṃ ghoracakṣuṣā \|*  
*nirdagdhukāmastvaniśaṃ dadarśa bhagavānajaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. As a reaction to that very statement, lord Sankara opened his third fierce eye with the intention to bum into ashes Lord Brahma. He thus stared at his fifth mouth.

## \|\| 2.35 \|\|

*tatastrinetrasya samudbhavanti vaktrāṇi pañcātha sudarśanāni \|*  
*śvetaṃ ca raktaṃ kanakāvadātaṃ nīlaṃ tathā piṅgajaṭaṃ ca śubhram \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then there had arisen five mouths (heads) to lord Sankara. One was of white, the other red, golden, blue and yellow colour respectively.

## \|\| 2.36 \|\|

*vaktrāṇi dṛṣṭvār'kasamāni sadyaḥ paitāmahaṃ vaktramuvāca vākyam \|*  
*samāhatasyātha jalasya budbudā bhavanti kiṃ teṣu parākramo 'sti \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Having seen the automatic origin of the five heads with sun splendour, the fifth head of Brahma said- "Bubbles naturally arise due to force of stream in water but void from the valour and meaningless?"

## \|\| 2.37 \|\|

*tacchrutvā krodhayuktena śaṅkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*nakhāgreṇa śiraśchinnaṃ brāhmaṃ paruṣavādinam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Having heard such harsh words, lord Sankara cut that head of Brahma off by a hard blow of nail.

## \|\| 2.38 \|\|

*tacchinnaṃ śaṅkarasyaiva savye karatale 'patat \|*  
*patate na kadācicca tacchaṅkarakarācchiraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The head so cut-off fell on the left palm of Lord Sankara. It was stuck there and could not be removed.

## \|\| 2.39-40 \|\|

*atha krodhāvṛtenāpi brahmaṇādbhuvatakarmaṇā \|*  
*sṛṣṭastu puruṣo dhīmān kavacī kuṇḍalī śarī \|\| 39 \|\|*

*dhanuṣpāṇirmahābāhurbāṇaśaktidharo 'vyayaḥ \|*  
*caturbhujo mahātūṇī ādityasamadarśanaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Lord Brahma in a fantasy of anger then created something phenomenal. It was the origin of a wiseman (Purusa) duly equipped with kavaca kundala (shield) and arrows. He was an archer, long armed, mighty, avyaya (robust), four-armed and a great bowman. His aura was shining like the sun.

## \|\| 2.41 \|\|

*sa prāha gaccha durbuddhe mā tvāṃ śūlin nipātaye \|*  
*bhavān pāpasamāyuktaḥ pāpiṣṭhaṃ ko jighāṃsati \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He said - "O wicked Sankara! I will not kill you if you leave this place at once. You are an evildoer and who will make his hands dirty by killing a sinner like you?

## \|\| 2.42 \|\|

*ityuktāḥ śekarastena puruṣeṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*trapāyukto jagāmātha rudro badarikāśramam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. As a response to the statement, Rudra ashamed left that place immediately for Badrikasrama.

## \|\| 2.43-44 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇasthānaṃ parvate hi himāśraye \|*  
*sarasvatī yatra puṇyā standane saritāṃ varā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tatra gatvā ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇamuvāca ha \|*  
*bhikṣāṃ prayaccha bhagavan mahākāpāliko 'smi bhoḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. So call Badrikasrama is situated at great Himalaya where Nara-Narayana reside and the greatest river Sarasvati flows there. Having approached there and found Nara- Narayana, lord Sankara said - "O lord! I am Mahakapalika. Please give me alms.”

## \|\| 2.45 \|\|

*ityukto dharmaputrastu rudraṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*savyaṃ bhujaṃ tāḍayasva triśūlena maheśvara \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The son of Dharma (Narayana) replied- "O Mahesvara! Give a blow with the trident to my left arm.

## \|\| 2.46 \|\|

*nārāyaṇavacaḥ śrutvā triśūlena trilocanaḥ \|*  
*savyaṃ nārāyaṇabhujaṃ tāḍayāmāsa vegavān \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In compliance with these words, lord Sankara hit hard on the left arm of Narayana with the trident.

## \|\| 2.47-48 \|\|

*triśūlābhihatānmārgāt tisro dhārā viniryayuḥ \|*  
*ekā gaganamākramya sthitā tārābhimamḍitā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dvitīyā nyapatad bhūmau tāṃ jagrāha tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*atristasmāt samudbhūto durvāsāḥ śaṅkarāṃśataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Three streams emanated from the points made by the trident at the arm of Narayana. One stream accessed upward and accompanied with the galaxy in the sky. The other fell down to the earth and was entertained by the great ascetic Atri. Being it the ray of Sankara, it gave birth to Durvasa.

## \|\| 2.49 \|\|

*tṛtīyā nyapatad dhārā kapāle raudradarśane \|*  
*tasmācchiśuḥ samabhavat saṃnaddhakavaco yuvā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The third stream was dropped on a dreadful skull (Kapala) and a baby got its birth therefrom. He immediately turned into a young-chap of dark-complexion equipped with a shield, bow and arrows.

## \|\| 2.50 \|\|

*śyāmāvadātaḥ śaracāpapāṇir garjanyathā prāvṛṣi toyado 'sau \|*  
*itthaṃ bruvan kasya viśātayāmi skandhācchiras tālaphalaṃ yathaiva \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. As the clouds thunder during rainy season, such was the dreadful voice of that young-chap. He was saying - "Who is to be beheaded by me like the fruit of Tala?"

## \|\| 2.51 \|\|

*taṃ śakaro 'bhyetya vaco vabhāṣe naraṃ hi nārāyaṇabāhujātam \|*  
*nipātayainaṃ nara duṣṭavākyaṃ brahmātmajaṃ sūryaśataprakāśam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Lord Sankara approached the man so bom from the arm of Sri Narayana and said- "O Nara! Kill this man originated by Brahma, harsh in tongue but glowing with the light of a hundred suns simultaneously."

## \|\| 2.52 \|\|

*ityevamuktaḥ sa tu śaṅkareṇa ādyaṃ dhanustvājagavaṃ prasiddham \|*  
*jagrāha tūṇāni tathākṣayāṇi yuddhāya vīraḥ sa matiṃ cakāra \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In compliance with the order so given, that warrior picked-up his bow known as Adya Ajagava and Tunlra and decided to battle.

## \|\| 2.53 \|\|

*tataḥ prayuddhau subhṛśaṃ mahābalau1 brahmātmajo bāhubhavaśca śārvaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ sahasraṃ parivatsarāṇāṃ tato haro 'bhyetya virañcimūce \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The son originated by Brahma and the Sankara-purusa so originated from the arm of Narayana thus, fought a fierce battle as long as many thousand divine years lapsed. Sri Sankara then approached lord Brahma and said.

## \|\| 2.54 \|\|

*jitastvadīyaḥ puruṣaḥ pitāmaha nareṇa divyadbhutakarmaṇā balī \|*  
*mahāpṛṣatkairabhipatya tāḍitastadadbhutaṃ ceha diśo daśaiva \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О Pitamaha! It is really surprising that Nara, an excellent warrior has defeated your purusa as a result of giving blows with his great arrows spread at the time of the battle around the ten directions.

## \|\| 2.55 \|\|

*brahma tamīśaṃ vacanaṃ babhāṣe nehāsya janmānyajitasya śaṃbho \|*  
*parājitaśceṣyate 'sau tvadīyo naro madīyaḥ puruṣo mahātmā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Brahma said that Isa - "This undefeated (Ajita) purusa has not been bom here for enduring defeat from others. If it is essential to declare one defeated, your Nara is the man who actually is defeated. The Purusa created by me is the greater warrior.

## \|\| 2.56 \|\|

*ityevamukto vacanaṃ trinetraścikṣepa sūrye puruṣaṃ viriñceḥ \|*  
*naraṃ narasyaiva tadā sa vigrahe cikṣepa dharmaprabhavasya devaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. As a reaction to that statement, lord Sankara threw the Purusa created by Brahma in the sun's orbit and threw that Nara in the body of Dharmaputra Nara.

## Chapter 3. Dialogue between Hari and Наra

## \|\| 3.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ karatale rudraḥ kapāle dāruṇe sthite \|*  
*saṃtāpamagamad brahmaṃścintayā vyākulendriyaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Pulastya said - "O Brahmins! As the dreadful skull (head) was stuck to the palm of lord Sankara, he fell in the grip of anxiety and gloom. It caused severe grief to him.

## \|\| 3.2 \|\|

*tataḥ samāgatā raudrā nīlāñcanacayaprabhā \|*  
*saraktamūrddhajā bhīmā brahmahatyā harāntikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then Brahmahatya (sin of Brahmana's murder) came near lord Sankara. She was of a complexion like a cluster of Nilanjana; her hair were of red colour; she was in creeping gesture and dreadful.

## \|\| 3.3 \|\|

*tāmāgatāṃ haro dṛṣṭvā papraccha vikarālinīm \|*  
*kāsi tvamāgatā raudre kenāpyarthena tadvada \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Having seen that dreadful figure, lord Sankara asked - "O dreadful lady! Tell me who you are and for what purpose you have come here?"

## \|\| 3.4 \|\|

*kapālinamathovāca brahmahatyā sudāruṇā \|*  
*brahmavadhyāsmi saṃprāptāṃ māṃ protīccha trilocana \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. That dreadful Brahmahatya replied - "Trilocana! Accept me. I am Brahmahatya come to you."

## \|\| 3.5 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ brahmahatyā viveśa ha \|*  
*triśūlapāṇinaṃ rudraṃ saṃpratāpitavigraham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. With these words, Brahmahatya entered into the body of Rudra who was already suffering from anxiety.

## \|\| 3.6 \|\|

*brahṇahatyābhibhūtaśca śarvo badarikāśramam \|*  
*āgacchanna dadarśātha naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Bearing so heavy a burden of Brahmahatya, lord Sankara returned to Badrikasrama but he did not see there the saints i.e. Nara and Narayana.

## \|\| 3.7 \|\|

*adṛṣṭvā dharmatanayau cintāśokasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma yamunāṃ snātuṃ sāpi śuṣkajalābhavat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. His pain was aggravated when he could not find both the saints. In the vagary of sheer agony and worry, he approached river Yamuna but her water was dried up when he got down for a bath.

## \|\| 3.8 \|\|

*kālindīṃ śuṣkasalilāṃ nirīkṣya vṛṣaketanaḥ \|*  
*plakṣajāṃ snātumagamadantarddhānaṃ ca sā gatā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Having seen Yamuna with no water, he went to Plaksaja (Sarasvati) for bath but as he could enter in its water, she vanished from there.

## \|\| 3.9 \|\|

*tatonu puṣkarāraṇyaṃ māgadhāraṇyameva ca \|*  
*saindhavāraṇyamevāsau gatvā snāto yathecchayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He then visited Puskararanya, Magadharanya and Saindhavaranya and took a bath frequently to the extent desired by him.

## \|\| 3.10 \|\|

*tathaiva naimiṣāraṇyaṃ dharmāraṇyaṃ tatheśvaraḥ \|*  
*snāto naiva ca sā raudrā brahmahatyā vyamuñcata \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He similarly, took a bath in Naimisaranya and Dharmaranya also but could not be escape from the tight grip of that fierce Brahmahatya.

## \|\| 3.11 \|\|

*saritsu tīrtheṣu tathāśrameṣu puṇyeṣu devāyataneṣu śarvaḥ \|*  
*samāyuto yogayuto 'pi pāpānnāvāpa mokṣaṃ jaladadhvajo 'sau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In spite of his (Sankara) being a Yogi and a number of pilgrimages he made, he took a dip in the sacred rivers, visited a number of hermitages and temples, yet he could not get-rid-of the evil so stuck to him.

## \|\| 3.12 \|\|

*tato jagāma nirviṇṇaḥ śaṅkaraḥ kurujāṅgalam \|*  
*tatra gatvā dadarśātha cakrapāṇiṃ khagadhvājam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Aggrieved at the failure of all his efforts for regrettable, lord Sankara ultimately visited Kurujangala. He saw there lord Visnu (the rider on eagle and a discus in his hand).

## \|\| 3.13 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|*  
*kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā haraḥ stotramudīrayat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Having seen with his eyes Pundarikaksa (Sri Narayana) with conch, discus and mace in his hands, he began to pray him.

## \|\| 3.14 \|\|

*hara uvāca \|*  
*namaste devatānātha namaste garuḍadhvaja \|*  
*śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇe vāsudeva namo 'stu te \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Sankara prayed - "O the king of gods! I salute you. О rider on Garuda! Accept my salute, О Vasudeva with conch, discus and mace in your hands! I salute you."

## \|\| 3.15 \|\|

*namaste nirguṇānanta aprarkyāya vedhase jñānājñāna nirālamba sarvālamba namo 'stu te \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Salute to everlasting, beyond three properties, inaccessible to imagination, the creator. Salute to the former of knowledge and ignorance, without any support and support to all creatures.

## \|\| 3.16 \|\|

*rajoyukta namaste 'stu brahmamūrte sanātana \|*  
*tvayā sarvamidaṃ nātha jagatsṛṣṭaṃ carācaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Salute to god with Rajas, immortal and Brahma in itself. О lord! You have created this entire universe with both movable and immovable properties.

## \|\| 3.17 \|\|

*sattvādhiṣṭhita lokeśa viṣṇumūrte adhokṣaja \|*  
*prajāpāla mahābāho janārdana namo 'stu te \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Salute to the resort of Sattva property, the god of world, the formation as Visnu, destroyer of sins, god of defending, most chivalrous and Janardana.

## \|\| 3.18 \|\|

*tamomūrtte ahaṃ hyeṣa tvadaṃśakrodhasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*guṇābhiyukta deveśa sarvavyāpin namo 'stu te \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О image of Tama! I am originated from the anger a particle of your entity. Salute to omnipresent, god of gods and all meritorious.

## \|\| 3.19 \|\|

*bhūriyaṃ tvaṃ jagannātha jalāmbarahutāśanaḥ \|*  
*vāyurbuddhirmanaś cāpi śarvarī tvaṃ namo 'stu te \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Salute to the ruler of this universe existing in the varied forms like the earth, water, ether, fire, wind, wisdom, mind and the night.

## \|\| 3.20 \|\|

*dharmo yajñastapaḥ satyaṭamahiṃsā śaucamārjavam \|*  
*kṣamā dānaṃ dayā lakṣamīrbrahmacaryaṃ tvamīśvara \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О god! You are religion (Dharma), austerity, truth, non-violence, purity, simplicity, forgiveness, generosity, kindness, wealth and celibacy in yourself.

## \|\| 3.21 \|\|

*tvaṃ sāṅgāścaturo vedāstvaṃ vedyo vedapāragaḥ \|*  
*upavedā bhavānīśa sarvo 'si tvaṃ namo 'stu te \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О god! You are the four Vedas with their parts (angas), you are the physician (Vaidya) and the best known to Vedas’ essence. You are Upaveda (scriptures) and everything you are. I salute you.

## \|\| 3.22 \|\|

*namo namaste 'cyutata cakrapāṇe namo 'stu te mādhava mīnamūrte \|*  
*loke bhavān kāruṇiko mato me trāyasva māṃ keśva pāpabandhāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Salute to Acyuta, Cakrapani, frequently. Salute to fish-form Madhava. I consider you to be kind to the world. О Kesava! Absolve me from the bondage of evils.

## \|\| 3.23 \|\|

*mamāśubhaṃ nāśaya vigrahasthaṃ yad brahmahatyābhibhavaṃ babhūva \|*  
*dagdho 'smi naṣṭo 'smyasamīkṣyakārī punīhi tīrtho 'si namo namaste \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Destroy the evils entered into my body as a result of the murder of the Brahmana committed by me. Owing to the act performed deliberately, I have burnt and destroyed myself in the fire of anxiety. You are holy and hence bless me with the reward of purity. I salute you frequently.

## \|\| 3.24 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ stutaścakradharaḥ śaṅkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*provāca bhagavān vākyaṃ brahmahatyākṣayāya hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Pulastya said - "At the prayer so submitted by Lord Sankara, Lord Visnu suggested for the repentance of Brahmapa's murder in following words-

## \|\| 3.25 \|\|

*hiriruvāca \|*  
*maheśvara śṛṇuṣvemāṃ mama vācaṃ kalasvanām \|*  
*brahmahatyākṣayakarīṃ śubhadāṃ puṇyavardhanīm \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Hari said - "O Mahesvara! Listen to my suggestion effacing the dire impact of the murder of the Brahmana; it is ear pleasing and enhances the noble deeds."

## \|\| 3.26 \|\|

*yo 'sau prāṅmaṇḍale puṇye madaṃśaprabhavo 'vyayaḥ \|*  
*prayāge vasate nityaṃ yogaśāyīti viśrutaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The holy Prayaga falling in the district of Pranga wherein resides an imperishable Purusa Yogasayi by name and has been bom with my own ray.

## \|\| 3.27 \|\|

*caraṇād dakṣīṇāttsya viniryātā saridvarā \|*  
*viśrutā varaṇetvayeva sarvapāpaharā śubhā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The renowned river Varana has emanated from his right foot and it is holy as also competent to absolve one from all evils.

## \|\| 3.28 \|\|

*savyādanyā dvitīyā ca asirityeva viśrutā \|*  
*te ubhe saricchreṣṭhe lokapūjye babhūvatuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Another renowned river Asi has emanated from his left foot. Both these rivers are considered most holy in this universe.

## \|\| 3.29 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ madhye tu yo deśastatkṣetraṃ yogaśāyinaḥ \|*  
*trailokyapravaraṃ tīrthaṃ sarvapāpapramocanam \|*  
*na tādṛśo 'sti gagane na bhūbhyāṃ na rasātale \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The territory lying between the above-said rivers is the region of that Yogasayi. It is the greatest in the three-worlds and is a holy place that absolves one from all evils. No other holy place analogous to it has existed in ether, earth and the nether world.

## \|\| 3.30 \|\|

*tatrāsti nagarī puṇyā khyātā vārāṇasī śubhā \|*  
*yasyāṃ hi bhogino 'pīśa prayānti bhavato layam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О god! There exists the renowned city of Varanasi. It is so sacred that the people indulging in worldly affairs too attain the position as you yourself bear.

## \|\| 3.31 \|\|

*vilāsinīnāṃ raśanāsvanena śrutisvanairbrahmaṇapuṅgavānām \|*  
*śucisvaratvaṃ guravo niśamya hāsyādaśāsanta muhurmuhustān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The echo of Vedas recited by the great Brahmins is mixed with the voice of luxury enjoying people and thus the resultant blending beholds all benevolent voices altogether. The preceptors administer with humour the voice so heard by them.

## \|\| 3.32 \|\|

*vrajatsu yoṣitsu catuṣpatheṣu padānyalaktāruṇitāni dṛṣṭvā \|*  
*yayau śaśī vismayameva yasyāṃ kiṃsvit prayātā sthālapadminīyam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The moon is contused at the movement of terrestrial lily when it looks at the red smeared feet of the women who stroll in the round abouts.

## \|\| 3.33 \|\|

*tuṅgani yasyāṃ suramandirāṇi rundhanti candraṃ rajanīsukheṣu \|*  
*divāpi sūryaṃ pavanāplutābhirdīrghābhirevaṃ supatākikābhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The temples are built of so great a height that the moon finds hurdle for its movement at night and the flags on their tombs are so large as their unfurling through the wind strokes which makes the beams of sunlight in the day vanish.

## \|\| 3.34 \|\|

*bhṛṅgāśca yasyāṃ śaśikāntabhittau pralobhyamānāḥ pratibimbiteṣu \|*  
*āleśyayoṣidvimalānanābjeṣvīyurbhramānnaiva ca puṣpakāntaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The paintings on women in Varanasi when they spread their reflection of face on the walls studded with Candrakantamani fascinate the bees to the extent that they forget to go to the flowers.

## \|\| 3.35 \|\|

*pariśramaścāpi parājiteṣu nareṣu saṃmohanakhelanena \|*  
*yasyāṃ jasakrīḍanasaṃgatāsu na strīṣu saṃbho gṛhadīrghokāsu \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. And, О Sambhu! Only in Varanasi and not in any another place, the people indulging in the enchanting activities and the women gathered for swimming (Jalakrida) in the ponds made in every home fight mutual competition.

## \|\| 3.36 \|\|

*na caiva kaścit paramandirāṇi ruṇaddhi śaṃbho sahasā ṛte 'kṣan \|*  
*na cābalānāṃ tarasā parākramaṃ karoti yasyāṃ surataṃ hi maktvā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Besides Pasa (dice used for gambling) where the houses of others are free to act voluntarily and where no person does any forcible valour with the women except at the appropriate time for courtship (such is Varanasi).

## \|\| 3.37 \|\|

*pāśagranthirgajendrāṇāṃ dānacchedo madacyutau \|*  
*yasyāṃ mānamadau puṃsāṃ kariṇāṃ yauvanāgame \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There takes place Pasagranthi in controlling the elephants, Danaccheda in their discharge of intoxication and Mana and Mada at the time of youth commenced in male elephants.

## \|\| 3.38 \|\|

*priyadoṣāḥ sadā yasyāṃ kauśikā netare janāḥ \|*  
*tārāgaṇe 'kulīnatvaṃ gadye vṛttacyutirvibho \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О god! Only owls are found favouring the night (evils/deficiencies) nobody else does so. The people there are noble and if evils (not to set in earth) are found there, only these exist with the galaxy. Nowhere is misconduct found there except in prose (breach of rhyme).

## \|\| 3.39 \|\|

*bhṛtacilubdhā vilāsinyo bhujaṅgaparivāritāḥ \|*  
*candrabhūṣitadehāśca yasyāṃ tvamiva śaṅkara \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О Sankara! The spotive women having attraction of their bhuti are found there surrounded by bhujangas and their bodies are decorated with the ornament Candra like you. (The term Bhuti is for 'ash' and 'wealth', Bhujanga for 'serpent' and 'debauchery' and Candra for 'moon' and an ornament is used herein).

## \|\| 3.40 \|\|

*īdṛśāyāṃ sureśāna vārāṇasyāṃ mahāśrame \|*  
*vasate bhavāṃllolaḥ sarvapāpaharo raviḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O Suresana! in the great hermitage of Varanasi endowed with such salient features, god sun (Ravi) resides. He absolves the creatures from all evils.

## \|\| 3.41 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhaṃ yatproktaṃ madaṃśo yatra keśavaḥ \|*  
*tatra gatvā suraśreṣṭha pāpamokṣamavāpsyasi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О the greatest god! You will be absolved from all evils when you see Kesava my own ray bom at the place known as Dasasvamedha.

## \|\| 3.42 \|\|

*ityevamukto garu.ḍadhvajena vṛṣadhvajastaṃ śirasā praṇamya \|*  
*jagāma vegād garuḍo yathāsau vārāṇasīṃ pāpavimocanāya \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The bull-rider (Vrsadhvaja) at the suggestion so given by the rider of Garuda (Visnu) travelled as fast as an eagle (Garuda) to Varanasi for getting release of the evil after duly saluting him.

## \|\| 3.43 \|\|

*gatvā supuṇyāṃ nagarīṃ sutīrthāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca lolaṃ sadaśaśvamedham \|*  
*snātvā ca tīrtheṣu vimuktapāpaḥ sa keśavaṃ draṣṭumupājagāma \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He first went to Dasasvamedha, saw god hola, bathed in all holy places and thus he absolved himself from the evil in that holiest city. He then walked to see lord Kesava.

## \|\| 3.44 \|\|

*keśavaṃ śaṅkaro dṛṣṭvā praṇipatyedamabravīt \|*  
*tavatprasādād hṛṣīkeśa brahmahatyā kṣayaṃ gatā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He bowed before Kesava and said- "O Hrsikesa! The evil of Brahmana’s murder with your grace has now been absolved.

## \|\| 3.45 \|\|

*nedaṃ kapālaṃ deveśa maddhastaṃ parimuñcati \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ vedmi na ca tadetanme vaktumarhasi \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. (Yet) О Kesava! This head is still stuck to my palm and I am unable to understand the reason behind it. You only can highlight it.

## \|\| 3.46 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca\|*  
*mahādevavacaḥ śrutvā keśavo vākyamabravīt \|*  
*vidyate kāraṇaṃ rudra tatsarvaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Pulastya said- Having heard Mahadeva, Kesava replied- "O Rudra! I tell you the reasons lying behind all this."

## \|\| 3.47 \|\|

*yo 'sau mamāgrato divyo hradaḥ padmotpalairyutaḥ \|*  
*eṣa tīrthavaraḥ puṇyo devagandharvapūjitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The divine pond with lotus flowers blossomed in front of me is sacred and a very holy place. It is worshipped by the gods and the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 3.48 \|\|

*etasminpravare tīrthe knānaṃ śaṃbho samācara \|*  
*snātamātrasya cādyaiva kapālaṃ parimokṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О Sambhu! Take a dip in this holiest pond. This head shall abandon your palm just when you take a dip in this pond.

## \|\| 3.49 \|\|

*tataḥ kapālī loke ca khyāto rudra bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*kapālamocanetyevaṃ tīrthaṃ cedaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. With this event О Rudra! You will gain popularity as Kapali and this place too shall be popularly known as Kapalamocana.

## \|\| 3.50 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evamuktaḥ sureśena keśavena maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kapālamocane sasnau vedostavidhinā mune \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Pulastya said - О sage! Mahesvara took a bath with the procedures mentioned in the Vedas in that pond when it was suggested by Kesava.

## \|\| 3.51 \|\|

*snātasya tīrthe tripurāntakasya paricyutaṃ hastatalāt kapālam \|*  
*nāmnā babhūvātha kapālamocanaṃ tattīrthavaryaṃ bhagavatprasādāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. As soon as dip was taken by lord Sankara (the killer of Tripura demon), the head stuck to his palm got separated and fell down. That holiest place then became famous as Kapalamocana by the grace of god.

## Chapter 4. War between Hari and Virabhadra

## \|\| 4.1-2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ kapālī saṃjāto devarṣe bhagavānharaḥ \|*  
*anena kāraṇenāsau dakṣeṇa na nimantritaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kapālijāyeti satīṃ vijñāyātha prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*yajñe cārhāpi duhitā dakṣeṇa na nimantritā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Pulastya said - О Devarsi! Lord Sankara became Kapali due to the above-said event. This was the reason why, he was ignored by Daksa Prajapati. In spite of Sati being qualified with all respects and her being his own daughter, she too was not invited as she was the wife of Kapali.

## \|\| 4.3 \|\|

*etasminnantare devīṃ draṣṭuṃ gautamanandinī \|*  
*jayā jagāma śailendraṃ mandaraṃ cārukandaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the meantime, Jaya, the daughter of Gautama went to the mountain Mandara which had the five cave in order to see the goddess Sati.

## \|\| 4.4 \|\|

*tāmāgatāṃ satī dṛṣṭvā jayamekāmuvāca ha \|*  
*kimarthaṃ vijayā nāgājjayantī cāparājitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Sati saw only Jaya; therefore she enquired of her as to why Vijaya, Jayanti and Aparajita did not come with her.

## \|\| 4.5-6 \|\|

*sā devyā vacanaṃ śrutvā uvāca parameśvarīm \|*  
*gatā nimantritāḥ sarvā makhe mātāmahasya tāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*samaṃ pitrā gautamena mātrā caivāpyahalyayā \|*  
*ahaṃ samāgatā draṣṭuṃ tvāṃ tatra gamanotsukā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. She replied- "They all were invited by the maternal grand-father (Daksa) in a yajna arranged there. Hence, they have gone there with father Gautama and mother Ahalya. I have come to see curiously your zeal to visit there.

## \|\| 4.7 \|\|

*kiṃ tvaṃ na vrajase tatra tathā devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*nāmantritāsi tātena utāhosvid vrajiṣyasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Aren't you and Mahesvara going there? Has your father not invited you? Or shall you go there?

## \|\| 4.8 \|\|

*gatāstu ṛṣayaḥ sarve ṛṣipatnyaḥ surāstathā \|*  
*mātṛṣvasaḥ śaśāṅkaśca sapatnīko gataḥ kratum \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All hermits, their wives and gods have gone there too, О maternal aunt (Mausi)! Sasanka too has gone there with his wife.

## \|\| 4.9 \|\|

*caturdaśasu lokeṣu jantavo ye carācarāḥ \|*  
*nimantritāḥ kratau sarve kiṃ nāsi tvaṃ nimantritā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. All movable and inert organisms from the fourteen lokas have been invited to function there. Are you alone uninvited?

## \|\| 4.10 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca\|*  
*jayāyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā vajrapātasamaṃ satī \|*  
*manyunābhiplutā brahman pañcatvamagamat tataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Pulastya said - О Brahmins! These words from Jaya appeared like a thunderbolt to Sati and she became angry to the extent that the common people are jeered and that stroke was so hard that she fell down dead.

## \|\| 4.11 \|\|

*jayā mṛtāṃ satīṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhaśokapariplutā \|*  
*muñcatī vāri netrābhyāṃ sasvaraṃ vilalāpa ha \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Having seen that Sati met with casual death, Jaya burst into tears and began wailing.

## \|\| 4.12 \|\|

*ākranditadhvaniṃ śrutvā śūlapāṇistrilocanaḥ \|*  
*āḥ kimetaditītyuktvā jayābhyāśamupāgataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. As the sound from the wailing was piercing, it awakened lord Sankara from his meditation. He came to Jay a and asked - "What is it?"

## \|\| 4.13 \|\|

*āgato dadṛśe devīṃ latāmiva vanaspateḥ \|*  
*kṛttāṃ paraśunā bhūmau ślathāṅgīṃ patitāṃ satīm \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Lord Sankara saw there Sati lying on the ground like a creeper cut off with a sharp blow by an axe. Her body was as pale as a dead one.

## \|\| 4.14 \|\|

*devīṃ nipatitāṃ dṛṣṭvā jayāṃ papraccha śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*kimiyaṃ patitā bhūmau nikṛtteva latā satī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Sankara having seen this asked Jaya - "Why has Sati fallen on ground like a cut-off creeper?

## \|\| 4.15-16 \|\|

*sā śaṅkaravacaḥ śrutvā jayā vacanamabravīt \|*  
*śratvā makhasthā dakṣasya bhaginyaḥ patibhiḥ saha \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ādityādyāstrilokeśa samaṃ śakrādibhiḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*mātṛṣvasā vipanneyamantarduḥkhena dahyatī \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Jaya replied- "O the ruler of three-worlds! My maternal aunt (Sati) has fallen down dead owing to sheer pain she felt when she heard that all her sisters with their husbands, Indra etc., gods and Adityas etc. have been invited in the yajna and gone there."

## \|\| 4.17 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā vaco raudraṃ rudraḥ krodhāpluto babhau \|*  
*kruddhasya sarvagātrebhyo niśceruḥ sahasārciṣaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Pulastya said - Lord Rudra became excessively angry on hearing this fierce statement from Jaya. Flames started coming out of the body of Sankara so annoyed.

## \|\| 4.18-19 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhāt trinetrasya gātraromodbhāva mune \|*  
*gaṇāḥ siṃhamukhā jātā vīrabhadrapurogamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gaṇaiḥ parivṛtastasmānmandarāddhimasāhvayam \|*  
*gataḥ kanakhalaṃ tasmād yatra dakṣo 'yajat kratum \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. О sages! The ganas having a mouth similar to that of a lion appeared from the furs of Sankara's body due to excessive fury. Virabhadra was the principal gana among them. He then went to the Himalaya from Mandara mountain in the company of all his ganai and Kanakhala from there where the yajna was commenced by Daksa.

## \|\| 4.20 \|\|

*tato gaṇānāmadhipo vīrabhadro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*diśi pratīcyuttarāyāṃ tasthau śūladharo mune \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О sage! The mightiest Vorabhadra, the foremost among the Ganas, then held a trident and stood at the west north.

## \|\| 4.21 \|\|

*jayā krodhād gadāṃ gṛhya pūrvadakṣiṇataḥ sthitā \|*  
*madhye triraśūladhṛk śarvastasthau krodhānmahāmune \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O great sages! Jaya in the state of excessive fury stood at the eastern-south with a macc in her hand and Sankara with a trident in his hand stood amid them.

## \|\| 4.22 \|\|

*maḍagārivadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo yakṣagandharvāḥ kimidaṃ tvityacintayan \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Indra etc. gods, hermits, demi-gods (Yaksa) and Gandharvas were caught in surprise when they saw Virabhadra in disguise of a lion.

## \|\| 4.23 \|\|

*tatastu dhanurādāya śarāṃścāśīviṣopamān \|*  
*dvārapālastadā dharmo vīrabhadramupādravat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The gate-man Dharma then rushed towards Virabhadra with bows and arrows serpent like.

## \|\| 4.24-25 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ sahasā dharmaṃ dṛṣṭvā gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*kareṇaikena jagrāha triśulaṃ vahnisannibham \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kārmukaṃ ca dvitīyena tṛtīyenātha mārgaṇān \|*  
*caturthena gadāṃ gṛhya dharmamabhyadravad gaṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The principal gana (Virabhadra) held a trident analogous to fire in one hand, a bow in another hand, an arrow in the third hand and a mace in the fourth hand and rushed to Dharma when he saw his sudden march.

## \|\| 4.26-27 \|\|

*tataścaturbhujaṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmarājo gaṇeśvaram \|*  
*tasthāvaṣṭabhunajo bhūtvā nānāyudhadharo 'vyayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*khaḍgacarmagadāprāsaparaśvadhavarāṅkuśaiḥ \|*  
*cāpamārgaṇabhṛttasthau hantukāmo gaṇeśvaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Imperishable Dharmaraja confronted four armed Virabhadra with enhancing his eight arms equipped with varied weapons. He stood boldly with the intention to finish Virabhadra and held a sword, carma (shield), mace, spear, axe, goad, bow and arrow in his hands.

## \|\| 4.28 \|\|

*gaṇeśvaro 'pi saṃkruddho hantuṃ dharma sanātanam \|*  
*vavarṣa mārgaṇāstīkṣṇān yathā prāvṛṣi toyadaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Virabhadra too started showering acute arrows on Sanatana Dharma like the clouds during the rainy season so that he could be killed.

## \|\| 4.29 \|\|

*tāvanyonyaṃ mahātmānau śaracāpadharau mune \|*  
*rudhirāruṇasiktāṅgau kiṃśukāviva rejatuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О sages! Both of them with arrows and bows soaked in blood and looked as red as the flower of canker bloom (kimsuka).

## \|\| 4.30 \|\|

*tato varāstrairgaṇanāyakena jitaḥ sa dharmaḥ tarasā prasahya \|*  
*parāṅmukho 'bhūdvimanā munīndra sa vīrabhadraḥ praviveśa yajñam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О king of sages! Dharmaraja had to move back as he was conquered by Virabhadra and thus, Virabhadra got way to enter into yajna.

## \|\| 4.31 \|\|

*yajñāvāṭaṃ praviṣṭaṃ taṃ vīrabhadraṃ gaṇeśvaram \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tu sahasā devā uttasthuḥ sāyudhā mune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. О sage! The gods suddenly stood up with weapons in their hands when they saw that Virabhadra has entered into the pavilion for offering.

## \|\| 4.32-35 \|\|

*vasavo 'ṣṭau mahābhāgā grahā nava sudāruṇāḥ \|*  
*indrādyā dvādaśādityā rudrāstvekādaśaiva hi \|\| 32 \|\|*

*viśvedevāśca sādhyāśca siddhagandharvapannagāḥ \|*  
*yakṣāḥ kiṃpuruṣāścaiva khagāśkradharāstathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*rājā vaivastādvaṃśād dharmakīrtistu viśrutaḥ \|*  
*somavaṃśodbhavaścogro bhojakīrtirmahābhujaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dītijā dānavāścānye ye 'nye tatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*te sarve 'bhyadravan raudraṃ vīrabhadramudāyudhāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. Eight Vasus, predominant nine stars, Indra etc., twelve Aditya, eleven Rudra, Visvedeva, Sadhya-ganas, Siddha, Gandharva, Pannaga, Yaksa, eunuch (Kinnaras), Ghosts (Bhuta), Birds, Cakradhara, renowned king Dharmakirti of Vaivasvata dynasty, Bhojakirti, the chivalrous king of lunar dynasty, demon, devil and all people present there picked up weapons and rushed to kill the dreadful Virabhadra.

## \|\| 4.36 \|\|

*tānāpatata evāśu cāpabāṇadharo gaṇaḥ \|*  
*abhidudrāva vegena sarvāneva śarotkaraiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The gana Virabhadra with bow and arrows attacked them and sppedily drove them by throwing arrowheads.

## \|\| 4.37 \|\|

*te śastravarṣamatulaṃ gaṇeśāya samutsṛjan \|*  
*gaṇeśo 'pi varāstraistān praciccheda bibheda ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. They all shot arrows in showers at Virabhadra. Virabhadra scattered all arrows by the expert use of his weapons.

## \|\| 4.38 \|\|

*śaraiḥ śastraiśca satataṃ vadhyamānā mahātmanā \|*  
*vīrabhadreṇa devādyā avahāramarkuta \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The gods etc., ceased fighting as they all were badly injured by the arrows and weapons blown by the unique warrior Virabhadra.

## \|\| 4.39 \|\|

*tato viveśa gaṇapo yajñamadhyaṃ suvistṛtam \|*  
*juhvānā ṛṣayo yatra havīṃṣi pravitanvate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Virabhadra then entered just at the centre of that gigantic premise of yajna. The hermits engaged in offering were giving oblations to the fire there.

## \|\| 4.40 \|\|

*tato maharṣayo dṛṣṭvā mṛgendravadanaṃ gaṇam \|*  
*bhītā hotraṃ parityajya jagmuḥ śaraṇamacyutam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The hermits ceased their perfonnance immediately when they saw. the lion-mouthed gana and sheltered Acyuta.

## \|\| 4.41 \|\|

*tānārtāścakrabhṛd dṛṣṭvā maharṣīstrastamānasān \|*  
*na bhetavyamitītyuktvā samuttasthau varāyudhaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Acyuta stood up with a discus in his hands and with words "don't be afraid" in the lips when he saw those hermits badly frightened and wailing.

## \|\| 4.42 \|\|

*samānamya tataḥ śārṅga śarānagniśikhopamān \|*  
*mumoca vīrabhadrāya kāyāvaraṇadāraṇān \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He then started shooting arrows like the flames powerful enough to penetrate the external cover of body on Virabhadra by giving a slight bend to his Sarnga bow.

## \|\| 4.43 \|\|

*te tasya kāyamāsādya amoghā vai hareḥ śarāḥ \|*  
*nipeturbhuvi bhagnāśā nāstikādiva yācakāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. As the beggar returns with a despair in mind from the atheist, the target hitting arrows shot by Sri Hari fell down on the ground after touching merely the body of Virabhadra.

## \|\| 4.44 \|\|

*śarāstvamoghānmoghatvamāpannānvīkṣya keśavaḥ \|*  
*divyairastrairvīrabhadraṃ pracchādayitumudyataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Kesava intended immediately for covering Virabhadra by divine weapons when he saw the futility of arrows in their mission.

## \|\| 4.45 \|\|

*tānastrānvāsudevena prakṣiptāngaṇanāyakaḥ \|*  
*vārayāmāsa śūlena gadayā mārgaṇaistathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Those arrows from Vasudeva too were destroyed by confronting with sula, mace and arrows.

## \|\| 4.46 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā vipannānyastrāṇi gadāṃ cikṣepa mādhavaḥ \|*  
*triśulena samāhatya pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Madhava threw his mace when he saw his weapons destroyed by Virabhadra. However, Virabhadra threw it on the earth with a blow of his trident.

## \|\| 4.47-49 \|\|

*tam gadāṃ viphalām dṛṣṭā lāṅgalaṃ prākaṣiṣaddhariḥ \|*  
*mangalam ca gaṇeśo'pi gadayā pratyavārayat \|\| 47 \|\|*

*muśalaṃ vīrabhadrāya pracikṣepa halāyudhaḥ \|*  
*lāṅgalaṃ ca gaṇeśo 'pi gadayā pratyavārayat \|\| 48 \|\|*

*muśalaṃ sagadaṃ dṛṣṭvā lāṅgalaṃ ca nivāritam \|*  
*vīrabhadrāya cikṣepa cakraṃ krodhāt khagadhvajaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. Musala and Langala were thrown on the part of Halayudha but these weapons too were thrown down by Virabhadra through his mace. Garudadhvaja severely in furiated and attacked with a discus Virabhadra when he saw the failure of attack by mace including Musala and plough.

## \|\| 4.50 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ śatasūryakalpaṃ sudarśanaṃ vīkṣya gaṇeśvarastu \|*  
*śūlaṃ parityajya jagāra cakraṃ yathā madhuṃ mīnavapuḥ surendraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Virabhadra (Ganesvara) had however, gobbled up that discus luminating with the light of several hundred suns by leaving his sula aside. It was done in the same way as lord Surendra had gobbled up the Madhu while disguised as a fish.

## \|\| 4.51 \|\|

*cakre nigīrṇe gaṇanāyakena krodhātirakto 'sitacārunetraḥ \|*  
*murārirabhyetya gaṇādhipendramutkṣipya vegād bhuvi niṣpipapeṣa \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When the discus was gobbled up by Gananayaka (Virabhadra) the dark and beautiful eyes of Murari turned red with anger. He went to Virabhadra, lifted him up at once, knocked him down on ground and started thrashing him.

## \|\| 4.52 \|\|

*haribāhūruvegena viniṣpiṣṭasya bhūtale \|*  
*sahitaṃ rudhirodgārairmukāccakraṃ vinigatam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Owing to the hard blows of arms and legs of Hari, the discus came out from the mouth of Virabhadra with blood when he was knocked down with a thud.

## \|\| 4.53 \|\|

*tato niḥsṛtamālokya cakraṃ kaiṭabhanāśanaḥ \|*  
*samādāya hṛṣīkeśo vīrabhadro mumoca ha \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Destroyer of demon Kaitabha, Hrsikesa then picked up the discus and left Virabhadra there.

## \|\| 4.54 \|\|

*hṛṣīkeśena muktastu vīrabhadro jaṭādharam \|*  
*gatvā nivedayāmāsa vāsudevātparājayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Virabhadra when liberated by Hrsikesa went to Lord Sankara and reported his defeat through Vasudeva.

## \|\| 4.55 \|\|

*tato jaṭādharo dṛṣṭvā gaṇeśaṃ śoṇitāplutam \|*  
*niśvasantaṃ yathā nāgaṃ krodhaṃ cakre tadāvyayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. When imperishable Jatadhara Sankara saw Virabhadra soaked with blood and breathing like a serpent, he became angry.

## \|\| 4.56 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhābhibhūtena vīrabhadro 'tha śaṃbhunā \|*  
*pūrvoddiṣṭe tadā sthāne sāyudhastu niveśitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In furiated Lord Sankara then restored Virabhadra to the place first determined with his weapons.

## \|\| 4.57 \|\|

*vīrabhadramathādiśya bhadrakālīṃ ca śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*viveśa krodhatāmrākṣo yajñavāṭaṃ triśūlabhṛt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Sankara, the trident holder, then passed necessary orders to Virabhadra and Bhadrakali and entered into the pavilion made for offering. His eyes were turned red with anger.

## \|\| 4.58 \|\|

*tatastu devapravare jaṭādhare triśūlapāṇau tripurāntakāriṇi \|*  
*dakṣasya yajñaṃ viśati kṣayaṅkare jāto ṛṣīṇāṃ pravaro hi sādhvasaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. When Mahadeva, the killer of Tripura demon, trident holder, destroyer entered into the yajna hosted by Daksa, all hermits were severely frightened.

## Chapter 5. Description of Kala-form of Siva

## \|\| 5.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*jaṭādharaṃ harirddaṣṭvā krodhādāraktalocanam \|*  
*tasmāt sthānādapākramya kubjāmre 'ntarhitaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari concealed him in Kubjamra and seated him there and left his place at once when he saw Jatadhara  whose eyes were reddened with anger.

## \|\| 5.2 \|\|

*vasavo 'ṣṭau haraṃ dṛṣṭvā susruvurvegato mune \|*  
*sā tu jātā saricchreṣṭhā sītā nāma sarasvatī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О sage! Eight vasus were melted on account of the temperature so created by the presence of Hara. It originated the great river Sita.

## \|\| 5.3 \|\|

*ekādaśa tathā rudrāstrinetrā vṛṣaketanāḥ \|*  
*kāndiśīkā layaṃ jagmuḥ samabhyetyaiva śaṅkaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. And Vrsaketana, three-eyed eleven rudras were frightened, rushed to lord Sankara and merged with him.

## \|\| 5.4 \|\|

*viśve 'śvinau caca sādhyāśca maruto 'nalabhāskarāḥ \|*  
*samāsādya puroḍāśaṃ bhakṣyāśca mahāmune \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О great sage! Visvas, Asvinikumaras, Sadhyas, wind, fire and sun picked up purodasa (oblation of offering) and ran away eating the same.

## \|\| 5.5 \|\|

*candraḥ samamṛkṣagaṇairniśāṃ samupadarśayan \|*  
*utpatyaruhya gaganaṃ svamadhiṣṭhānamāsthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The moon with the galaxy abandoned the night alone, ascended and stopped at their respective places. They withheld their movements.

## \|\| 5.6 \|\|

*kaśyapādyāśca ṛṣayo japantaḥ śatarudriyam \|*  
*puṣpāñjalipuṭā bhūtvā praṇatāḥ saṃsthitā mune \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sage! Kasyapa etc., hermits started chanting Satarudriya, took flowers in their palms and stood up humbly.

## \|\| 5.7 \|\|

*asakṛd dakṣadayitā dṛṣṭvā rudraṃ balādhikam \|*  
*śakrādīnāṃ sureśānāṃ kṛpaṇaṃ vilalāpa ha \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Having seen Rudra mightiest among Indra etc., gods, the wife of Daksa began wailing frequently in a pathetic condition.

## \|\| 5.8 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhābhibhūtena śaṅkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*talaprahārairamarā bahavo vinipātitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In furiated lord Sankara killed numerous gods merely by slapping them with his palm.

## \|\| 5.9 \|\|

*pādaprahārairamarā triśulenāpare mune \|*  
*dṛṣṭyagninā tathaivānye devādyāḥ pralayīkṛtāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О sage! Some of them were killed by kicks, some other by blowing trident while a few among them were killed by the fire emanating eye of lord Sankara.

## \|\| 5.10 \|\|

*tataḥ pūṣā haraṃ vīkṣya vinighnantaṃ surāsurān \|*  
*krodhād bāhū prasāryatha pradudrāva maheśvaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Pusa-sun rushed with both his arms extended towards Mahesvara when he saw lord Sankara killing the gods and demons severely.

## \|\| 5.11 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ bhagavān saṃnirīkṣya trilocanaḥ \|*  
*bāhubhyāṃ pratijagrāha kareṇaikena śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Lord Sankara caught both his arms by using his single hand when he saw him advancing.

## \|\| 5.12 \|\|

*karābhyāṃ pragṛhītasya śaṃbhunāṃśumato 'pi hi \|*  
*karāṅgulibhyo niścerurasṛgdhārāḥ samantataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Sambhu gave a blow so hard that the fingers of both arms with sun started flowing blood stream from all the four directions.

## \|\| 5.13 \|\|

*tato vegena mahatā aṃśumantaṃ divākaram \|*  
*bhrāmayāmāsa satataṃ siṃho mṛgaśiśuṃ yathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He then started rotating round the sun so rapidly as the lion rotates the young stag through his jaws.

## \|\| 5.14 \|\|

*bhrāmitasyātivegena nāradāṃśumato 'pi hi \|*  
*bhujau hasvatvamāpannau truṭitasnāyubandhanau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Narada! The muscular joints of both arms were split and they fell short.

## \|\| 5.15 \|\|

*rudhirāplutasarvāṅgamaṃśumantaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*saṃnirībhyotsasarjainamanyato\|bhijagāma ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When Mahesvara saw the sun soaked in blood from all joints of his body, he left him and went somewhere else.

## \|\| 5.16 \|\|

*tatastu pūṣā vihasan daśanāni vidarśayan \|*  
*provācaihyehi kāpālin punaḥ punaratheśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Pusa then began to laugh and exhibiting his teeth he frequently challenged with the words - "O Kapali! Come! Come to me for a duel."

## \|\| 5.17 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhābhibhūtena pūṣṇe vegena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*muṣṭināhatya daśanāḥ pātitā dharaṇītale \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Sambhu gave a boxing on his jaw so hard that Pusas teeth fell down on the earth.

## \|\| 5.18 \|\|

*bhagnadantastathā pūṣā śoṇitābhiplutānanaḥ \|*  
*papāta bhuvi niḥsaṃjño vajrāhata ivācalaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus, Pusa fell down on the ground unconscious like a mountain hit hard by the thunderbolt. His teeth were all scattered and blood was oozing from mouth.

## \|\| 5.19 \|\|

*bhago\|bhivībhya pūṣāṇaṃ patitaṃ rudhirokṣitam \|*  
*netrābhyāṃ ghorarūpābhyāṃ vṛṣadhvajamavaikṣata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When Bhaga saw Pusa soaked in blood and fallen on the ground, he stared Vrsabhadhvaja with fierce eyes.

## \|\| 5.20 \|\|

*tripuraghnastataḥ kruddhastalenāhatya cakṣuṣī \|*  
*nipātayāmāsa bhuvi kṣobhayansarvadevatāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In furiated Sankara (killer of Tripura demon) then slapped at the face of Bhaga fiercely resulting which both his eyes fell down on the ground.

## \|\| 5.21 \|\|

*tato divākarāḥ sarve puraskṛtya śatakratum \|*  
*marudbhiśca hutāśaiśca bhayājjagmurdiśo daśa \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Adityas in the company of Marudganas and fires then ran away to the ten directions under the lead of Indra. \*

## \|\| 5.22 \|\|

*pratiyāteṣu deveṣu prahlādādyā ditīsvarāḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya tataḥ sarve tasthuḥ prāñjalayo mune \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О sage! On the departure of the gods, Prahlada etc. demons bowed at the feet of Mahesvara and stood before him with folded hands.

## \|\| 5.23 \|\|

*tatastaṃ yajñavāṭaṃ tu śaṅkaro ghoracakṣuṣā \|*  
*dadarśa dagdhuṃ kopena sarvāṃścaiva surāmurān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Sankara then started looking with fierce eyes at that pavilion made for offering and all gods including the demons so as to bum them into ashes.

## \|\| 5.24 \|\|

*tato nililyire vīrāḥ praṇemurdudrustathā \|*  
*bhayādanye haraṃ dṛṣṭvā gatā vaivasvatakṣayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Some warriors present there were hidden due to extreme of fear, some began to salute, a few among them ran away and a certain number of them were killed by lord Sankara.

## \|\| 5.25 \|\|

*trayo 'gnayastribhirnerduḥsahaṃ samavaikṣata \|*  
*dṛṣṭamātrāstrinetreṇa bhasmībhūtābhavan kṣaṇāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Lord Mahesvara then saw three fires with his three eyes. The fires so stared at him were extinct within a second.

## \|\| 5.26 \|\|

*agnau praṇaṣṭe yajño 'pi bhūtvā divyavapurmṛgaḥ \|*  
*dudrāva viklavagatirdakṣiṇāsahito 'mbare \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The yajna too turned itself in a stage of divine body when the fires were extinguished and all rushed to the sky above with Daksina. Its race was a race with anxiety.

## \|\| 5.27-28 \|\|

*tamevānusasāreśaścāpamānamya vegavān \|*  
*śaraṃ pāśupataṃ kṛtvā kālarūpī maheśvaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*arddhena yajñavāṭānte jaṭādhara iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*arddhena gagane śarvaḥ kālarūpī ca kathyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Mahesvara in the form of Kala (the death god) put immediately Pasupata arrow on the bow, gave tension to the string and chased yajna very fast. Lord Sankara with his halfpart (Ardhahsa) was popularly known as Ja( adhara (Siva) in the premises of the yajna and by his other half-part in the sky is called Kalarupa.

## \|\| 5.29 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kālarūpī tvayākhyātaḥ śaṃbhurgaganagocaraḥ \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ ca svarūpaṃ ca sarvaṃ vyākhyātumarhasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Narada said - "You have addressed Satikara as Kalarupa while moving in the sky. Explain please, his complete feature and characteristics.

## \|\| 5.30 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*svarūpaṃ tripuraghnasya vadiṣye kālapūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*yenāmbaraṃ muniśreṣṭha vyāptaṃ lokahitepsunā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Pulastya said - "O great sage! I tell you of the features completely of that Kalarupa and murderer of Tripura demon, Sankara who moved in the sky for all benevolence.

## \|\| 5.31 \|\|

*yatrāśvinī ca bharaṇī kuttikāyāstathāṃśakaḥ \|*  
*meṣo rāśiḥ kujakṣetraṃ tacchiraḥ kālarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Asvini and Bharani constellation with complete feature but a foot (pada) of Krttika in zodiac Aries at the region of Mars is the head of that Kalarupa Mahadeva.

## \|\| 5.32 \|\|

*āgneyāśāstrayo brahman prājāpatyaṃ kavergṛham \|*  
*saumyārddha vṛṣanāmedaṃ vadanaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The territory of Venus comprising three rays of Kfttika constellation, complete Rohini and two initial feet of Mrgasira constellation i.e. the zodiac Taurus in his mouth.

## \|\| 5.33 \|\|

*mṛgārddhamārdrādityāṃśāstrayaḥ saumyagṛhaṃ tvidam \|*  
*mithunaṃ bhujayostadasya gaganasthasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The territory of mercury comprising the rest of two foot to Mrgasira, complete Ardra constellation and three feet of Punarvasu i.e. the zodiac Gemini is the two arms of the Soli residing in the sky.

## \|\| 5.34 \|\|

*ādityāṃśaśca puṣyaṃ ca āśleṣā śaśino gṛham \|*  
*rāśiḥ karkaṭako nāma pārśve makhavināśinaḥ\|tha \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The territory of moon consisting of one foot of Punarvasu, complete Pusya and Aslesa constellation i.e. the zodiac Cancer is the two collateral parts of god Sankara who ruined the yajna.

## \|\| 5.35 \|\|

*pitryarkṣaṃ bhagadaivatyamuttarāṃś ca kesarī \|*  
*sūryakṣetraṃ vibhorbrahman hṛdayaṃ parigīyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. О Brahmin! The territory of sun consisting of complete Magha, complete Рurа Phalguni and one foot of uttara Phalguni i.e. the zodiac Leo is called the heart of Lord Sankara.

## \|\| 5.36 \|\|

*uttarāṃśāstrayaḥ pāṇiścitrārdhaṃ kanyakā tviyam \|*  
*somaputrasya sadmaitad dvitīyaṃ jaṭharaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The second territory of Mercury consisting of three feet of uttara Phalguni, complete Hasta constellation and two feet of Citra constellation i.e. the zodiac Virgo is the belly (stomach) of lord Sankara.

## \|\| 5.37 \|\|

*citrāṃśadvitayaṃ svātirviśākhāyāṃśakatrayam \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ sukrasadanaṃ tulā nābhirudāhṛtā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The second territory of Venus consisting of the remaining two feet of Citra, complete Svati and three feet of Visakha i.e. the zodiac Libra is called the navel of lord Mahadeva.

## \|\| 5.38 \|\|

*viśākhāṃśamanūrādhā jyeṣṭhā bhaumagṛhaṃ tvidam \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ vṛściko rāśirmeḍhraṃ kālasavarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The second territory of Mars consisting of Visakha one foot, Anuradha and Jyestha complete i.e. the zodiac Scorpion is the penis (linga) of that Kalarupa Mahadeva.

## \|\| 5.39 \|\|

*mūlaṃ pūrvottarāṃśaśca devācajāryagṛhaṃ dhanuḥ \|*  
*ūruyugalamīśasya amararṣe pragīyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The territory of Jupiter consisting of the complete Mula constellation and complete Purvasadha including one foot of uttarasadha i.e. the zodiac Sagittarius is the couple thigh of that Mahesvara.

## \|\| 5.40 \|\|

*uttarāṃśāstrayo ṛkṣaṃ śravaṇaṃ makaro mune \|*  
*dhaniṣṭhārdhaṃ śatabhiṣā jānunī parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O hermit! The territory of Saturn consisting of the remaining three feet of uttarasadha, the complete constellation Sravana and two initial feet of Dhanistha i.e. Capricorn is the two pubics of that Paramesvara Mahesvara.

## \|\| 5.41 \|\|

*dhaniṣṭhārdhaṃ śatabhiṣā prauṣṭhapadyāṃśakatrayam \|*  
*saureḥ sadmāparamidaṃ kumbho jaṅghe ca viśrate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The second territory of Saturn consisting of fust half of Dhanistha, complete Satabhisa an the three feet of Purvabhadrapada i.e. the zodiac Aquarius are the two legs of that lord.

## \|\| 5.42 \|\|

*proṣṭhapadyāṃśamekaṃ tu uttarā revatī tathā \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ jīvasadanaṃ mīnastu caraṇāvubhau \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The second territory of Jupiter consisting of one foot of Purvabhadrapada, complete uttarabhadrapada and Revati i.e. the zodiac Pisces are his two feet.

## \|\| 5.43 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā kālarūpaṃ trinetro yajñaṃ krodhānmārgarājaghāna \|*  
*viddhaścāsau vedanābuddhimuktaḥ khe saṃtasthau tārakābhiścitāṅgaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The three-eyed lord hit hard the yajna in the vagary of anger as Kala himself. Conceiving no pain feeling, the arrow shot yajna covered its body with the galaxy of yajna and settled in the sky.

## \|\| 5.44 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*rāśayo gaditā brahmaṃstvayā dvādaśa vai mama \|*  
*teṣāṃ viśeṣato brūhi lakṣaṇāni svarūpataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Narada said - "O Brahmin! You have thus, imparted knowledge on the twelve zodiacs. Kindly, now continue with explaining their characteristics according to their features (physique).

## \|\| 5.45 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*svarūpaṃ tava vakṣyāmi rāśīnāṃ śṛṇu nārada \|*  
*yādṛśā yatra saṃcārā yasmin sthāne vasanti ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Pulastya said- О Narada! I explain now the features of the zodiacs. Please, listen attentively. I tell you all about their appearance, the orbits in which they move and where they reside.

## \|\| 5.46 \|\|

*meṣaḥ samānamūrtiśca ajāvikadhanādiṣu \|*  
*saṃcārasthānamevāsya dhānyaratnākarādiṣu \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The zodiac Aries has the feature of sheep. It circulates its presence in sheep, goat, wealth, cereals and gems etc.

## \|\| 5.47 \|\|

*navaśādūlasaṃchannavasudhāyāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ carati phulleṣu sarasāṃ pulineṣu ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. It moves daily on the banks of reservoirs covered by vegetation blossomed and throughout the earth covered with new grown Durva (long lift plant).

## \|\| 5.48 \|\|

*vṛṣaḥ sadṛśarūpo hi carate gokulādiṣu \|*  
*tasyādhivāsabhūmittu kuṣīvaladharāśrayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The zodiac Taurus has the features of a bull and it appears in the commune of cows. It resides on the lands pertaining to the farmers.

## \|\| 5.49 \|\|

*strīpuṃsayoḥ samaṃ rūpaṃ śayyāsanaparigrahaḥ \|*  
*vīṇāvādyadhṛṅ mithunaṃ gītanartakaśilpiṣu \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The zodiac Gemini has feature of a couple (man and woman in joined form). It resides at the cot and the seat. It holds a lyre and musical instruments in its hands. It circulates its rays on singers, dancers and craftsman.

## \|\| 5.50 \|\|

*sthitaḥ krīḍāratirnityaṃ vihārāvanirasya tu \|*  
*mithunaṃ nāma vikhyātaṃ rāśirdvedhātmakaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This dual form (couplet) zodiac is called Gemini. This zodiac prefers games (luxuries) and resides at picnic spots (vihara bhumis).

## \|\| 5.51 \|\|

*karkiḥ kulīreṇa samaḥ salilasthaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*kedāravāpīpuline viviktāvanireva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The zodiac cancer is crab-like in feature and lives in the water. It moves to the fields full of water, the river banks and solitary places.

## \|\| 5.52 \|\|

*sihastu parvatāraṇyadurgakandarabhūmiṣu \|*  
*vasate vyādhapallīṣu gahvareṣu guhāsu ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The zodiac Leo resides in mountains, forests, inaccessible places, caves, himting places, trenches and the valleys.

## \|\| 5.53 \|\|

*vrīhipradīpikakarā manāvārūḍhā ca kanyakā \|*  
*carate strīratisthāne vasate naḍvaleṣu ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The zodiac Virgo is with a lamp and Vrihi in its hand and seated on a boat in appearance. It resides in the genitals and nipples of the woman.

## \|\| 5.54 \|\|

*tulāpāṇiśca puruṣo vīthyāpaṇavicārakaḥ \|*  
*nagarādhvānaśālāsu vasate tatra nārada \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. О Narada! The zodiac Libra strolls in the streets and markets, appears in masculine feature with a balance in its hands. It resides in cities, highways and buildings.

## \|\| 5.55 \|\|

*śvabhravalmīkasaṃcārī vṛściko vṛścikākṛtiḥ \|*  
*viṣagomayakīṭādipāṣāṇādiṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The appearance of the zodiac Scorpion is Scorpion-like. It walks through the pits and termites. It resides in poison, cowdung, insects and stones.

## \|\| 5.56 \|\|

*dhanustu raṅgajaghano dīpyamāno dhanurdharaḥ \|*  
*vājiśūrāstravidvīraḥ sthāyī gajarathādiṣu \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The appearance of the zodiac Sagittarius is horse-like in pubic region. It is glowing and is an archer. It is known to horse riding, war- craft, chivalrous and expert in operation with weapons. It resides in elephants and chariots etc.

## \|\| 5.57 \|\|

*mṛgāsyo makaro brahman vṛṣaskandhekṣaṇāṅgajaḥ \|*  
*makaro 'sau nadīcārī vasate ca mahodadhau \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О Brahmin! Appearance of the zodiac Capricorn has a deer like mouth, bull like shoulders and elephant-like eyes. This zodiac swims in rivers and resides in the ocean.

## \|\| 5.58 \|\|

*riktamumbhaśca puruṣaḥ skandhadhārī jalāplutaḥ \|*  
*dyūtaśālācaraḥ kumbhaḥ sthāyī śauṇḍikasadmasu \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The zodiac Aquarius appears as a person soaked in water with a pitcher on its shoulder. It moves through casino and resides in bar (liquor sipping place).

## \|\| 5.59 \|\|

*mīnadvayamathāsaktaṃ mīnastīrthābdhisaṃcaraḥ \|*  
*vasate puṇyadeśeṣu devabrāhnaṇasadmasu \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The zodiac Pisces appears as two fishes joined each other. It circulates through holy places and the oceans. It resides in sacred countries, temples and in the residences of Brahmins.

## \|\| 5.60 \|\|

*lakṣaṇā gaditāstubhyaṃ meṣādīnāṃ mahāmune \|*  
*na kasyacit tvayākhyeyaṃ guhyametatpurātanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. О great hermit! thus, I have told you the characteristics of Aries etc. zodiacs. Please, don't disclose this mystery to anybody.

## \|\| 5.61 \|\|

*etan mayā te kathitaṃ surarṣe yathā trinetraḥ pramātha yajñam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ purāṇaṃ paramaṃ pavitramākhyātavānpāpaharaṃ śivaṃ ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O Devarsi! I have completely explained the complete episode on destruction of yajna as spread by three-eyed Mahadeva. I have thus described this episode, most ancient, holiest, capable of absolving sins and showering with welfare as also enabling to perform noble deeds.

## Chapter 6. Episode of burning of Kama

## \|\| 6.1-4 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*hṛdbhavo brahmaṇo yo 'sau dharmo divyavapurmune \|*  
*dākṣāyāṇī tasya bhāryā tasyāmajanayatsutān \|\| 1 \|\|*

*hariṃ kuṣṇaṃ ca devarṣe nārāyaṇanarau tathā \|*  
*yogābhyāsaratau nityaṃ harikṛṣṇau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*naranārāyaṇau caiva jagato hitakāmyayā \|*  
*tapyetāṃ ca tapaḥ saumyau purāṇavṛṣisattmau \|\| 3 \|\|*

*prāleyādriṃ samāgamya tīrthe badarikāśrame \|*  
*gṛmantau tatparaṃ brahma gaṅgāyā vipule taṭe \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Pulastya said - О hermit! The divine body Dharma bom from the heart of Brahma, had reproduced Hari, Krsna, Nara and Narayana sons by virtue of consummating with his wife Daksayani. О divine sage! Hari and Krsna engrossed themselves with exercise on Yoga. Nara and Narayana, the greatest among all ancient sages began austerity with Parambrahma at the ever broad bank of the sacred Ganges in Badrikasrama, a place situated in the great Himalaya.

## \|\| 6.5 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇābhyāṃ ca jagadetaccarācaram \|*  
*tāpitaṃ tapasā brahman śakraḥ kṣobhaṃ tadā yayau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О Brahmin! Indra (the king of gods) became anxious when this entire universe consisting of active and inert organisms felt the heat (energy) on account of the penance made by Nara and Narayana.

## \|\| 6.6 \|\|

*saṃkṣubdhastapasā tābhyāṃ kṣobhamaṇāya śatakratuḥ \|*  
*rambhādyāpsarasaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ preṣayatsa mahāśramam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. As Indra was aggrieved, he sent the most beautiful divine prostitutes (Apsaras) so as to entice them and impede their penance. Among such prostitutes, Rambha was also sent.

## \|\| 6.7 \|\|

*kandarpaśca sudurdharṣaścūtāṅkuramahāyudhaḥ \|*  
*samaṃ sahacareṇaiva vasantenāśramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The sex-god (Kamadeva) with special weapon in the form of mango buds too went to that hermitage with his assistant spring (season) with a mission to deviate their penance.

## \|\| 6.8 \|\|

*tato mādhavakandarpau tāścaivāpsaraso varāḥ \|*  
*badaryāśramamāgamya vicikrīḍuryathecchayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The spring, sex-god and all divine prostitutes then began to spread sensuous feelings everywhere in Badrikasrama arbitrarily.

## \|\| 6.9 \|\|

*tato vasante saṃprāpte siṃśukā jvalanaprabhāḥ \|*
