*uttiṣṭhadhvaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ snātuṃ tīrthaṃ hi naimiṣam \|*  
*drakṣyāmaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ pītavāsasamacyutam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Prahlada ordered- "Be ready, all of us will go for a bath in the holy Naimisa and see there Pundarikaksa putting Pitambara and who is called Acyuta.

## \|\| 7.40 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ityuktā dānavendreṇa sarve te daityadānavāḥ \|*  
*cakrurudyogamatulaṃ nirjagmuśca rasātalāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Pulastya said - "All demons made compliance to the order, became ready and then came out from that nether world."

## \|\| 7.41 \|\|

*te samabhyetya daiteyā dānavāśca mahābalāḥ \|*  
*nemiṣāraṇyamāgatya snānaṃ cakrurmudānvitāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those mightiest Danavas took a bath in Naimisaranya with pleasure.

## \|\| 7.42 \|\|

*tato ditīśvaraḥ śrīmān mṛgavyāṃ sa cacāra ha \|*  
*caran sarasvatīṃ puṇyāṃ dadarśa vimalodakām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The demon king Prahlada then wished for hunting and started strolling in the forest adjacent to that place. He while strolling saw Sarasvati river which had cool and pure water.

## \|\| 7.43 \|\|

*tasyādūre mahāśākhaṃ śalavṛkṣaṃ śaraiścitam \|*  
*dadarśa bāṇānaparān mukhe lagnān parasparam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He further saw, at a little distance, a huge pipala tree having vast extended branches but it was shot by arrows stuck there. Some arrows were compact at their points (heads).

## \|\| 7.44 \|\|

*tatastānadbhutākārān bāṇān nāgopavītakān \|*  
*dṛṣṭvātulaṃ tadā cakre krodhaṃ daityeśvaraḥ kila \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Prahlada became angry when he saw those nagopavita arrows having excellent shape.

## \|\| 7.45 \|\|

*sa dadarśa tato 'dūrātkṛṣṇājinadharau munī \|*  
*samunnatajaṭābhārau tapasyāsaktamānasau \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He then saw two hermits engrossed deep in penance. They had put the hide of a black stag on the body and had long matted hair.

## \|\| 7.46 \|\|

*tayośca pārśvayordivye dhanuṣī lakṣaṇānvite \|*  
*śārṅgamāgavaṃ caiva akṣyyau ca maheṣudhī \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. There were kept at their sides, Sarnga and Ajagava divine bows and fwo grand and undepleting arrow-holders (tarakasa).

## \|\| 7.47-48 \|\|

*tau dṛṣṭvāmanyata tadā dāmibikāviti dānavaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ provāca vacanaṃ tāvubhau puruṣottamau \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kiṃ bhavadbhyāṃ samāraḥdhaṃ dambhaṃ dharmavināśanam \|*  
*kva tapaḥ kva jaṭābhāraḥ kva cemau pravarāyudhau \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The demon king Prahlada deemed them pomp and egoistic and said to them - why are you both doing such ostentation? One side you are immersed in penance and put matted hair so long while you have kept these divine weapons on the other.

## \|\| 7.49 \|\|

*athovāca naro daityaṃ kā te cintā ditīśvara \|*  
*sāmarthye sati yaḥ kuryāt tatsaṃpadyeta tasya hi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Nara then replied - "O demon king! Why are you so worried about our possession? If someone is competent to execute anything particular, he would have naturally the concerning equipment."

## \|\| 7.50 \|\|

*athovāca ditīśastau kā śaktiryuvayoriha \|*  
*mayi tiṣṭhati daityendre dharmasetupravartake \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Prahlada said- When I am here, the sole founder of religion, what power should you bath have?

## \|\| 7.51 \|\|

*narastaṃ pratyuvācātha āvābhyāṃ śaktirūrjitā \|*  
*na kaścicchaknuyād yoddhuṃ naranārāyaṇau yudhi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Nara replied- "We possess supreme powers. Nobody can dare to battle with us (Nara and Narayana) in the battle-field.

## \|\| 7.52 \|\|

*daityeśvarastastaḥ kruddhaḥ pratijñāmāruroha ca \|*  
*yathā kathañcijjeṣyāmi naranārāyaṇau raṇe \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Prahlada them promised- "I will defeat Nara and Narayana in battle by virtue of my divine powers."

## \|\| 7.53 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā ditīśvaraḥ sthāpya balaṃ vanānte \|*  
*vitatya cāpaṃ guṇamāvikṛṣya taladhvaniṃ ghorataraṃ cakāra \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. With this resolution, great Prahlada posted his army at the frontier of that forest, gave tension to his bow, tied the string on it and thus made a challenging sound by pulling and dropping the string.

## \|\| 7.54 \|\|

*tato narastvājagavaṃ hi cāpamānamya bāṇān subahuñśitāgrān \|*  
*mumoca tānapratimaiḥ pṛṣatkaiściccheda daityastapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Nara picked up his Ajagava bow and shot several sharp arrows. These arrows were, however, cut-off by the arrows having several wings shot by Prahlada. All those arrows were thus shattered into pieces.

## \|\| 7.55 \|\|

*chinnān samīkṣyātha naraḥ pṛṣatkān daityeśvareṇāpratimeva saṃkhye \|*  
*kruddhaḥ samānamya mahādhanustato mumoca cānyān vividhān pṛṣatkān \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Having seen the unique power of Prahlada and the arrows split by him, Nara gave a bend to his bow again and shot a number of arrows.

## \|\| 7.56 \|\|

*ekaṃ naro dvau ditijeśvaraśca trīn dharmasūnuścaturo ditīśaḥ \|*  
*narastu bāṇān pramumoca pañca ṣaḍ dratyanātho niśitān pṛṣatkān \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In a counter to the single arrow from Nara, Prahlada shot two, three when two arrows were shot by Nara and six arrows when five arrows were shot by Nara.

## \|\| 7.57 \|\|

*saptarṣimukhyo dvicatuśca daityo narastu ṣaṭ trīṇi ca daityamukhye \|*  
*ṣaṭtrīṇi caikaṃ ca ditīśvareṇa muktāni bāṇāni narāya vipra \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О Brahmin! Prahlada shot eight arrows when seven were shot by Nara and ten arrows for nine arrows from him.

## \|\| 7.58 \|\|

*ekaṃ ca ṣaṭ pañca nareṇa muktāstvaṣṭau śarāḥ sapta ca dānavena \|*  
*ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau nava ṣaṇnareṇa dvisaptatiṃ daityapatiḥ sasarjja \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Prahlada shot fifteen arrows when Nara shot twelve arrows at him. Similarly, he shot seventy-two arrows when Nara shot thirty six arrows.

## \|\| 7.59 \|\|

*śataṃ narastrīṇi śatāni daityaḥ ṣaḍ dharmaputro daśa daityarājaḥ \|*  
*tato 'pyasaṃkhyeyatarān hi bāṇān mumocatustau subhṛśaṃ hi kopāt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Three hundred arrows here shot by demon king when Nara shot one hundred arrows. He again shot one thousand arrows against six hundred arrows from Nara's side. Both of them then shot numerous arrows in order to defeat each other.

## \|\| 7.60 \|\|

*tato naro bāṇagaṇairasakhyairavāstaradbhūmimatho diśaḥ kham \|*  
*sa cāpi daityapravaraḥ pṛṣatkaiściccheda vegāt tapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Nara then covered the earth, ether and directions through a pile of arrows blown. Prahlada too on his part split them all by shooting arrows having gold wings.

## \|\| 7.61 \|\|

*tataḥ patattribhirvīrau subhṛśaṃ naradānavau \|*  
*yuddhe varāstrairyudhyetāṃ ghorarūpaiḥ parasparam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Both these warriors then hit fierce weapons and arrows at one another.

## \|\| 7.62 \|\|

*tatastu daityena varāstrapāṇinā cāpe niyuktaṃ tu pitāmahāstram \|*  
*maheśvarāstraṃ puruṣottameva samaṃ samāhatya nipetatustau \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Prahlada then took a supreme weapon in hand and put Brahmistra on his bow while Nara (Purusottama) exercised Mahesvarastra. Both these weapons collided with each other and were destroyed simultaneously.

## \|\| 7.63 \|\|

*brahmastre tu praśamite prahlādaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*gadāṃ pragṛhya tarasā pracaskanda rathottamāt \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Having seen that Brahmastra failed in its target, Prahlada was in furiated. He picked up his mace and jumped down from his chariot.

## \|\| 7.64 \|\|

*gadāpāṇiṃ samāyāntaṃ daityaṃ nārāyaṇastadā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvātha pṛṣṭhataścakre naraṃ yoddhūmanāḥ svayam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. When Narayana saw Prahlada advancing with his mace, he pulled back Nara and came in front for coupling with his attack.

## \|\| 7.65 \|\|

*tato dītīśaḥ sagadaḥ samādravat saśārṅgapāṇiṃ tapasāṃ nidhānam \|*  
*khyātaṃ purāṇarṣimudāravikramaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ nārada lokapālam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О Narada! Prahlada, the demon king with his mace then rushed towards great chivalrous Narayana who was with his Sarnga bow.

## Chapter 8. Boon offering to Prahlada

## \|\| 8.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*śārṅgapāṇinamāyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvāgre dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*paribhrāmya gadāṃ vegāt mūrdhni sādhyamatāḍayat \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Pulastya said- The demon king gave a strong blow on the head of Sadhya (Narayana) when he saw him marching forward.

## \|\| 8.2 \|\|

*tāḍitasyātha gadayā dharmaputrasya nārada \|*  
*netrābhyāmapatad vāri vahnivarṣanibhaṃ bhuvi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Narada! On account of the severe pain caused by such a hard blow, tears like fire-rain fell from the eyes of Narayana onto the ground.

## \|\| 8.3 \|\|

*mūrdhni nārāyaṇasyāpi sā gadā dānavārpitā \|*  
*jagāma śatadhā brahmañśailaśṛṅge yathāśaniḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Brahmin! As the thunderbolt is split when it is fallen on the mountain peak, the mace blown on the head of Narayana was split into several hundred pieces.

## \|\| 8.4 \|\|

*tato nivṛtya daityendraḥ samāsthāya rathaṃ drutam \|*  
*ādāya kārmukaṃ vīrastūṇad bāṇaṃ samādade \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The demon king then turned back immediately, rode on his chariot and took out an arrow from his tarakasa.

## \|\| 8.5 \|\|

*ānamya cāpaṃ vegena gārddhūpatrāñsilīmukhān \|*  
*mumoca sādhyāya tadā krodhandhakāritānanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He then in blind fury shot a number of arrows having vulture wings at Narayana.

## \|\| 8.6 \|\|

*tānāpatata evāśu bāṇāṃścandrārddhasannibhān \|*  
*ciccheda bāṇairaparairnirbibheda ca dānavam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Narayana cut-off those half-moon shaped arrows with his arrows and some other arrows were also shot to hit at Prahlada.

## \|\| 8.7 \|\|

*tato nārāyaṇaṃ daityo daityaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*āvidhyetāṃ tadānyonyaṃ marmabhidbhirajihyagaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then Narayana and Prahlada both exercised a number of acute and direct hitting arrows on each other.

## \|\| 8.8 \|\|

*tato 'mbare saṃnipāto devānāmabhavanmune \|*  
*didṛkṣūṇāṃ tadā yuddhaṃ laghu citraṃ ca suṣṭhu ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О hermit! A crowd of gods desirous to see this short-term, excellent and hurried battle gathered in the sky.

## \|\| 8.9 \|\|

*tataḥ surāṇāṃ dundubhyas tvavādyanta mahāsvanāḥ \|*  
*puṣpavarṣamanaupamyaṃ mumucuḥ sādhyadaityayauḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Those gods then played the trumpets making a loud noise and showered flowers on both the warriors.

## \|\| 8.10 \|\|

*tataḥ paśyatsu deveṣu gaganastheṣu tāvubhau \|*  
*ayudhyetāṃ maheṣvāsau prekṣakaprītivarddhanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. These great warriors and archers then fought a war throwing in surprise the crowd of spectators in the sky who all were gods.

## \|\| 8.11 \|\|

*babandhatustadākāśaṃ tāvubhau śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ \|*  
*diśaśca vidiśaścaiva chādayetāṃ śarotkaraiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Both of them shot numerous arrows and these covered the entire sky. All directions and the angles of those directions were filled with the stock of arrows so blown.

## \|\| 8.12-13 \|\|

*tato nārāyaṇaścāpaṃ samākṛṣya mahāmune \|*  
*bibheda mārgaṇaistīkṣṇaiḥ prahlādaṃ sarvamarmasu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tathā daityeśvaraḥ kruddhaścāpamānamya vegavān \|*  
*bibheda hṛdaye bāhvorvadane ca narottamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. O great hermit! Narayana exercised acute arrows and hit hard at the sensitive spots of Prahlada's body while Prahlada too hit at the heart region, both arms and on the face of Narayana.

## \|\| 8.14 \|\|

*tato 'syato daityapateḥ kārmukaṃ muṣṭibandhanāt \|*  
*cicchedaikena bāṇena candrārdhākāravarcasā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Narayana then shot an acute half-moon shaped arrow and cut-off the bow held by Prahlada just from the portion where the fist is made.

## \|\| 8.15 \|\|

*apāsyata dhanuśchinnaṃ cāpamādāya cāparam \|*  
*adhijyaṃ lāghavāt kṛtvā vavarṣa niśitāñśarān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Prahlada threw immediately that bow and replaced it with another. He then shot a shower of arrows at Narayana.

## \|\| 8.16 \|\|

*tānapyasya śarān sādhyaśchittvā bāṇairavārayat \|*  
*kārmukaṃ ca kṣurapreṇa ciccheda puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Narayana again split those arrows and cutoff that bow too.

## \|\| 8.17 \|\|

*chinnaṃ chinnaṃ dhanurdaityastvanyadanyatsamādade \|*  
*samādattaṃ tadā sādhyo mune ciccheda lāghavāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О hermit! Prahlada replaced one after another bows but all were cut-off frequently by Narayana with his extreme expertise in archery.

## \|\| 8.18 \|\|

*saṃchinneṣvatha cāpeṣu jagrāha ditijeśvaraḥ \|*  
*parighaṃ dāruṇāṃ dīrghaṃ sarvalohamayaṃ dṛḍham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Prahlada, when all bows were over, picked up a fierce and formidable Parigha made up of iron in large quantum.

## \|\| 8.19 \|\|

*parigṛhyātha parighaṃ bhrāmayāmāsa dānavaḥ \|*  
*bhrāmyamāṇaṃ sa ciccheda nārācena mahāmuniḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Не thus gave a circular move to Parigha but, in the meantime, Narayana shot an arrow and it was cut into parts.

## \|\| 8.20 \|\|

*chinne tu parighe śrīmān prahlādo dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*mudgaraṃ bhrāmya vegena pracikṣepa narāgraje \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When Parigha was cut-off, Prahlada gave a circle to Mudgara and threw it at Narayana.

## \|\| 8.21 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ balavān mārgaṇairdaśabhirmune \|*  
*ciccheda daśadhā sādhyaḥ sa chinno nyapatad bhuvi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О hermit! The mighty Narayana shot ten arrows and cut that Mudgara into ten pieces. It thus fell on the ground.

## \|\| 8.22 \|\|

*mudgare vitathe jāte prāsamāvidhya vegavān \|*  
*pracikṣepa narāgryāya taṃ ca ciccheda dharmajaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Prahlada took Prasa and threw it at Narayana when he saw that attack by Mudgara has failed. Narayana cut it also with his arrows.

## \|\| 8.23 \|\|

*prāse chinne tato daityaḥ śaktimādāya cikṣipe \|*  
*tāṃ ca ciccheda balavān kṣurapreṇa mahātapāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Prahlada on failure of attack by Prasa, took Sakti and threw it immediately but it was also cut into pieces by Narayana.

## \|\| 8.24 \|\|

*chinneṣu teṣu śastreṣu dānavo 'nyanmahaddhanuḥ \|*  
*samādāya tato bāṇairavatastāra nārada \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О Narada! The demon king then took other supreme bows (Mahadhanusa) and showered arrows on Narayana when the stock of all other weapons was finished and could do nothing.

## \|\| 8.25 \|\|

*tato nārāyaṇo devo daityanāthaṃ jagadguruḥ \|*  
*nārācena jaghānātha hṛdaye suratāpasaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then Jagadguru and supreme austere Narayana made a blow with Naraca just at the heart of the demon king.

## \|\| 8.26 \|\|

*saṃbhinnihṛdayo brahman devenādbhutakarmaṇā \|*  
*nipapāta rathopasthe tamapovāha sārathiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О Brahmin! That demon king fell down at the middle portion of his chariot on account of the severe blow at the heart region by Naraca (a weapon). His charioteer then immediately took him away.

## \|\| 8.27 \|\|

*sa saṃjñāṃ sucireṇaiva pratilabhya ditīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sudṛḍhaṃ cāpamādāya bhūyo yoddhamupāgataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The demon king came back to consciousness after many hours but he again appeared at that place for another battle. A strong bow this time was in his hand.

## \|\| 8.28 \|\|

*tamāgataṃ saṃnirīkṣya pratyuvāca narāgrajaḥ \|*  
*gaccha daityendra yotsyāmaḥ prātastvāhnikamācara \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Having seen him re-appeared, Narayana said- "O demon king! we will not fight in the morning. Go back and perform Anhika-karma

## \|\| 8.29 \|\|

*evamukto ditīśastu sādhyenādbhutakarmaṇā \|*  
*jagāma naimiṣāraṇyaṃ kriyāṃ cakre tadā'hnikīm \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Prahlada returned, visited Naimisaranya and performed Anhika-karma there.

## \|\| 8.30 \|\|

*evaṃ yudhyati deve ca prahlādo hyasuro mune \|*  
*rātrau cintayate yuddhe kathaṃ jeṣyāmi dāmbhikam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О hermit! Prahlada kept his mind busy throughout the night on a strategy to defeat Narayana by duly recollecting the experiences of the day.

## \|\| 8.31 \|\|

*evaṃ nārāyaṇenāsau sahāyudhyata nārada \|*  
*divyaṃ varṣasasraṃ tu daityo devaṃ na cājayat \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O Narada! Prahlada fought for several thousand divine years with Narayana; still he could not win him over.

## \|\| 8.32 \|\|

*tato varṣasahasrānte hyajite puruṣottame \|*  
*pītavāsasamabhyetya dānavo vākyamabravīt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. When he could not win Narayana in spite of the tremendous battle with him in which he applied his all skill and expertise, he went to lord Visnu and said-

## \|\| 8.33 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ devadeveśa sādhyaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim \|*  
*vijetuṃ nādya śaknomi etanme kāraṇaṃ vada \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О Mahadeva! Please tell me the reason why I could not win victory over Narayana till date?

## \|\| 8.34 \|\|

*pītavāsā uvāca \|*  
*durjayo 'sau mahābāhustvayā prahlāda dharmajaḥ \|*  
*sādhyo vipravaro dhīmān mṛdhe devāsurairapi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Lord Visnu replied- "O Prahlada! the great chivalrous son of Dharma is beyond your powers and you cannot defeat him. Those intelligent Sadhya Devas are invincible and undefeatable even by all the gods.

## \|\| 8.35 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*yadyasau durjayo deva mayā sādhyo raṇājire \|*  
*tatkathaṃ yatpratijñātaṃ tadasatyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Prahlada said- "O god! If those Sadhyadevas are unconquerable, what will then be of my promise? It will then prove a mere fallacy.

## \|\| 8.36 \|\|

*hīnapratijño deveśa kathaṃ jīveta mādṛśaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttavāgrato viṣṇo kariṣye kāyaśodhanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. "О lord! How can a man like me live life when spotted as false and resolute? О Visnu! I will therefore, give-up my breathing before you."

## \|\| 8.37 \|\|

*pulstya uvāca \|*  
*ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ devāgre dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*śiraḥsnātastadā tasthau gṛṇan brahma sanātanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Pulastya said- "With these words the demon king Prahlada set his breathing in head, seated himself there and started chanting the hymns relating to everlasting Brahma."

## \|\| 8.38 \|\|

*tato daityapatiṃ viṣṇuṃ pītavāsābravīdvacaḥ \|*  
*gaccha jeṣyasi bhaktyā taṃ na yuddhena kathañcana \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Lord Visnu then said to Prahlada- "Go there again. Remember that you can only win them with devotion and not by ensuing battle."

## \|\| 8.39 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*mayā jitaṃ devadeva trailokyamapi suvrata \|*  
*jito 'yaṃ tvatprasādena śakraḥ kimuta dharmajaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Prahlada said- О god of gods! О great resolute! I have won the three-world by virtue of having your pleasure with me. What to say about these sons of Dharma.

## \|\| 8.40 \|\|

*asau yadyajayo deva trailokyenāpi suvrataḥ \|*  
*na sthātuṃ tvatprasādeva śakyaṃ kimu karomyaja \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О unborn! If that resolute is undefeated by any person in the three-world and I cannot stand before him even after so backed by your pleasure, tell me then, what should I do?

## \|\| 8.41 \|\|

*pītavāsā uvāca \|*  
*so 'haṃ dānavaśārdūla lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*dharmaṃ pravarttāpayituṃ tapaścaryāṃ samāsthitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Lord Visnu said- О great demon king! Narayana is nobody else but I myself and busy there on penance in order to establish religion above all so that it could render place to all.

## \|\| 8.42 \|\|

*tasmādyadicchasi jayaṃ tamārādhaya dānava \|*  
*taṃ parājeṣyase bhaktyā tasmācchuśrūṣa dharmajam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence, О danavas! Do their worship if you want to win them. You can defeat them by your sheer devotion. Hence, serve those sons of Dharma.

## \|\| 8.43 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca\|*  
*ityuktaḥ pītavāsena dānavendro mahātmanā \|*  
*abravīdvacanaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ samāhūyāndhakaṃ muneṣa \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Pulastya said- О hermit, Prahlada pleased with this, called Andhaka and ordered.

## \|\| 8.44 \|\|

*daityāśca dānavāścaiva paripālyāstvayāndhaka \|*  
*mayotsṛṣṭamidaṃ rājyaṃ pratīcchasva mahābhuja \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Prahlada said- "O Andhaka! Provide maintenance to all daityas and danavas. О chivalrous! I abandon and assign the state and all stately affairs to you.

## \|\| 8.45 \|\|

*ityevamukto jagrāha rājyaṃ hairaṇyalocaniḥ \|*  
*prahlādo 'pi tadāgacchat puṇyaṃ badarikāśramam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In compliance with the order of Prahlada, Andhaka (son of Hiranyaksa) took over the liability of the state. Prahlada then went to Badrikasrama.

## \|\| 8.46 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ naraṃ ca ditijeśvaraḥ \|*  
*kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā vavande caraṇau tayoḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He saluted with his head on their (Nara and Narayana) feet at Badrikasrama.

## \|\| 8.47 \|\|

*tamuvāca mahātejā vākyaṃ nārāyaṇo 'vyayaḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ praṇato 'sīha māmajitvā mahāsura \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Narayana, the greatest genius and imperishable said to him- "O great demon king! Why have you shifted to salute instead of defeating me in battle."

## \|\| 8.48 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca\|*  
*kastvāṃ jetuṃ prabho śaktaḥ kastvattaḥ puruṣo 'dhikaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ hi nārāyaṇo 'nantaḥ pītavāsā janārdanaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Prahlada replied- "O lord! Who can conquer you? Who is the man here greater than you? You yourself are Janardana, Narayana immortal and Pitambaradhari.

## \|\| 8.49 \|\|

*tvaṃ devaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣastvaṃ viṣṇuḥ śārṅgacāpadhṛk \|*  
*tvamavyayo maheśānaḥ śāśvataḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. You are Pundarikaksa and Visnu with the Sarhga bow. You are imperishable, Mahesvara and immortal Purusottama.

## \|\| 8.50 \|\|

*tvāṃ yoginaścintayanti cārcayanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*japanti snātakāstvāṃ ca yajanti tvāṃ ca yājñikāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Yogis do meditation, scholars worship, celibates (snataka) do japa of your revered name and yajnikas perform yajna.

## \|\| 8.51 \|\|

*tvamacyuko hṛṣīkeśaścakrapāṇirdharādharaḥ \|*  
*mahāmīno hayaśirāstvameva varakacchapaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. You are Acyuta, Hrsikesa, Cakrapani, Dharadhara, Mahamatsya, Hayagriva and the greatest Kacchapa (Kurma).

## \|\| 8.52 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣaripuḥ śrīmān bhagavānatha sūkaraḥ \|*  
*matpiturnāśanakaro bhavānapi nṛkesarī \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. You are Sriman, killer of Hiranyaksa and god pig (Sukara). You yourself are the killer of my father god Nrsimha.

## \|\| 8.53 \|\|

*brahma trinetro 'mararāḍ hutāśaḥ pretādhipo nīrapatiḥ samīraḥ \|*  
*sūryo mṛgāṅko 'calajaṅgamādyo bhavān vibho nātha khagendraketo \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. You are Brahma, Mahadeva, Indra, Agni, Yama, Varuna and you are wind. О sovereign god! О administrator, О Garudadhvaja! You are the cause of the sun, moon, the immovable and movable.

## \|\| 8.54 \|\|

*tvaṃ pṛthvī jyotirākāśaṃ jalaṃ bhūtvā sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tvayā vyāptaṃ jagatsarvaṃ kastvāṃ jeṣyati mādhava \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. You are the earth, fire, sky and water. You are present in this whole universe in several thousand forms. О Madhava! Who will conquer you?

## \|\| 8.55 \|\|

*bhaktyā yadi hṛṣīkeśa toṣameṣi jagadguro \|*  
*nānyathā tvaṃ praśakto 'si jetuṃ sarvagatāvyaya \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О Jagadguru! О Hrsikesa! You can satisfy yourself only on the devotion made. О omniscient! О everlasting! you cannot be won in any way and by anybody.

## \|\| 8.56 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca\|*  
*parituṣṭo 'smi te daitya stavenānena suvrata \|*  
*bhaktyā tvanānyayā cāhaṃ tvayā daitya parājitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Lord said- О great resolute! О Daitya! I am pleased with your prayer. О Daitya! This exclusive devotion has defeated me.

## \|\| 8.57 \|\|

*parājitaśca puruṣo daitya daṇḍaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*daṇḍārthaṃ te pradāsyāmi varaṃ vṛṇu yamicchasi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О Daitya! The defeated man is given punishment but instead of receiving any punishment from you, it is I who will bless you. Ask for anything that you desire.

## \|\| 8.58-59 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇa varaṃ yāce yaṃ tvaṃ me dātumarhasi \|*  
*tanme pāpaṃ layaṃ yātu śārīraṃ mānasaṃ tathā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vācikaṃ ca jagannātha yattvayā saha yudhyataḥ \|*  
*nareṇa yadyapyabhavad varametatprayaccha me \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Prahlada said- О Narayana! You are competent to bless me with what I ask for. Hence, О Jagannatha! May the evil committed on my part through body, mind and speech in course of fighting, all that may be absolved. I pray and ask for it. Please, bless me with this boon.

## \|\| 8.60 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhavatu daidyendra pāpaṃ te yātu saṃkṣayam \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ prārthaya varaṃ taṃ dadāmi tavāsura \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Narayana said- О demon king! May it be as you wish. May your evils so committed be absolved. О demon! Ask for another thing. I will render it also.

## \|\| 8.61 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca \|*  
*yā yā jāyeya me buddhiḥ sā sā viṣṇo tvadāśritā \|*  
*devārcane ca niratā tvaccittā tvatparāyaṇā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Prahlada said- О Visnu! Whatever inspiration would get birth in my mind may that all be shelter to you, for worship to god and for meditation on you.

## \|\| 8.62 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ bhaviṣyatyasura varamanyaṃ yamicchasi \|*  
*taṃ vṛṇīṣva mahābāho pradāsyāmyavicārayan \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Narayana said- О demon! It shall be as desired. О chivalrous! Ask more whatever you like. I shall bless all that without application of my analysis.

## \|\| 8.63 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca\|*  
*sarvameva mayā labdhaṃ tvatprasādādadhokṣaja \|*  
*tvatpādapaṅkajābhyāṃ hi khyātirastu sadā mama \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Prahlada said- О Adhoksaja! I have got everything with your grace. May my popularity live long with

## \|\| 8.64 \|\|

*evamastvaparaṃ cāstu nityamevākṣayo 'vyayaḥ \|*  
*ajaraścāmaraścāpi matprasādād bhaviṣyasi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Sri Narayana said- It shall be as asked. Besides it, you shall be immortal, always youthful and invulnerable with my grace.

## \|\| 8.65 \|\|

*gacchasva daityaśārdūla svamāvāsaṃ kriyārataḥ \|*  
*na karmabandho bhavato maccittsya bhaviṣyati \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О lion to the demon dynasty! Go back to your residence and always be busy with religious deeds. You will not be betrayed by the bondage of Karma (deed) since your mind will be always with me.

## \|\| 8.66 \|\|

*praśāsayadamūn daityān rājyaṃ pālaya śāśvatam \|*  
*svajātisadṛśaṃ daitya kuru dharmamanuttamam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Rule ceaselessly over the demon subjects. О Daitya! Observe supreme religion as prescribed for your race.

## \|\| 8.67 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ityukto lokanāthena prahlādo devamabravīt \|*  
*kathaṃ rājyaṃ samādāsye parityaktaṃ jagadguro \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Pulastya said- When these words on blessing were over, Prahlada said to god- "O Jagadguru! Tell me, how should I regain the state, already abandoned?"

## \|\| 8.68 \|\|

*tamuvāca jagatsvāmī gaccha tvaṃ nijamāśrayam \|*  
*hitopadeṣṭā daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ tathā bhava \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The lord of the universe (Visnu) said- Retum to your residence and be preceptor to the Daityas and Danavas.

## \|\| 8.69 \|\|

*nārāyaṇenaivamuktaḥ sa tadā daityanāyakaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya vibhuṃ tuṣṭo jagāma nagaraṃ nijam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Prahlada accepted this suggestion, bowed before the lord and returned to his residence thereafter.

## \|\| 8.70 \|\|

*dṛṣṭaḥ sabhājitaścāpi dānavairandhakena ca \|*  
*nimantritaśca rājyāya na pratyaicchatsa nārada \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. О Narada! Andhaka and the Danavas greeted Prahlada on his return, requested to accept the throne again but he did not accept that offer.

## \|\| 8.71 \|\|

*rājyaṃ parityajya mahāsurendro niyojayan satpathi dānavendrān \|*  
*dhyāyan smaran keśavamaprameyaṃ tasthau tadā yogaviśuddhadehaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The great demon king (Prahlada) thus abounded the state, preached to the Danavas the ethics, engrossed himself in unique Kesava and attained purity of body through Yoga.

## \|\| 8.72 \|\|

*evaṃ purā nārada dānavendro nārāyaṇenottamapūruṣeṇa \|*  
*parājitaścāpi vimucya rājyaṃ tasthau mano dhātari sanniveśya \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. О Narada! long long ago Prahlada thus defeated by Purusottama Narayana, abandoned his state voluntarily and attained supreme position by virtue of his mind exclusively concentrated on lord Narayana.

## Chapter 9. Description of battle of demons and gods

## \|\| 9.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*netrahīnaḥ kathaṃ rājye prahlādenāndhako mune \|*  
*abhiṣikto jānatāpi rājadharmaṃ sanātanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada asked- "O hermit! Why did Prahlada incoronate the blind Andhaka in spite of his being well conversant with rules of everlasting Rajadharma?"

## \|\| 9.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*labdhacakṣurasau bhūyo hiraṇyākṣe 'pi jīvati \|*  
*lalo 'bhiṣikto daityena prahlādena nije pade \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Pulastya said- "He had regained eye-sight even at the time when his father Hiranyaksa was alive. As he was no more blind, Prahlada was justified in assigning to him the throne.

## \|\| 9.3 \|\|

*nārada uvāca\|*  
*rājye 'ndhako 'bhiṣiktastu kimācarata suvrata \|*  
*devādibhiḥ saha kathaṃ samāste tad vadasva me \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Narada asked again- О great resolute! Tell me what was done by Andhaka after the incoronation and what was his behaviour with the gods?

## \|\| 9.4-6 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*rājye 'bhiṣikto daityendro hiraṇyākṣasuto 'ndhakaḥ \|*  
*tapasārādhya deveśaṃ śūlapāṇiṃ trilocanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ajeyatvamavadhyatvaṃ surasiddharṣipannagaiḥ \|*  
*adāhyatvaṃ hutāśena akledyatvaṃ jalena ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa varalabdhastu daityo rājyamapālayat \|*  
*śukraṃ purohitaṃ kṛtvā samadhyāste tato 'ndhakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Pulastya replied- Andhaka after the incoronation, sat in penance for the pleasure of three-eyed lord Mahadeva. He thus was bestowed with powers by the undefeated gods, siddha, hermits and serpents, unbumt by fire and undrowned in water from lord Mahadeva. He then held the rein of state under the priestmanship of Sukracarya.

## \|\| 9.7 \|\|

*tataścakro samudyogaṃ devānāmandhako 'suraḥ \|*  
*ākramya vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ manujendrān parājayat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The demon Andhaka then developed war- craft and strategy for conquering the gods. He thus defeated all the kings on earth.

## \|\| 9.8 \|\|

*parājitya mahīpālān sahāyārthe niyojya cā \|*  
*taiḥ samaṃ meruśikharaṃ jagāmādbhutadarśanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After defeating kings, he appointed them as assistants to handle state affairs; he climbed in their company at the excellent peak of Meru mountain.

## \|\| 9.9 \|\|

*śakro 'pi surasainyāni samudyojya mahāgajam \|*  
*samāruhyāmarāvatyāṃ guptiṃ kṛtvā viniryayau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Indra too came out after assigning the proper defence-related instructions for Amaravati. He rode on Airavata elephant and set out to see that peak with the divine army.

## \|\| 9.10 \|\|

*śakrasyānu tathaivānye lokapālā mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*āruhya vāhanaṃ svaṃ svaṃ sāyudhā niryayurbahiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Other Lokapalas equipped with their weapons rode on their respective carriages (vans) and followed god Indra.

## \|\| 9.11 \|\|

*devasenāpi ca samaṃ śakroṇādbhutakarmaṇā \|*  
*nirjagāmātivegena gajavājirāthādibhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The divine army consisting of elephants, horses, chariot etc. also set out speedily with Indra, the king of gods.

## \|\| 9.12 \|\|

*agrato dvādaśādityāḥ pṛṣṭhataśca trilocanāḥ \|*  
*madhye 'ṣṭau vasavo viśve sādhyāśvimarutāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*yabhavidyādharādyāśca svaṃ svaṃ vāhanamāsthitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At the front of the army there were twelve Adityas, Trilocana (Rudraganas) at the back and eight Vasus, Visvedeva, Sadhya, Asvinikumara, Marudganas, demi-gods, Vidyadhara etc. in the middle. All began to march forward in their respective carriages (vans).

## \|\| 9.13 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*rudrādīnāṃ vadasveha vāhanāni ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*ekaikasyāpi dharmatra paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Narada said- О master in religion! Describe the names of carriages (vahanas) on which Rudra etc. had marched. I am curious to know this topic in detail.

## \|\| 9.14 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣva kathayiṣyāmi sarveṣāmapi nārada \|*  
*vāhanāni samāsena ekaikasyānupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Pulastya said- О Narada! I explain all vahanas in a series and precisely. Please, listen to me carefully.

## \|\| 9.15 \|\|

*rudrahastalotpanno mahāvīryo mahājavaḥ \|*  
*śvetavarṇo gajapatirdevarājasya vāhanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The white coloured Gajapati (Airavata), excellent in speed and power is the carriage (vahana) of god Indra. It originated from the palm of Rudra.

## \|\| 9.16 \|\|

*rudrorusaṃbhavo bhīmaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇo manojavaḥ \|*  
*pauṇḍrako nāma mahiṣo dharmarājasya nārada \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Narada! A buffalo called Paundraka, most fierce, dark in colour, a racer as mind itself, is the carriage of Dharmaraja. It originated from the thigh of Rudra.

## \|\| 9.17 \|\|

*rudrakarmamalodbhūtaḥ śyāmo jaladhisaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*śiśumāro divyagatiḥ vāhanaṃ varuṇasya ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The sisumara called Jaladhi is the carriage of Varuna. It was originated from the ear-wax (soil) of Rudra. It has dark-complexion and has divine speed.

## \|\| 9.18 \|\|

*raudraḥ śakaṭacakrākṣaḥ śailākāro narottamaḥ \|*  
*ambikāpādasaṃbhūto vāhanaṃ dhanadasya tu \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Narottama, having eyes like chariot wheels, a gigantic body as the mountain, a fierce figure is the carriage of Kubera. It originated from the feet of Ambika.

## \|\| 9.19 \|\|

*ekādaśānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ vāhanāni mahāmune \|*  
*gandharvāśca mahāvīryā bhujagondrāśca dāruṇāḥ \|*  
*śvetāni saurabheyāṇi vṛṣāṇyugrajavāni ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O great hermit! The carriages of eleven Rudras are white bulls. They originated from the ray of Gandharvas, fierce serpents and Saurabhi.

## \|\| 9.20 \|\|

*rathaṃ candramasaścārddhūsahasraṃ haṃsavāhanam \|*  
*harayo rathavāhāśca ādityā munisattama \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О great hermit! Half a thousand (i.e. five hundred) swans are the carriers of the moon's chariot and the horses carry the chariots of Adityas.

## \|\| 9.21 \|\|

*kuñjarasthāśca vasavo yakṣāśca naravāhanāḥ \|*  
*kinnarā bhujagārūḍhā hayārūḍhau tathāśvinau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Elephants are the carriages of Vasus, men are the carriages of demi-gods, serpents are the carriages of eunuchs (Kinnaras) and horses are die carriages of Asvinikumaras.

## \|\| 9.22 \|\|

*sāraṅgadhiṣṭhitā brahman maruto ghoradarśanāḥ \|*  
*sukārūḍhāśca kavayo gandharvāśca padātinaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О Brahmin! Stags are the carriages of fierce face Marudganas, parrots are the carriages of poets (Bhrgus) and Gandharvas are pedestrians.

## \|\| 9.23 \|\|

*āruhya vāhanānyevaṃ svāni svānyamarottamāḥ \|*  
*saṃnahya niryayurhṛṣṭā yuddhāya sumahaujasaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The great gods glowing with brilliance thus marched forward for war with cheers on their faces, properly equipped with weapons and rode on their respective carriers.

## \|\| 9.24 \|\|

*nārada uvāca\|*  
*gaditāni surādīnāṃ vāhanāni tvayā mune \|*  
*daityānāṃ vāhanānyevaṃ yathāvad vaktumarhasi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Narada said- О hermit! You have described the carriers of gods etc. Please, describe in the same way the carriers used by the Daityas for their riding.

## \|\| 9.25 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣva dānavādīnā vāhanāni dvijottama \|*  
*kathayiṣyāmi tattvena yathāvacchrotumarhasi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Pulastya said- О great Brahmin! Listen to the carriers used by the Danavas. I am going to describe them in substance.

## \|\| 9.26 \|\|

*andhakasya ratho divyo yuktaḥ paramavājibhiḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇavarṇaiḥ sahasrāras tranalvaparimāṇavān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. An immaterial (alankika) chariot of Andhaka is operated by the dark- complexioned horses. It has one thousand spikes. (The wood is fixed between the centre and the radius) and it is measured as twelve hundred hands in size.

## \|\| 9.27 \|\|

*prahlādasya ratho divyaścandravarṇairhayottamaiḥ \|*  
*uhyamānastathāṣṭābhiḥ śvetarukmamayaḥ subhaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The pink coloured beautiful and divine chariot of Prahlada is driven by eight best horses of moon tint.

## \|\| 9.28 \|\|

*virojanasya ca gajaḥ kujambhasya turaṅgamaḥ \|*  
*jambhasya tu ratho dviyo hayaiḥ kāñjanasannibhaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The carriage of Virocana is an elephant and Kumbhaja has a horse while the divine chariot of Jambha is driven by golden coloured horses.

## \|\| 9.29 \|\|

*śaṅkukarṇasya turago hayagrīvasya kuñjaraḥ \|*  
*ratho mayasya vikhyāto dundubheśca mahoragaḥ \|*  
*śambarasya vimāno 'bhūdayaḥ śaṅkormṛgādhipaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The carriage of Sanku Kama is a horse, the carriage of Hayagriva is an elephant, Maya has a grand chariot and the carriage of Dundubhi is a giant serpent.

## \|\| 9.30 \|\|

*vabalavṛtrau ca balinau gadāmusaladhāriṇau \|*  
*padbhyāṃ daivatasainyāni abhidravitumudyatau \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The carriage of Sambara is a Vimana and a lion is the carriage of Ayahsanku. Bala and Vrtra, the mighty Danavas, were ready to attack the divine army with mace and musala but without any carriage.

## \|\| 9.31-32 \|\|

*tato raṇo 'bhūt tumulaḥ saṃkulo 'tibhayaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*rajasā saṃvṛto lokī piṅgavarṇena nārada \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nājñāsīcca pitā putraṃ na putraḥ pitaraṃ tathā \|*  
*svānevānaye nijaghnurvai parānanye ca suvrata \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. A fierce battle was then fought. О Narada! The entire universe was covered with yellow coloured dust. It was so thick that a father was unable to recognise his son and a son his father. О great resolute! Some soldiers began to blow their weapons on their own people and some others began to attack the opponents on account of being tough to recognise.

## \|\| 9.33-34 \|\|

*abhidruto mahāvego rathopari rathastadā \|*  
*gajo mattagajendraṃ ca sādī sādinamabhyagāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*padātirapi saṃkruddhaḥ padātinamatholbaṇam \|*  
*parasparaṃ tu pratyaghnannanyonyajayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The warrior on the chariot attacked another chariot, the elephant with another warrior, elephant and horse riders marched forward to attack the soldiers who rode on horses. The pedestrians began to attack pedestrian soldiers. Thus, all these warriors began to shower blows on each other in order to defeat them.

## \|\| 9.35-36 \|\|

*tatastu saṃkule tasmin yuddhe daivāsure mune \|*  
*prāvartata nadī ghorā śamayantī raṇādrajaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śoṇitodā rathāvarttā yodhasaṃghaṭṭavāhinī \|*  
*gajakumbhamāhakūrmā śaramīnā duratyayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. О hermit! As a result of such fierce battle between gods and demons, there flowed an inaccessible river in which the water was of blood whirls were made by broken chariots, tortoise-like shells of dead elephants body and fish heads were seen. It was swaying the crowd of warriors and it had merged the dust so raised initially when the battle was started.

## \|\| 9.37-40 \|\|

*tīkṣṇāgraprāsamakarā mahāsigrāhavāhinī \|*  
*antraśaivalasaṃkīrṇā patākāphenamālinanī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*gṛdhrakaṅkamahāhaṃsā śyenacakraāhvamaṇḍitā \|*  
*vanavāyasakādambā gomāyuśvāpadākulā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*piśācamunisaṃkīrṇā dustarā prākṛtairjanaiḥ \|*  
*rathaplavaiḥ saṃtarantaḥ śūrāstāṃ prajagāhire \|\| 39 \|\|*

*āgulphaādavamajjantaḥ sūdayantaḥ parasparamḥ \|*  
*samuttaranto vegena yodhā jayadhanepsavaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. There were a large stock of crocodiles of sharp edge Prasa (weapon), Graha of axes, intestine algae, flags froth, Grdhra and Kanka flamingo, Sуеnа, Cakravaka, wild crow Kalahansa, jackal and sages Pisaca. It was tough to cross by common people. The chivalrous warriors who intended to gain victory were immersed up to the knees. They were crossing that river through the boats made of broken chariots yet were busy in blowing sharp weapons on each other.

## \|\| 9.41-42 \|\|

*tatastu raudro suradaityasādane mahāhave bhīrubhayaṅkare 'tha \|*  
*rakṣāṃsi yakṣāśca susaprahṛṣṭāḥ piśācayūthāstvabhiremire ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*pibantyasṛggāḍhataraṃ bhaṭānāmāliṅgya māṃsāni ca bhakṣayanti \|*  
*vasāṃ vilumpanti ca vanisphuranti garjantyathānyonyamatho vayāṃsi \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. The monsters and demi-gods as also Pisacas were very glad to see such a fierce battle between the demons and gods in which both were meeting to destruction while it was dreadful to the cowards. The Pisaca and monsters were sipping concentrated blood and eating flesh with mirth. The carnivorous birds were busy piercing the flesh in pieces and they would reveal annoyance had any other bird come and interfered with their work.

## \|\| 9.43 \|\|

*muñcanti phetkāraravāñśivāśca krandanti yodhā bhuvi vedanārttāḥ \|*  
*śastraprataptā nipatanti cānye yuddhaṃ śmaśānapratimaṃ babhūva \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The jackals were yelling, the warriors injured and fallen down were crying in pain. Some soldiers began to fall down wounded by the blows from weapons and arms again and gradually the entire battle-field was turned into a cremation ground.

## \|\| 9.44 \|\|

*tasmiñśivāghorarave pravṛtte murāsurāṇāṃ subhayaṅkare ha \|*  
*yuddhaṃ babhau prāṇapaṇepaviddhaṃ dvandve 'tiśastrākṣagato durodaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The battle between the gods and demons was fought so fiercely with the yelling of jackals, that it appeared as if the warriors skilled in war-craft betted their life with weapon formed pasa had engaged themselves in gambling.

## \|\| 9.45 \|\|

*hiraṇyacakṣustanayo raṇe 'ndhako rathe sthito vājisahasrayojite \|*  
*mattebhaṣṭaṣṭasthitamugratejasaṃ sameyivān devapatiṃ śatakratum \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Andhaka, the son of Hiranyaksa marched forward by riding on a chariot driven by one thousand horses to fight against Indra, the king of gods who rode on the intoxicated Airavata elephant.

## \|\| 9.46 \|\|

*samāpatantaṃ mahiṣādhirūḍhaṃ yamaṃ pratīcchad balavān ditīśaḥ \|*  
*prahlādanāmā turagāṣṭayuktaṃ rathaṃ samāsthāya samudyātāstraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The demon king Prahlada rode on a chariot driven by eight horses, took weapons in hands and faced aggressive Yama on a buffalo boldly in the battle.

## \|\| 9.47 \|\|

*virocanaścāpi jaleśvaraṃ tvagājjambhastvathāgād dhanadaṃ balāḍhyam \|*  
*vāyuṃ samabhyetya ca śambaro 'tha mayo hutāśaṃ yuyudhe munīndra \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O great hermit! Virocana advanced to fight with Varuna in battle, Jambha marched to face the mighty Kubera, Sambara marched to face Vayu while Maya began to fight against fire-god.

## \|\| 9.48 \|\|

*anye hayagrīvamukhā mahābalā ditestanūjā danupuṅgavāśca \|*  
*surān hutāśārkavasūrakeśvarān dvandvaṃ samāsādya mahābalānvitāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hayagriva etc. other mighty Daitya and Danavas began to fight against fire, sun, eight vasus and urgesvara etc. gods.

## \|\| 9.49 \|\|

*garjantyathānyonyamupetya yuddhe cāpāni karṣantyativegitāśca \|*  
*muñcanti nārācagaṇān sahasraśa agaccha he tiṣṭhasi kiṃ bruvantaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. They faced each other with sharp challenging statements, gave extra-tension to their bows, shot a shower of arrows and began to say- "Oh! Come! Come hurriedly. Why are you so stopped?"

## \|\| 9.50 \|\|

*śaraistu tīkṣṇairatitāpayantaḥ śastrairamoghairabhitāḍayantaḥ \|*  
*mandākinīveganibhāṃ vahantīm pravartayanto bhayadāṃ nadīṃ ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Showering arrows and making attack with acute weapons those people gave an extreme flow to a fierce battle river whose flow was analogous to that of Mandakini.

## \|\| 9.51 \|\|

*trailokyamākāṅkṣibhirugravegaiḥ surāsurairnārada saṃprayuddhe \|*  
*piśācarakṣogaṇapuṣṭivardhanīmuttartumicchadbhirasṛgnadī babhai \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Narada! The aggressive gods and demons intended to cross the blood-stream which was making healthy the Pisacas and monsters and to win the three-worlds.

## \|\| 9.52 \|\|

*vādyanti tūryāṇi surāsurāṇām paśyanti khasthā munisiddhasaṃghāḥ \|*  
*nayanti tānpsarasāṃ gaṇāgryā hatā raṇe ye 'bhimukhāstu śūrāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. (At that time) several musical instruments were being played from both sides (i.e. gods and demons), a crowd of hermits and siddhas were observing that battle and the warriors killed in war were being brought to heaven by the nymphs.

## Chapter 10. Victory of Andhaka

## \|\| 10.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ pravṛtte saṃgrāme bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhane \|*  
*sahasrakṣo mahācāpamādāya vyasṛjaccharān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Pulastya said- On having started the fear aggravating battle for cowards, lord Indra began to shoot arrows from his grand bow.

## \|\| 10.2 \|\|

*andhako 'pi mahāvegaṃ dhanurākṛṣya bhāsvaram \|*  
*purandarāya cikṣepa śarān barhiṇavāsasaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Andhaka too reciprocated the attack on Indra by shooting at him numerous arrows having the shape of peacock wings.

## \|\| 10.3 \|\|

*tāvanyonyaṃ sutīkṣṇāgraiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ \|*  
*rukmapuṅkhairmahāvegairājaghnaturubhāvapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Both of them injured each other by shooting the arrows of bend nodes, wing shaped and most acute.

## \|\| 10.4-5 \|\|

*cacaḥ kruddhūḥ śatamakhaḥ kuliśaṃ bhrāmya pāṇinā \|*  
*cikṣepa daityarājāya taṃ dadarśa tathāndhakaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ājaghāna ca bāṇaughairastraiḥ sa nārada \|*  
*tān bhasmasāttadā cakre nagāniva hutāśanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Aggrieved Indra then gave a circular motion to thunderbolt and threw it at Andhaka. Andhaka saw it and О Narada! he also attacked with arrows, weapons and arms. As the fire bums in ashes the trees, the thunderbolt had burnt them all.

## \|\| 10.6 \|\|

*tato 'tiveginaṃ vajraṃ dṛṣṭvā balavatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*samāplutya rathāttasthau bhuvi bāhu sahāyavān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The mightiest Andhaka then jumped from the chariot down without weapon in hand and stood on ground when he saw thunderbolt rapidly approaching him.

## \|\| 10.7 \|\|

*rathaṃ sārathinā sārdhaṃ sāśvadhvajasakūbam \|*  
*bhasma kṛtvātha kuliśamandhakaṃ samupāyayau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. That thunderbolt first burnt into ashes the charioteer, horse, flag and Kubara including chariot and then accessed to Andhaka.

## \|\| 10.8 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ vegena muṣṭināhatya bhūtale \|*  
*pātayāmāsa balavān jagarja ca tadāndhakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The mighty Andhaka blew his fist on thunderbolt knocked it down and began to yell with anger.

## \|\| 10.9 \|\|

*taṃ garjamānaṃ vīkṣyātha vāsavaḥ sāyakairdṛḍham \|*  
*vavarṣa tān vārayan sa samabhyāyācchatakratum \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Indra shot a shower of arrows at him when he saw him yelling in anger. He shattered them all and then rushed to Satakratu (Indra).

## \|\| 10.10 \|\|

*ājaghāna talenebhaṃ kumbhamadhye padā kare \|*  
*jānunā ca samāhatya viṣāṇaṃ prababhañja ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He slapped at the stomach of Airavata and hit hard at his trunk by foot. He further gave a sharp blow on his tusk and broke it down.

## \|\| 10.11 \|\|

*vāmamuṣṭyā tathā pārśvaṃ samāhatyāndhakastvaran \|*  
*gajendraṃ pātayāmāsa prahārairjarjarīkṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. And Andhaka then hurriedly hit at the side of that elephant by his left fist. It was intolerable and the giant elephant thus fell down on the ground.

## \|\| 10.12 \|\|

*gajendrāt patamānācca avaplutya śatakratuḥ \|*  
*pāṇinā vajramādāya praviveśāmarāvatīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Indra jumped from Airavata when it was falling, took the thunderbolt in hand and moved hurriedly to Amaravati.

## \|\| 10.13 \|\|

*paraṅmukhe sahasrākṣe tadā daivatabalaṃ mahat \|*  
*pātayāmā dratyendraḥ pādamuṣṭitalādibhiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. That demon-king used frequently his fist, legs, hands and killed a considerable part of the divine army when Indra showed his back to the battle.

## \|\| 10.14 \|\|

*tato vaivasvato daṇḍaṃ paribhrāmya dvijottama \|*  
*samabhyadhāvat prahlādaṃ hantukāmaḥ surottamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O great Brahmin! Yama then rushed toward Prahlada to give a sharp blow with his danda to which he was giving circular motion rapidly.

## \|\| 10.15 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ bāṇaighairvavarṣaṃ ravinandanam \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putraś cāpamānamya vegavān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the chivalrous son of Hiranyakasipu saw the son of Rabi (Yama) marching forward, a shower of arrows flow from his bow.

## \|\| 10.16 \|\|

*tāṃ bāṇavṛṣṭimatulāṃ daṇḍenāhatya bhāskariḥ \|*  
*śātayitvā pracikṣepa daṇḍaṃ lokabhayaṅkaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Yamaraja destroyed that cluster of arrows through his danda and threw them with full might on Prahlada.

## \|\| 10.17 \|\|

*sa vāyupathamāsthāya dharmarājakare sthitaḥ \|*  
*jajvāla kālagninibho yadvad dagdhuṃ jagattrayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Having discharged from the hand of Yama, that danda began luminating in flames like Kalagni. It appeared as if the time for destruction of three-world has come.

## \|\| 10.18 \|\|

*jājvalyamānāmāyāntaṃ daṇḍaṃ dṛṣṭvā diteḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*prākrośanti hataḥ kaṣṭaṃ prahlādo 'yaṃ yamena hi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Daityas began crying when they saw Kaladanda forwarding- "Alas! Prahlada is now killed by Yamaraja."

## \|\| 10.19 \|\|

*tamākranditamākarṇya hiraṇyākṣasuto 'ndhakaḥ \|*  
*provāca mā bhaiṣṭaca mayi sthite ko 'yaṃ surādhamaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Having attracted to their cries, Andhaka cooled them by saying- "Don’t be afraid. What is the existence of this meanest god till I am living."

## \|\| 10.20 \|\|

*ityevasuktvā vacanaṃ vegenābisasāra ca\| jagrāha pāṇinā daṇeḍaṃ hasan savyena nārada \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О Narada! He rushed with these words and caught that danda with the left hand smilingly.

## \|\| 10.21 \|\|

*tamādāya tato vegād bhrāmayāmāsa cāndhakaḥ \|*  
*jagarja ca mahānādaṃ yathā prāvṛṣi toyadaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Andhaka then gave it a circular motion and cried in anger so loud as if clouds during rainy season thundered.

## \|\| 10.22 \|\|

*prahlādaṃ rakṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā daṇḍād daityeśvareṇa hi \|*  
*sādhuvādaṃ dadurhṛṣṭā daityadānavayūthapāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When the commanders in Daitya and Danavas' army saw Prahlada defended by Andhaka, they cheered loud and tendered gratitude for him.

## \|\| 10.23 \|\|

*bhrāmayantaṃ mahādaṇḍaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhānusuto mune \|*  
*duḥsahaṃ durdharaṃ matvā antardhānamagād yamaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О hermit! When Yama, the son of Surya saw Andhaka has gripped the Mahadanda and giving in circular motion; he immediately vanished from there assuming it intolerable and acute to bear.

## \|\| 10.24 \|\|

*antarhite dharmarāje prahlādo 'pi mahāmune \|*  
*dārayāmāsa balavān devasainyaṃ samantataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О great hermit! When Yama so vanished, mighty Prahlada began to kill the divine army all around.

## \|\| 10.25-26 \|\|

*varuṇaḥ śiśumārastho baddhvā pāśairmahāsurān \|*  
*gadayā dārayāmāsa tamabhyāgād virocanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tomarairvajrasaṃsparśaiḥ śaktibhirmārgaṇairapi \|*  
*jaleśaṃ tāḍayāmāsa mudgaraiḥ kaṇapairapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. When Varuna riding on Sisumara (sunsa) had fastened the demons with Pasa and began to give hard blows from his mace, Virocana immediately appeared there to face him. He gave hard blows with his tomaras, saktis, arrows, mudgaras, kanapa and spears on Varuna.

## \|\| 10.27 \|\|

*tatastaṃ gadayābhyetya pātayitvā dharātale \|*  
*abhidrutya babandhātha pāśairmattagajaṃ balī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Varuna rushed at him, hit him hard with his mace, knocked him down and gripped his elephant by Pasa (strings).

## \|\| 10.28 \|\|

*tān pāśāñśatadhā cakre vegācca danujeśvaraḥ \|*  
*varuṇaṃ ca samabhyetya madhye jagrāha nārada \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Virocana split in several pieces those pasas. О Narada! He caught the loin of Varuna in a hard grip.

## \|\| 10.29 \|\|

*tato dantī ca śṛṅgābhyāṃ pracikṣepa tadāvyayaḥ \|*  
*mamarda ca tathā padbhyāṃ savāhaṃ salileśvarām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The elephant imperishable then blew its teeth and knocked down Varuna on ground. He then crushed him with his chariot under its huge feet.

## \|\| 10.30 \|\|

*taṃ mardyamānaṃ vīkṣyātha śaśāṅkaḥ śiśirāśumān \|*  
*abhyetya tāḍayāmāsa mārgaṇaiḥ kāyadāraṇaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Having seen Varuna so crushed, the moon god rushed there and shot arrows on the elephant.

## \|\| 10.31 \|\|

*sa tāḍyamānaḥ śiśirāṃśubāṇairavāpa pīḍāṃ paramāṃ gajendraḥ \|*  
*duṣṭaśca vegāt payasāmadhīśaṃ muhurmuhuḥ pādatalairmamarda \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The elephant suffered severe pain but was not afraid of crushing Varuna under its feet. His feet were churning Varuna's body barbarously.

## \|\| 10.32-33 \|\|

*sa mṛdyamāno varuṇo gajendraṃ padbhyāṃ sugāḍhaṃ jagṛhe maharṣe \|*  
*pādeṣu bhūmiṃ karayoḥ spṛśaṃśca mūrddhānamullālya balānmahātmā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*gṛhyāṅgulībhiśca gajasya pucchaṃ kṛtveha bandhaṃ bhujageśvareṇa \|*  
*utpāṭya cikṣepa virocanaṃ hi sakuñjaraṃ khe saniyantṛvāham \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. О great hermit! Chivalrous Varuna gripped tightly both feet of the elephant, lifted his head and body by taking support from his hands and feet, gripped the elephant's tail, fastened Virocana with the serpent and threw him along with the elephant, the chariot and charioteer up into the sky.

## \|\| 10.34 \|\|

*kṣipto jaleśena virocanastu sakuñjaro bhūmitale papāta \|*  
*sāṭṭaṃ sanyatrārgalaharmyabhūmi puraṃ sukeśeriva bhaskareṇa \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. As Bhaskara once collapsed the city consisting of multi-storeyed buildings, apparatus, gates and palaces pertaining to Sukesi, the elephant thrown by Varuna fell with a heavy thud on the ground.

## \|\| 10.35 \|\|

*tato jaleśaḥ sagadaḥ sapāśaḥ sambhyadhāvad ditijaṃ nihantum \|*  
*tataḥ samākrandamanuttamaṃ hi muktaṃ tu daityairghanarāvatulyam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Varuna then rushed to slaughter other Daityas with mace and Pasa in his hand. Daityas began to cry in pain as loud as the clouds thunder.

## \|\| 10.36 \|\|

*hā hā hato 'sau varuṇena vīro virocano dānavasainyapālaḥ \|*  
*prahlāda he jambhakujambhakādyā rakṣadhvamabhyetya sahāndhakena \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. "Oh! the chivalrous Virocana is being thrashed by Varuna. О Prahlada! Come with Jambha, Kujambha etc. and Andhaka and ensure his defence.

## \|\| 10.37 \|\|

*aho mahātmā balavāñjaleśaḥ saṃcūrṇayan daityabhaṭaṃ savāham \|*  
*pāśena baddhvā gadayā nihanti yathā paśuṃ vājimakhe mahendraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Oh! the warrior Varuna was thrashing Virocana by blows from mace after fastening him in Pasa so barbarously as Indra slaughtered the animal in horse sacrifice (Asvamedha).

## \|\| 10.38 \|\|

*śrutatvātha śabdaṃ ditijaiḥ samīritaṃ jambhapradhānā ditijeśvarāstataḥ \|*  
*samabhyadhāvaṃstvaritā jaleśvaraṃ yathā pataṅgā jvalitaṃ hutāśanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Having heard the grievous call from Daityas, Jambha etc. prominent Daityas rushed so fast towards Varuna as the insects rush to the flames.

## \|\| 10.39 \|\|

*tānāgatān vai prasamīkṣya devaḥ prāhlādisutsṛjya vitatya pāśam \|*  
*gadāṃ samudbhrāmya jaleśvarastu dudrāva tān jambhamukhānarātīn \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When Varuna saw such a composite attack from the Daityas, he left Virocana, immediately spread Pasa in its full length, gave a circular motion to mace and turned towards Jambha etc. enemies.

## \|\| 10.40 \|\|

*jambhaṃ ca pāśena tathā nihatya tāraṃ talenāśanisaṃnibhena \|*  
*pādena vṛtraṃ tarasā kujambhaṃ nipātayāmāsa balaṃ ca muṣṭyā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Не knocked down Jambha by fastening him with Pasa, Tara demon by slapping, Vrtrasura by kick, Kujambha and Bala demons by hard hit through boxing.

## \|\| 10.41 \|\|

*tenārditā devavareṇa daityāḥ saṃprādravan dikṣu vimuktaśastrāḥ \|*  
*tato 'ndhakaḥ satvarito 'bhyupeyād raṇāya yoddhuṃ jalanāyakena \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The daityas so knocked down by Varuna dropped down their weapons and ran away hither and thither. Andhaka then immediately appeared there to face Varuna.

## \|\| 10.42 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ gadayā jaghāna pāśena baddhvā paruṇo 'sureśam \|*  
*taṃ pāśamāvidhya gadāṃ pragṛhya cikṣepa daityaḥ sa ca jaleśvarāya \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Varuna tied that demon king in Pasa and blew his mace on his body. The demon snatched these weapons and threw them on Varuna.

## \|\| 10.43 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ prasamīkṣya pāśaṃ gadāṃ ca dākṣāyaṇinandanastu \|*  
*viveśa vegāt payasāṃ nidhānaṃ tato 'ndhako devabalaṃ mamarda \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Having seen Pasa and mace forwarding, Varuna (Baksayani's son) immediately entered into the sea. Andhaka then started killing the Deva army.

## \|\| 10.44 \|\|

*tato hutāśaḥ suraśatrusainyaṃ dadāha roṣāt pavanāvadhūtaḥ \|*  
*tamabhyayād dānavaviśvakarmā mayo mahābāhurudagravīryaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The fire blazed by wind then started burning the demon army into ashes. The demon architect (Visvakarma) chivalrous Maya then appeared before him.

## \|\| 10.45 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ saha śambareṇa samīkṣya vahniḥ pavanena sārdham \|*  
*śaktyā mayaṃ śambarametya kaṇṭhe saṃtāḍya jagrāha balānmaharṣe \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О great hermit! When the fire god saw Maya forwarding with Sambara, he joined with the wind god, hit hard by sakti at the throat of Sambara and gripped them forcibly.

## \|\| 10.46 \|\|

*śaktyā sa kāyāvaraṇe vidārite saṃbhinnadeho nyapatat pṛthivyām \|*  
*mayaḥ prajajvāla ca śamvaro 'pi kaṇṭhāvalagne jvalane pradīpte \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. As the shield of Maya was penetrated, his injured body fell down on the ground on account of the severe blow from sakti. Sambara's throat too began burning.

## \|\| 10.47 \|\|

*sa dahyamāno ditijo 'gninātha suvisvaraṃ ghorataraṃ rurāva \|*  
*siṃhābhipanno vipine yathaiva matto gajaḥ krandati vedanārttaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. That demon began weeping so loudly as the intoxicated elephant trumpets in pain when attacked by a lion. This was due to burning from fire so erupted.

## \|\| 10.48 \|\|

*taṃ śabdamākarṇya ca śambarasya daityeśvaraḥ krodhaviraktadṛṣṭiḥ \|*  
*āḥ kiṃ kimetannanu kena yuddhe jito mayaḥ śambaradānavaśca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Having heard that piteous cry, Andhaka filled with anger said- "Aha! What is it? Who has defeated Maya and Sambara in battle?

## \|\| 10.49 \|\|

*tato 'bruvan daityabhaṭā ditīśaṃ pradahyate hyeṣa hutāśanena \|*  
*rakṣasva cābhyetya na śakyate 'nyairhutāśano vārayituṃ raṇāgre \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The demon warriors then reported- "The fire is burning him. Rescue him immediately. Nobody other than you can prevent the fire in the battle.

## \|\| 10.50 \|\|

*itthaṃ sa daityairabhinoditastu hiraṇyacakṣustanayo maharṣe \|*  
*udyamya vegāt parighaṃ hutāśaṃ samādravat tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bruvan hi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. О great hermit! As soon as the report was over, Andhaka picked up Parigha and rushed towards the fire ordering him to stop, stop now.

## \|\| 10.51 \|\|

*śrutvāndhakasyāpi vaco 'vyayātmā saṃkruddhacittastvarito hi daityam \|*  
*utpāṭya bhūmyāṃ ca viniṣpipeṣa tato 'ndhakaḥ pāvakamāsasāda \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Avyayatma fire immediately lifted that daitya up and then dashed down forcibly when it heard the challenge from Andhaka. By then Andhaka accessed to the fire.

## \|\| 10.52 \|\|

*samājaghānātha hutāśanaṃ hi varayudhenātha varāṅgamadhye \|*  
*samāhato 'gniḥ parimucya śambaraṃ tathāndhakaṃ sa tvarito 'bhyadhāvat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He gave a sharp blow on the head of fire with a weapon. The fire so injured, then left Sambara and rushed immediately towards Andhaka.

## \|\| 10.53 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ parigheṇa bhūyaḥ samāhananmūrdhni tadāndhako 'pi \|*  
*sa tāḍito 'gnirditijeśvareṇa bhayāt pradudrāva raṇājirādvi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Andhaka again hit hard with Parigha on the head of fire. The fire god could not tolerate such a sharp blow one after another; was badly frightened and ran away from the battlefield.

## \|\| 10.54 \|\|

*tato 'ndhako mārutacandrabhāskarān sādhyān sarudrāśvivasūn mahoragān \|*  
*yān yāñśareṇa spṛśate parākramī parāṅmukhāṃstānkṛtavān raṇājirāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Andhaka, the most chivalrous demon, then gave sharp blows from his arrows to the wind, moon, sun, Sadhya, Rudra, Asvinikumaras, Vasus and giant serpents. They all could not stand there and departed from the battle-field.

## \|\| 10.55 \|\|

*tato vijityāmarasainyasugraṃ sendraṃ sarudraṃ sayamaṃ sasomam \|*  
*saṃpūjyamāno danupuṅgavaistu tadāndhako bhūmimupājagāma \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thus, Andhaka subjugated the entire armies of Indra, Rudra, Yama, Soma etc., praised by the danavas and then descended onto the earth.

## \|\| 10.56 \|\|

*āsādya bhūmiṃ karadān narendrān kṛtvā vaśe sthāpya carācaraṃ ca\| jagatsamagraṃ praviveśa dhīmān pātālamagryaṃ puramaśmakāhvam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He then subjugated all kings, imposed taxes on them, enslaved the entire movable and immovable world and lastly, entered into the nether world and accessed to his Asmaka city.

## \|\| 10.57 \|\|

*tatra sthitasyāpi mahāsurasya gandharvavidyādharasiddhasaṃghāḥ \|*  
*sahāpsarobhiḥ paricāraṇāya pātālamabhyetya samāvasanta \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. In order to render services to Andhaka, then great king to Danava, Gandharvas including nymphs, Vidyadharas and group of Siddhas came down to the nether world and began residing there.

## Chapter 11. Description of Puskara Dvipa

## \|\| 11.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*yadetad bhavatā proktaṃ sukeśinakaro 'mbarāt \|*  
*pātito bhuvi sūryoṇa tatkadā kutra kutra ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said- "You had explained the collapsed city of Sukesi from sky to the earth which was done by Surya. Please, tell us when and where that incident happened?

## \|\| 11.2 \|\|

*sukeśīti ca kaścāsau kena dattaḥ puro 'sya ca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ pātito bhūmyāmākāśād bhāskareṇa hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. "Who was Sukesi? Who had given him that city and why did Bhaskara clash it down on the earth?

## \|\| 11.3 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca\|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā kathāmetāṃ purātanīm \|*  
*yathoktavān svayaṃbhūrmāṃ kathyamānāṃ mayānagha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Pulastya said- О innocent hermit! I am going to tell this most ancient episode as I heard it from lord Brahma. Please, listen to it carefully.

## \|\| 11.4 \|\|

*āsīnniśācarapatirvidyutkeśīti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro guṇajyeṣṭhaḥ sukeśirabhavattataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There was a famous demon king called Vidyutkesi. He was blessed with a meritorious son Sukesi.

## \|\| 11.5 \|\|

*tasya tuṣṭastatheśānaḥ puramākāśacāriṇam \|*  
*prādādajeyatvamapi śatrubhiścāpyavadhyatām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Lord Siva was pleased with him and rendered him a mobile city in the sky and also made him Unconquerable and invulnerable by the enemies.

## \|\| 11.6 \|\|

*sa cāpi śaṅkarāt prāpya varaṃ gaganagaṃ puram \|*  
*reme niśācaraiḥ sārddhū sadā dharmapathi sthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He began to live happily abidingly religion with demons on receipt of that mobile city in the space.

## \|\| 11.7 \|\|

*sa kadācid gato 'raṇyaṃ māgadhaṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatrāśramāṃstu dadṛśo ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Once he visited Magadharanya and saw there asramas of hermits extremely devoted to god.

## \|\| 11.8 \|\|

*maharṣin sa tadā dṛṣṭvā praṇipatyābhivādya ca\| pratyuvāca ṛṣīn sarvān kṛtāsanaparigrahaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He did salute to them, seated there and said-

## \|\| 11.9 \|\|

*sukeśiruvāca \|*  
*praṣṭumicchāmi bhavataḥ saṃśayo 'yaṃ hṛdi sthitaḥ \|*  
*kathayantu bhavanto me na cauvājñāpayāmyaham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Sukesi said- "I am not passing any order but went to make some enquiries on some points still not clear to me. Please, give me an appropriate explanation.

## \|\| 11.10 \|\|

*kiṃsvicchreyaḥ pare loke kimu ceha dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kena pūjyastathā satsu kenāsau sukhamedhate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O great Dvijas! What is welfare (benevolent) in this mortal and that immortal world? How does a man deserve honour among gentlemen and how can he attain to pleasure?

## \|\| 11.11 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca\|*  
*itthaṃ sukeśivacanaṃ niśamya paramarṣayaḥ \|*  
*procurvimṛsya śreyor'thamiha loke paratra ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Pulastya said- "Those great hermits first did introspection and then replied on the enquiry so made by Sukesi."

## \|\| 11.12 \|\|

*ṛṣa ūcuḥ \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ kathayiṣyāmastava rākṣasapuṅgava \|*  
*yaddhi śreyo bhaved vīra iha cāmutra cāvyayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The hermits said- "O demon king! О warrior! We now say about the everlasting and benevolent thing in

## \|\| 11.13 \|\|

*śreyo dharmaḥ pare loke iha ca kṣaṇadācara \|*  
*tasmin samāśritaḥ satsu pūjyastena sukhī bhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O demon! Religion is the welfare for both the material and metaphysical worlds. The man resorted to religion deserves honour among gentlemen and attains peace too.

## \|\| 11.14 \|\|

*sukeśiruvāca \|*  
*kiṃlakṣaṇo bhaved dharmaḥ kimācaraṇasatkriyaḥ \|*  
*yamāśritya na sīdanti devādyāstu taducyatām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Sukesi said- "What is the characteristic of religion? What are the noble deeds and conduct inherent therein, resorting to which the gods etc., never feel the cruel touch of sorrows. Kindly describe the same.

## \|\| 11.15 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ paramo dharmaḥ sadā yajñādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*svādhyāyavedavettṛtvaṃ viṣṇupūjāratiḥ smṛtā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The hermits said- "The supreme religion of gods is to perform yajna etc., deeds, perseverance, to perform yajna etc., deeds, perseverance, to acquire knowledge on Vedas and keep themselves engross in the worship of lord Visnu.

## \|\| 11.16 \|\|

*daityānāṃ bāhuśalitvaṃ mātsaryaṃ yuddhasatkriyā \|*  
*vedanaṃ nītiśāstrāṇāṃ harabhaktirudāhṛtā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The religion of daityas is to acquire physical stamina, jealousy, war craft, knowledge on ethics and devotion to god Siva.

## \|\| 11.17 \|\|

*siddhānāmudito dharmo yogayuktiranuttamā \|*  
*svādhyāyaṃ brahmavijñānaṃ bhaktirdvābhyāmapi sthirā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. It is the religion of Siddhas that they do practise Yoga study on the Vedas, science on Brahma and a firm devotion to Visnu and Siva.

## \|\| 11.18 \|\|

*utkṛṣṭopāsanaṃ jñeyaṃ nṛtyavādyeṣu veditā \|*  
*sarasvatyāṃ sthirā bhaktirgāndharvo dharma ucyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The religion of Gandharva is to perform worship, to acquire knowledge on dance and music and undeviated devotion for goddess Sarasvati.

## \|\| 11.19 \|\|

*vidyādharatvamatulaṃ vijñānaṃ pauruṣe matiḥ \|*  
*vidyādharāṇāṃ dharmo 'yaṃ bhavānyāṃ bhaktireva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The religion of Vidyadharas is to acquire unique learning, science, strong inspiration for mind application and devotion for Bhavani.

## \|\| 11.20 \|\|

*gandharvavidyāveditvaṃ bhaktirbhānau tathā sthirā \|*  
*kauśalyaṃ sarvaśilpānāṃ dharmaḥ kiṃpuruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The religion of eunuchs is to acquire knowledge on Gandharva Vidya, strong devotion to god sun and expertise in all crafts.

## \|\| 11.21 \|\|

*brahmacaryamamānitvaṃ yogābhyāsaratirdṛḍhā \|*  
*sarvatra kāmacāritavaṃ dharmo 'yaṃ paitṛkaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The religion of ancestors is to observe celibacy, egolessness, strong attachment with practice on Yoga and frequent touring worldwide.

## \|\| 11.22 \|\|

*brahmacaryaṃ yatāśitvaṃ japyaṃ jñānaṃ ca rākṣasa \|*  
*niyamāddharmaveditvamārtho dharmaḥ pracakṣyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О monster! The religion of hermits is to observe celibacy, balance food-habits, Japa, conscience and to acquire knowledge on religion regularly.

## \|\| 11.23-24 \|\|

*svādhyāyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ ca dānaṃ yajanameva ca \|*  
*akārpaṇyamanāyāsaṃ dayāhiṃsā kṣamā damaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*jitendriyatvaṃ śaucaṃ ca māṅgalyaṃ bhaktiracyute \|*  
*śaṅkare bhāskare devyāṃ dharmo 'yaṃ mānavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The religion of human beings is to do perseverance, celibacy, donation, yajna, generosity, attachment for hard labour, kindness, non-violence, forgiveness, control on senses, purity, benevolence and devotion for Visnu, Sankara, Bhaskara and the goddess.

## \|\| 11.25 \|\|

*dhanādhipatyaṃ bhogāni svādhyāyaṃ śakararcanam \|*  
*ahaṅkāramaśauṇḍīryaṃ dharmo 'yaṃ guhyakeṣviti \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The religion of Guhyakas is to acquire wealth in abundance, to enjoy, to do perseverance, worship of god Sankara, egotism and cowardice.

## \|\| 11.26 \|\|

*paradārāvamarśitvaṃ pārakyer'the ca lolupā \|*  
*svādhyāyaṃ tryambake bhaktirdharmo 'yaṃ rākṣasaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The religion of monsters is to do intercourse with other's wife, greed for other's money, to do perseverance and worship of god Siva.

## \|\| 11.27 \|\|

*avivekamathājñānaṃ śaucahānirasatyatā \|*  
*piśācānāmayaṃ dharmaḥ sadā cāmiṣagṛdhnutā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The religion of Pisacas is to live without discretion, in ignorance, impurity, falsehood and temptation for flesh diet.

## \|\| 11.28 \|\|

*yonayo dvādaśaivaitāstāsu dharmāśca rākṣasa \|*

28\. О monster! These are the twelve yonis. Pitamaha Brahma has described their twelve sacred and supreme position deserving religions.

## \|\| 11.29 \|\|

*sukeśiruvāca \|*

29\. Sukesi said- Again highlight the religion of mankind out of the twelve everlasting and immortal religions.

## \|\| 11.30 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*
