50\. The sages replied- Listen to us about that territory. Presently, it belongs to Vasudva (Hari) but it will go to lord Байкала in future. This territory of Hari is extended from Yogasayi to Kesava-darsana. It is known as Varanasi Puri.

## \|\| 15.51 \|\|

*yogaśāyinamārabhya yāvat keśavadarśanam \|*  
*etat kṣetraṃ hareḥ puṇyaṃ nāmnā vārāṇasī purī \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When it was heard, god sun cursed by Sankara at that time fell down in the middle of Varuna and Asi rivers.

## \|\| 15.52 \|\|

*tacchrutvā bhagavān bhānurbhavanetrāgnitāpitaḥ \|*  
*varaṇāyāstathaivāsyāstvantare nipapāta ha \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. As god sun was anxious due to excessive temperature caused to the body as a result of lord Siva's burning eye-rays, he first took a bath in Asi and then Varuna river.

## \|\| 15.53 \|\|

*tataḥ pradahyati tanau nimajyāsyāṃ lulad raviḥ \|*  
*varaṇāyāṃ samabhyetya nyamajjata yathecchayā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Не began to rush from Asi to Varuna and then Varuna to Asi frequently like an Alatacakra due to the burning sensation felt by having Siva’s eye imposed.

## \|\| 15.54-55 \|\|

*bhuyo 'siṃ varaṇāṃ bhūyo bhūyo 'pi varaṇāmasim \|*  
*lulaṃstriṇetravahnyārtto bhramate 'lātacakravat \|\| 54 \|\|*

*etasminnantare brahman ṛṣayo yakṣarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*nāgā vidyādharāścāpi pakṣiṇo 'psarasastathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. О Brahmin! О hermit! All hermits, monsters, serpents, vidyadhara, birds, nymphs and bhuta-preta on sun's chariot rushed in the meantime to the abode of Brahma and reported this tragedy.

## \|\| 15.56 \|\|

*yāvanto bhāskararathe bhūtapretādayaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*tāvanto brahmasadanaṃ gatā vedayituṃ mune \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Lord Brahma then visited Mandara mountain, an attractive abode of Mahesvara to ask his grace for sun in company of gods.

## \|\| 15.57 \|\|

*tato brahma surapatiḥ suraiḥ sārdha samabhyagātaṭ \|*  
*ramyaṃ maheśvarāvāsaṃ mandaraṃ ravikāraṇāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He met Sulapani there, pleased him for the sake of sun and brought him to Varanasi.

## \|\| 15.58 \|\|

*gatvā dṛṣṭvā ca deveśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śūlapāṇinam \|*  
*prasādya bhāskarārthāya vārāṇasyāmupānayat \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Lord Sankara lifted him up with support of hand, addressed him as lola and again seated him on the chariot.

## \|\| 15.59 \|\|

*tato divākaraṃ bhūyaḥ pāṇinādāya śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā nāmāsya loleti rathamāropayat punaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. When sun was again seated on his chariot, lord Brahma went to Sukesi and settled him again with kith and kin, the subject and city in the sky.

## \|\| 15.60-61 \|\|

*āropite dinakare brahmābhyetya sukeśinam \|*  
*sabāndhavaṃ sanagaraṃ punarāropayad divi \|\| 60 \|\|*

*samāropya sukeśiṃ ca pariṣvajya ca śaṅkaram \|*  
*praṇamya keśavaṃ devaṃ vairājaṃ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Brahma returned to his abode known as Vairaja just after he re-settled Sukesi in sky, embraced lord Sankara and saluted Kesava there.

## \|\| 15.62 \|\|

*evaṃ purā nārada bhāskareṇa puraṃ sukeśerbhuvi sannipātitam \|*  
*divākaro bhūmitale bhavena kṣiptastu dṛṣṭyā na ca saṃpradagdhaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O Narada! The sun god during ancient period had thus dashed the city of Sukesi down on the earth and Mahadeva had thrown down the sun on the ground and not burnt him by the fire dwelling in his third eye.

## \|\| 15.63 \|\|

*āropito bhṛmitalād bhavena bhūyo 'pi bhānuḥ pratibhāsanāya \|*  
*svayaṃbhuvā cāpi niśācarendras tvāropitaḥ khe sapuraḥ sabandhuḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Sankara again established sun for shining regularly from the earth to the sky and Brahma had settled again Sukesi with his city and commune in the sky.

## Chapter 16. Description of Sleep of Gods &amp; Austerities on Dvitiya and Kalastami

## \|\| 16.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*yānetān bhagavān prāha kāmibhiḥ śaśinaṃ prati \|*  
*ārādhanāya devābhyāṃ harīśābhyāṃ vadasva tān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said- Kindly describe the fasts/resolutions you referred to for sensuous people about moon for the worship of Sri Hari and Sankara.

## \|\| 16.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca\|*  
*śṛṇuṣva kāmibhiḥ proktān vratān puṇyān kalipriya \|*  
*ārādhanāya śarvasya keśavasya ca dhīmataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Pulastya said- О Kalipriya Narada! The holy fasts as referred to by sensuous people for worship of Mahadeva and lord Kesava is now being told by me. Listen to these carefully.

## \|\| 16.3 \|\|

*yadā tvāṣāḍhī saṃyāti vrajate cottarāyaṇam \|*  
*tadā svapiti deveśo bhogibhoge śriyaḥ patiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Sripati Devesa (lord Visnu) slumber on the bed of Sesanaga when uttarayana is over and full moon of Asadha month comes nearer.

## \|\| 16.4 \|\|

*pratisupte vibhau tasmin devagandharvaguhyakāḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ mātaraścāpi prasuptāścāpyanukramāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The gods, gandharva, guhyaka and devamatas are also asleep when that sovereign god is gone to sleep.

## \|\| 16.5 \|\|

*nārada uvāca\|*  
*kathayasva kurādīnāṃ śayane vidhimuttamam \|*  
*sarvamanukrameṇaiva puraskṛtya janārdanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Narada requested- Kindly tell me the procedure adopted by the gods including Janardana and first start it with Hari.

## \|\| 16.6 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*mithunābhigate sūrye śuklapakṣe tapodhana \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ jagatsvāmī śayanaṃ parikalpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Pulastya said- О austere hermit! Janardana, the ruler of this entire universe, goes to sleep on Ekadasi tithi when the sun enters into the zodiac Gemini during the fortnight when the moon shines.

## \|\| 16.7-8 \|\|

*śeṣāhibhogaparyaṅkaṃ kṛtvā saṃpūjya keśavam \|*  
*kṛtvopavītakaṃ caiva samyaksaṃpūjya vai dvijān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*anujñānaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaśca dvādaśyāṃ prayataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*labdhvā pītāmbaradharaḥ svasti nidrāṃ samānayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Subsequent to worship of Sri Kesava with sacred thread on shoulder and body of Sesanaga as a cot, one should lay Pitambaradhara on Dvadasi tithi for sleeping with due permission of Brahmanas and maintaining control on senses as also with observing the purity.

## \|\| 16.9 \|\|

*trayodaśyāṃ tataḥ kāmaḥ svapate śayane śubhe \|*  
*kadambānāṃ sugandhānāṃ kusumaiḥ parikalpite \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then on Trayodasi tithi, Kamadeva sleeps on a holy cot made up of scented Kadamba flowers.

## \|\| 16.10 \|\|

*caturdaśyāṃ tato yakṣāḥ svapanti sukhaśītale \|*  
*sauvarṇapaṅkajakṛte sukhāstīrṇopadhānake \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then there sleep on Caturdasi Yaksas (demi-gods) on cots made by the golden lotus with quilts and sheets duly spread.

## \|\| 16.11 \|\|

*paurmamāsyāmumānāthaḥ svapate carmasaṃstare \|*  
*vaiyāghre ca jaṭābhāraṃ samudgranthyānyacarmaṇā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On Purnamasi tithi (full moon day) Sankara sleeps on the bed of tiger a hide by tying his matted hair with another hide.

## \|\| 16.12 \|\|

*tato divākaro rāśiṃ saṃprayāti ca karkaṭam \|*  
*tato 'marāṇāṃ rajanī bhavate dakṣiṇāyanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The sun then enters into the zodiac Cancer and from this day Daksinayana in the night commences for all gods.

## \|\| 16.13 \|\|

*brahmā pratipadi tathā nīlotpalamaye 'nagha \|*  
*talpe svapiti lokānāṃ darśayan mārgamuttamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О innocent! Brahma sleeps on the bed of blue lotus on Pratipada tithi guiding people the right and fair way.

## \|\| 16.14-16 \|\|

*viśvakarmā dvitīyāyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ gireḥ sutā \|*  
*vināyakaścurthyā tu pañcamyāmapi dharmarāṭ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ skandaḥ prasvapiti saptamyāṃbhagavān raviḥ \|*  
*kātyāyanī tathāṣṭamyāṃ navamyāṃ kamalālayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*daśamyāṃ bhujagendrāśca svapante vāyubhojanāḥ \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ tu kṛṣṇāyāṃ sādhyā brahman svapanti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. О Brahmin! Visvakarma sleeps on dvitiya, goddess Parvati on trtiya, Ganesa on caturthi, Dharmaraja on pancami, Skanda on sasthl, god sun on saptami, Katyayani on astami, Laksmi on navami, the serpents living on air sleep on dasami and Sadhya-ganas on ekadasi.

## \|\| 16.17 \|\|

*eṣa kramaste gadito nabhādau svapane mune \|*  
*svapatsu tatra deveṣu prāvṛṭkālaḥ samāyayau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О hermit! We have told you the orderly manner for slumbering the gods in sravana etc. months. There comes the rainy season when gods are asleep.

## \|\| 16.18 \|\|

*kaṅkāḥ samaṃ balākābhirārohanti nagottamān \|*  
*vāyasāścāpi survanti nīḍāni ṛṣipuṅgava \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О the great hermit! the particulars of dust rode on the peak of mountains and crows start building their nests while feminine crows kept on sleeping throughout this season due to laxity arisen in their womb.

## \|\| 16.19 \|\|

*vāyasāśca svapantyete ṛtau garbhabharālasāḥ \|*  
*yasyāṃ tithyāṃ prasvapiti viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*\|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The tithi in which Visvakarma goes to sleep that sacred dvitiya tithi is called as Asunyasayana.

## \|\| 16.20-21 \|\|

*dvitīyā sā śubhā puṇyā aśūnyaśayanoditā \|*  
*tasyāṃ tithāvarcya hariṃ śrīvatsāṅkaṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*\|\| 20 \|\|*

*paryaṅkasthaṃ samaṃ lakṣmyā gandhapuṣpādibhirmune \|*  
*tato devāya śayyāyāṃ phalāni prakṣipet kramāt \|*  
*surabhīṇī nivedyetthaṃ vijñāpyo madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. O hermit! One should on that tithi first worship Hari having four arms, Srivatsa mark on heart and body on Sesanaga's cot with Laksmi by offering fragrance and flowers etc., then offer fruits and scents and prayer as under-

## \|\| 16.22 \|\|

*yathā hi lakṣmyā na viyujyase tvaṃ trivikramānanta jagannivāsa \|*  
*tathāstvaśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ sadaiva asmākameveha tava prasādāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О Trivikrama! О Ananta, О Jagannivasa! As you never be separated from Laksmi, our living should never be void of wife by your grace.

## \|\| 16.23 \|\|

*yathā tvaśūnyaṃ tava deva talpaṃ samaṃ hi lakṣmyā varadācyuteśa \|*  
*satyena tenāmitavīrya viṣṇo gārhasthyanāśo mama nāstu deva \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O god! О Varada! О Acyuta! О Isa! О lord Visnu! As your bed never is void of Laksmi, our household life should never be destroyed by virtue of this truth.

## \|\| 16.24 \|\|

*ityuccārya praṇamyeśaṃ prasādya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*naktāṃ bhuñjīta devarṣe tailakṣāravivarjitamaṭ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О divine hermit! subsequent to the prayer so made, one should salute again and again the gracious god for his pleasure and eat food at night without oil and salt mixed.

## \|\| 16.25 \|\|

*dvitīye 'hni dvijāgryāya phalān dadyād vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*lakṣmīdharaḥ prīyatāṃ me ityuccārya nivedayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The wise man should offer fruit to the learned Brahmin by chanting "May Laksmidhara be gracious to me" on the next day.

## \|\| 16.26 \|\|

*anena tu vidhānena cāturmāsyavrataṃ caret \|*  
*yāvad cavṛścikarāśisthaḥ pratibhāti divākaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. One should observe Caturmasya fast till the sun remains on the zodiac Scorpio by observing this procedure.

## \|\| 16.27 \|\|

*tato vibudhyanti surāḥ kramaśaḥ kramaśo mune \|*  
*tulāsther'ke hariḥ kāmaḥ śivaḥ paścādvibudhyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О hermit! Then the gods awake in an orderly manner. Hari is awakened when the sun enters into the zodiac Libra. Kama and Siva awake thereafter.

## \|\| 16.28 \|\|

*tatra dānaṃ dvitīyāyāṃ mūrttirlakṣmīdharasya tu \|*  
*saśayyāstaraṇopetā yathā vibhavamātmanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then the icon of Laksmidhara with their bed should be donated according to one’s own capacity on Dvitiya.

## \|\| 16.29 \|\|

*eṣa vratastu prathamaḥ proktastava mahāmune \|*  
*yasmiṃś cīrṇe viyogastu na bhavediha kasyacit \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О great hermit! Thus, I have told you about the procedure for the first fast. By observing it, nobody suffers from the pain of separation from his wife throughout his life in this world.

## \|\| 16.30 \|\|

*nabhasye māsi ca tathā yā syātkṛṣṇāṣṭamī śubhā \|*  
*yuktā mṛgaśireṇaiva sā tu kālāṣṭamī smṛtā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Similarly, Krsnastami with Mrgasira constellation in the month of Bhadrapada is assumed as Kalastami.

## \|\| 16.31 \|\|

*tasyāṃ sarveṣu liṅgeṣu tithau svapiti śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*vasate saṃnidhāne tu tatra pūjākṣayā smṛtā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. God Sankara on that tithi sleeps in all lingas and resides in the premises where these lingas are found. The worship of lord Sankara made on his occasion is assumed as integrated.

## \|\| 16.32 \|\|

*tatra snāyīna vai vidvān gomūtreṇa jalena ca \|*  
*snātaḥ saṃpūjayet puṣpairdhattūrasya trilocanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The learned man should take a bath with a mixture of water and cow urine on that tithi. He should worship god Sankara by offering the flower of thorn apple plant after having such a bath.

## \|\| 16.33 \|\|

*dhūpaṃ kesaraniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhusarpiṣī \|*  
*prīyatāṃ me virūpākṣastvityuccārya ca dakṣiṇām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O the best Dvija! One should offer Brahmin daksina and naivedya and gold with words on his lips that "May Virupaksa be gracious to me" after offering Dhupa made of gum extracted from saffron, honey and ghee as naivedya.

## \|\| 16.34-35 \|\|

*viprāya dadyānnaivedyaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*tadvadāśvayuje māsi upavāsī jitendriyaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*navamyāṃ gomayasnānaṃ kuryātpūjāṃ tu paṅkajaiḥ \|*  
*dhūpayet sarjaniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhumodakaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Similarly, one should observe fasts on Navami tithi in Asvina month, take a bath by rubbing cowdung on the body, hold control over the senses and do worship by offering lotus flowers, dhupa of gum extracted from Sarja tree and naivedya of honey and modaka.

## \|\| 16.36 \|\|

*kṛtopavāsastavaṣṭamyāṃ navamyāṃ snānamācaret \|*  
*prīyatāṃ me hiraṇyākṣo dakṣiṇā satilā smṛtā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Не should observe fast on Astami and offer daksina mixed with sesamum with the words on his lips after a bath that "May I deserve the grace of god Hiranyaksa."

## \|\| 16.37-38 \|\|

*kārttike payasā snānaṃ karavīreṇa cārcanam \|*  
*dhupaṃ śrīvāsaniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhupāyasam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*sanaivedyaṃ ca rajataṃ dātavyaṃ dānamagraje \|*  
*prīyatāṃ gavān sthāsuriti vācyamaniṣṭhuram \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. He should take a milk bath and worship by offering the flower of Karavira. Then dhupa of gum from Srivasa (sarala) tree, naivedya of honey and sweet meat (payasa) should be offered and with chanting that "May I deserve the grace of god Sthanu"; silver with naivedya should be given to the Brahmin.

## \|\| 16.39 \|\|

*kṛtvopavāsamaṣṭamyāṃ navamyāṃ snānamācaret \|*  
*māsi mārgaśire snānaṃ dadhnārcā bhadrayā smṛtā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One should observe fast on Astami and take a curd bath on Navami in the month of Margasira. Worship with offering Bhadra (specific medicine) on this occasion has been suggested.

## \|\| 16.40 \|\|

*dhūpaṃ śrīvṛkṣaniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhunodanam \|*  
*saṃnivedyā raktaśālirdakṣiṇā parikīrttitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The learned man should offer dhupa of gum from Srivrksa and naivedya of honey and odana and give daksina of Raktasali with chanting that "salute to Sarva, may you be pleased with me."

## \|\| 16.41-42 \|\|

*namo 'stu prīyatāṃ śarvastviti vācyaṃ ca paṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*pauṣe snānaṃ ca haviṣā pūjā syāttagaraiḥ subhaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*dhūpo madhukaniryāso naivedyaṃ madhu śaṣkulī \|*  
*samudgā dakṣiṇā proktā prīmanāya jagadguroḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. The wise man should take a bath with ghee and worship with beautiful flowers of tagara in the month of Pausa. Then dhupa of gum from madhuka tree and naivedya of honey and saskuli should be offered and daksina with munja (mudga) for the pleasure of Jagadguru is given with chanting- О god of gods Tryambaka! I salute you.

## \|\| 16.43-44 \|\|

*vācyaṃ namaste deveśa tryambaketi prakīrtayet \|*  
*māghe kuśodakasnānaṃ mṛgamadena cārcyanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*dhūpaḥ padambaniryāso naivedyaṃ satilodanam \|*  
*payobhaktaṃ sanaivedyaṃ sarukmaṃ pratipādayet \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. One should take a bath with kusa immersed water and do worship with musk in the month of Magha. Dhupa of gum from Kadamba tree and naivedya of sesamum and odana should then be offered. Daksina consisting of gold with milk and cooked rice with words on lips- "May Umapati (Sankara) confer grace on me" should then be given.

## \|\| 16.45 \|\|

*prīyatāṃ me mahādeva umāpatiritīrayet \|*  
*evameva samuddiṣṭaṃ ṣaḍbhirmāsaistu pāraṇam \|*  
*pāraṇānte trinetrasya snapanaṃ kārayetkramāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus, provision of Parana (first) after six months has been explained. At the end of Parana one should perform the bathing of Mahadeva in an orderly manner.

## \|\| 16.46 \|\|

*gorocanāyāḥ sahitā guḍena devaṃ samālabhya ca pūjayeta \|*  
*prīyasva dīno 'smi bhavantamīśa macchokanāśaṃ prakuruṣva yogyam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. One should smear the icon of Mahadeva with gorocana mixed jaggery and pray as- "O god! I am a pauper and am sheltered by you. Grant me grace and eradicate my agony."

## \|\| 16.47-49 \|\|

*tatastu phālgune māsiṃ kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ yatavrata \|*  
*upavāsaṃ samudītaṃ kartavyaṃ dvijasattama \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dvitīye 'hni tataḥ snānaṃ pañcagavyena kārayet \|*  
*pūjayetkundakusumairdhūpayet candanaṃ tvapi \|\| 48 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāṃ ca dvijātibhyo naivedyasahitāṃ mune \|*  
*vāsoyugaṃ prīṇayecca rudramuccārya nāmataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. O resolute Brahmin! One should then observe fast on Krsnastami of Phalguna. He should give a bath with pancagavya to the icon, offer dhupa of sandal, flower of kunda and naivedya of jaggery; and odana with ghee in a copper vessel should then be offered. Brahmins should be given daksina with naivedya and two garments and lord Mahadeva should be pleased by chanting frequently "Rudra".

## \|\| 16.50-52 \|\|

*vāsoyugaṃ prīṇayecca rudramuccārya nāmataḥ \|*  
*caitre codumbaraphalaiḥ snānaṃ mandārakārcanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*gugguluṃ mahiṣākhyaṃ ca ghṛtāktaṃ dhūpayed budhaḥ \|*  
*samodakaṃ tathā sarpiḥ prīṇanaṃ vinivedayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇā ca sanaivedyaṃ sṛgājinamudāhṛtam \|*  
*nāṭyeśvara namaste 'stu idamuccārya nārada \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. One should give a bath with gulara- immersed water and worship by offering the flowers of mandara in the month of Caitra. The wise man should then offer dhupa of guggula known as Mahisa by duly mixing it with ghee and ghee with modaka for the pleasure of god. Daksina of deer-hide with naivedya is to be given with chanting as- "Salute to Natakesvara." Thus, Devanatha should be pleased with sheer obeisance.

## \|\| 16.53-55 \|\|

*prīṇanaṃ devanāthāya kuryācchraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*vaiśākhe snānamuditaṃ sugandhakusumāmbhasā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*pūjanaṃ śaṅkarasyoktaṃ cūtamañjaribhirvibho \|*  
*dhūpaṃ sarjājyayuktaṃ ca naivedyaṃ saphalaṃ ghṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*nāmajapyamapīśasya kālaghneti vipaścitā \|*  
*jalakumbhān sanaivedyān brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

53-55. O sovereign god! A provision of giving a bath with scented flowers and worship of Sankara with mango-buds is made in the month of Vaisakha. Dhupa of gum from Saija tree mixed with ghee and naivedya of ghee and fruit is to be offered. The wise man should do japa of Kalaghna Siva and daksina of naivedya, sacred thread and water-pot with cereal etc. should be given to the expert and devoted Brahmana.

## \|\| 16.56-58 \|\|

*sopavītān sahānnādyāṃstaccittaistatparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe snānaṃ cāmalakaiḥ pūjār'kakusumaistathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*dhūpayettattrinetraṃ ca āyatyāṃ puṣṭikārakam \|*  
*saktūṃśca saghṛtān deve dadhnāktān vinivedayet \|\| 57 \|\|*

*upānadyagalaṃ chatraṃ dānaṃ dadyācca bhaktimān \|*  
*namaste bhaganetraghna pūṣṇo daśananāśana \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. A bath with Amalaka water and worship by offering mandara flower should be done in the month of Jyestha. Dhupa and naivedya of curd mixed sattu and ghee should then be offered to Trinetra for prosperity in future. One should give in daksina an umbrella and a pair of shoes with chanting- "O Bhagnetraghna and splitter of Pusnas teeth, I salute you” for the pleasure of the ruler of this universe.

## \|\| 16.59-60 \|\|

*idamuccārayedbhaktyā prīṇanāya jagatpateḥ \|*  
*āṣāḍhe snānamuditaṃ śrīphalairarcanaṃ tathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*dhattūrakusumaiḥ śuklairdhūpayet silhakaṃ tathā \|*  
*naivedyāḥ saghṛtāḥ pūpāḥ dakṣiṇā saghṛtā yavāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. One should give a bath with Srlphala water and do worship with the white flowers of thorn apple (plant) in the month of Asadha. Dhupa of silhaka and naivedya of Pupa mixed ghee should then be offered. Daksina of ghee mixed barley should then be offered with chanting loudly- "O destroyer of Daksa-yanja, I salute you."

## \|\| 16.61-64 \|\|

*namaste dakṣayajñaghna idamuccairudīrayet \|*  
*śrāvaṇe mṛgabhojyena snānaṃ kṛtvār'cayeddharam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*śrīvṛkṣapatraḥ saphalairdhūpaṃ dadyāt tathāgurum \|*  
*naivedyaṃ saghṛtaṃ dadyāt dadhi pūpān samodakān \|\| 62 \|\|*

*dadhyodanaṃ sakṛsaraṃ māṣadhānāḥ saśaṣkulīḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ śvetavṛṣabhaṃ dhenuṃ ca kapilāṃ śubhām \|\| 63 \|\|*

*kanakaṃ rakkavasanaṃ pradadyād brāhmaṇāya hi \|*  
*gaṅgādhareti japtavyaṃ nāma śaṃbhośca paṇḍitaiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. A bath is to be given with pearl-immersed water (Mrgabhojya) and worship with bilvapatras and fruits should be made of Mahadeva. Dhupa of Aguru should be offered. Then Pupa cooked in ghee, modaka, curd, dadhyodana, pulse of urda, fried barley and kacanti should be offered as naivedya. The wise man subsequent to it should give daksina of a white bull, a kapila cow, gold and red coloured cloth in daksina and do japa of Sankara's name as Gangadhara.

## \|\| 16.65 \|\|

*amībhiḥ ṣaḍbhiraparairmāsaiḥ pāraṇamuttamam \|*  
*evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ saṃpūjya ṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*akṣayān labhate kāmān maheśvaravaco yathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Second Parana is done subsequent to these next six months. Thus,  a man attains to everlasting ambitions as stated by Mahesvara himself if worshipped Vrsabhadhvaja for a year.

## \|\| 16.66 \|\|

*idamuktaṃ vrataṃ puṇyaṃ sarvākṣayakaraṃ śubham \|*  
*svayaṃ rudraṇa devarṣe tattathā na tadanyathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О divine hermit! This fast sacrosanct and worth fulfilling all desires has been stated by Rudra himself. It is the same as stated by him. It cannot be even imagined that it shall be otherwise.

## Chapter 17. Description of the birth of Mahisasura

## \|\| 17.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*māsi cāśvayuje brahman yadā padmaṃ jagatpateḥ \|*  
*nābhyā niryāti hi tadā deveṣvetānyatho 'bhavan \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Pulastya said- О Brahmin! with generation of lotus from the navel of lord Visnu the following things originated from the other gods.

## \|\| 17.2 \|\|

*kandarpasya karāgre tu kadambaścārudarśanaḥ \|*  
*tena tasya parā prītiḥ kadambena vivarddhate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A beautiful Kadamba originated on the fore portion of Kamadeva's hand. This is the reason, why he is pleased when Kadamba flower is offered.

## \|\| 17.3 \|\|

*yakṣāṇāmadhipasyāpi maṇibhadrasya nārada \|*  
*vaṭavṛkṣaḥ samabhavat tasmistasya yatiḥ sadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Narada! A banyan tree originated from Manibhadra, the king of demi-gods (Yaksas). Hence, he has affection for the banyan tree.

## \|\| 17.4-5 \|\|

*maheśvarasya hṛdaye dhattūraviṭapaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*saṃjātaḥ sa ca śarvasya patikṛt tasya nityaśaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo madhyato dehāñjāto marakataprabhaḥ \|*  
*kha daraḥ kaṇṭakī śreyānabhavadviśvakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. As thorn apple plant was grown on the heart of Mahesvara; it is always a favourite of his Khadira like Marakatamani originated from the middle part of Brahma's body and beautiful Kantaki tree originated from the body of Visvakarma.

## \|\| 17.6 \|\|

*girijāyāḥ karatale kundasulmastvajāyata \|*  
*gaṇādhipasya kumbhastho rājate sindhuvārakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Kunda's creeper was grown on the palm of Parvati and Sindhuvaraka tree existed in the Kumbha region of Ganapati.

## \|\| 17.7 \|\|

*yamasya kṣiṇe pārśve pālāśo dakṣiṇottare \|*  
*kṛṣṇodumbarako rudrājjātaḥ kṣomakaro vṛṣaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Palasa and Krsna Udumbara tree originated in the right and upside right (daksinottara) collateral parts of the body. Udvejaka-vrksa (vasaka adusa) originated from Rudra.

## \|\| 17.8 \|\|

*skandasya bandhujīvastu raveraśvattha eva ca \|*  
*kātyāyanayāḥ śamījātābilvo lakṣmāyāḥ kare 'bhavat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Bandhujiva from Skanda, Asvatha (pipala) from sun, Sami from Katyayani and Bela tree was grown on the hand of Laksmi.

## \|\| 17.9 \|\|

*nāgānāṃ pataye brahmañcharastambo vyajāyata \|*  
*vāsukervistṛte pucche pṛṣṭhe dūrvā sitāsitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О Brahmin! Sarastamba (sarapata) originated from the king serpent (sesa) and white dark Durva was grown on the broad tail and back of Vasuki.

## \|\| 17.10 \|\|

*sādhyānāṃ hṛdaye jāto vṛkṣo haritacandanaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ jāteṣu sarveṣu tena tat ratirbhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A tree of Harita candana originated in the heart of Sadhyas. Having so originated the above trees and creepers, the gods concerned do grace on devotees when they are so worshipped.

## \|\| 17.11 \|\|

*tatra ramye śubhe kāle yā śuklaikādaśī bhavet \|*  
*tasyāṃ saṃpūjayed viṣṇuṃ tena khaṇḍo 'sya pūryate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One should do worship of lord Visnu on Sukla Ekadasi that fall in that auspicious part of the period. It fulfils the inchoate desire of any kind during this period.

## \|\| 17.12 \|\|

*puṣṣaiḥ putraiḥ phalairvāpi gandhavarṇarasnvitaiḥ \|*  
*oṣadhībhiśca mukhyābhiryāvatsyāccharadāgamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. One should worship lord Visnu during thepleasant season (Sarada Rtu) which knocks by offering leaves, flowers and fruits of different fragrance, colour and essence (juice) as also the prime medicines.

## \|\| 17.13-15 \|\|

*ghṛtaṃ tilā brīhiyavā hiraṇyakankādi yat \|*  
*maṇimuktāpravālāni vastrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rasāni svādukaṭvamlakaṣāyalavaṇāni ca \|*  
*tiktāni ca nivedyāni tānyakhaṇḍāni yāni hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tatpūjārthaṃ pradātavyaṃ keśavāya mahātmane \|*  
*yadā saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇamakhaṇḍaṃ bhavate gṛhe \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Не should offer ghee, sesamum, vrihi, barley, silver, gold, gem, pearl, coral, different kind clothes and things having bitter, salty, pungent, sour, astringent tastes regularly for the worship of lord Kesava. The home of such a devotee avails of the perfection with all prosperity when worship with this procedure is made for a year.

## \|\| 17.16 \|\|

*kṛtopavāso devarṣe dvitīye 'hani saṃyataḥ \|*  
*snānena tena snāyīta yenākhaṇḍaṃ hi vatsaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О divine hermit! He should observe fast and take a bath on the following day with due control over senses so that such a worship may run undisturbed throughout the year.

## \|\| 17.17 \|\|

*siddhārtakaistilairvāpi tenaivodvartanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*haviṣā padmanābhasya snānameva samācaret \|*  
*home tadeva gaditaṃ dāne śaktirnijā dvija \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There is a provision of massage with white mustard or sesamum oil. Padmanabha should be given a bath with ghee. О Brahmin! ghee should be used for havana and donation, as per capacity of the devotee, provided.

## \|\| 17.18 \|\|

*pūjayetātha kusumaiḥ pādādārabhya keśavam \|*  
*dhūpayed vividhaṃ dhūpaṃ yena syād vatsaraṃ param \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Kesava should then be worshipped from feet to the head and offer dhupa of niunerous kinds. There should be no shortage in offering throughout the year (samvatsara).

## \|\| 17.19 \|\|

*hiraṇyaratnavāsobhiḥ pūjayeta jagad gurum \|*  
*rāgakhāṇḍavacoṣyāṇi haviṣyāṇi nivedayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He should worship Jagadguru with gold, gems and garments and offer Raga-khandva (special sweet), cosya and oblations (havisya) as naivedya.

## \|\| 17.20 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ padmanābhaṃ jagad gurum \|*  
*vijñāpayenmuniśreṣṭha mantreṇānena suvrata \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О great resolute! О great hermit! One should do prayer to Padmanabha (Visnu) subsequent to worship of him.

## \|\| 17.21 \|\|

*namo 'stu te padmanābha padmādhava mahādyute \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣaṇi tvakhaṇḍāni bhavantu me \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О resolute of husband of Laksmi! О great lord! Salute to you. May our Dharma, Artha Kama and Moksa be complete and undisturbed.

## \|\| 17.22 \|\|

*vikāsipadmapatrākṣa yathākhaṇḍosi sarvataḥ \|*  
*tena satyena dharmādya akhaṇḍāḥ santu keśava \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О blossomed lotus eyed! As you are perfect with all respects, my religion etc. should receive perfection by virtue of that truth.

## \|\| 17.23 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ sopavāso jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*aghaṇḍaṃ pārayed brahman vrataṃ vai sarvavastuṣu \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Brahmin! One should so observe fast throughout the year with due control over the senses and by offering all things to god regularly.

## \|\| 17.24 \|\|

*asmiṃścīrṇe vrataṃ vyaktaṃ parituṣyanti devatāḥ \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣādyāstvakṣayāḥ saṃbhavanti hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The gods definitely are pleased as a result of observing this fast and the four industries (viz. Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksa) of the devotee meet to perfection.

## \|\| 17.25 \|\|

*etāni te mayoktāni vratānyuktāni kāmibhiḥ \|*  
*prakṣyāmyadhunā tvetadvaiṣṇavaṃ pañjaraṃ śubham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I have thus described these fasts to be observed by Kami (desirous) people. I will now describe this Vaisnava Panjara all benevolent for human-beings.

## \|\| 17.26 \|\|

*namo namaste govinda cakraṃ gṛhya sudarśanam \|*  
*prācyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo tvāmāhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О Govind! I salute you. О Visnu! Please defend me at east with Sudarsan discus in your hands. I am sheltered under you.

## \|\| 17.27 \|\|

*gadāṃ kaumodakīṃ gṛhya padmanābhāmitadyute \|*  
*yāmyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo tvamāhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О unique in splendour! О Padmanabha! defend me at south with Kaumodaki mace in your hand. О Visnu! I am sheltered under you.

## \|\| 17.28 \|\|

*halamādāya saunandaṃ namaste puraṣottama \|*  
*pratīcyāṃ rakṣa me viṣṇo bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О the best Purusa! I salute you. Defend me at west with Saunanda plough in your hand. О Visnu! I have come in your sole shelter.

## \|\| 17.29 \|\|

*musalaṃ śātanaṃ gṛhya puṇḍarīkākṣa rakṣa māma \|*  
*uttarasyāṃ jagannātha bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О Pundarikaksa! Defend me at north with your destructive musala. О ruler of this universe! I have come to your shelter.

## \|\| 17.30 \|\|

*śārṅgamādāya ca dhanurastraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ hare \|*  
*namaste rakṣa rakṣaghna aiśānyāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О Hari! Defend me at Isana angle. О great defender! I salute you. I have come under your shelter.

## \|\| 17.31 \|\|

*pāñcajanyaṃ mahāśaṅkhamantarbodhyaṃ ca paṅkajam \|*  
*pragṛhay rakṣa māṃ viṣṇo āgneyyāṃ yajñasūkara \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. О yajnasukara Visnu! Ensure my defence at Agnikona with the great conch-shell Pancajanya and conscience giver lotus.

## \|\| 17.32 \|\|

*carma sūryaśataṃ gṛhya khaṅgaṃ candramasaṃ tathā \|*  
*nairṛtyāṃ māṃ ca rakṣasva divyamūrte nṛkesarin \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. О divine feature Nrsimha! Ensure my defence at Nairtya angle with Suryasata shield and Candramasa sword.

## \|\| 17.33 \|\|

*vaijayantīṃ pragṛhya tvaṃ śrīvatsaṃ kaṇṭhabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*vāyavyāṃ rakṣa māṃ deva aśvaśīrṣa namo 'stu te \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О Asvasirsa god! Ensure my defence at Vayavya angle with Vaijayanti garland mid Srivatsa ornament around your throat. I salute you.

## \|\| 17.34 \|\|

*vainateyaṃ samāruhya antarikṣe janārdana \|*  
*māṃ tvaṃ rakṣājita sadā namaste tvaparājati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О victorious Janardana! Ensure my defence at the space of riding on Vainateya (garuda). О undefeated! I salute you always.

## \|\| 17.35 \|\|

*viśālākṣaṃ samāruhya rakṣa māṃ tvaṃ rasātale \|*  
*akūpāra namastubhyaṃ mahāmoha namo 'stu te \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. О Akupara (great tortoise) ensure my defence at Rasatala by riding on huge-eyed Garuda. О Mahamoha! Salute to you.

## \|\| 17.36 \|\|

*karaśīrṣāṅghrarveṣu tathāṣṭabāhupañjaram \|*  
*kṛtvā rakṣasva māṃ deva namaste puruṣottama \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О Purusottama! Defend me by Astapanjara in hands, head and joints etc. О god! Salute to you.

## \|\| 17.37-38 \|\|

*etaduktaṃ bhagavatā vaiṣṇavaṃ pañjaraṃ mahat \|*  
*purā rakṣārthamīśena kātyāyanyā dvijottama \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nāśayāmāsa sā yatra dānavaṃ mahiṣāsuram \|*  
*namaraṃ raktabījaṃ ca tathānyān surakaṇṭakān \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. О great Brahmin! Lord Sankara (Isa) had chanted this Vaisnava Panjara for the defence of Katyayani where she had killed Mahisasura, Namara, Raktabija and many other enemies of gods.

## \|\| 17.39 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kāsau kātyāyānī nāma yacā jaghne mahiṣāsuram \|*  
*namaraṃ raktabījaṃ ca tathānyān kurakaṇṭakān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Narada asked- "Who is Katyayani named by you as the killer of Mahisasura, Raktabija and many other enemies of gods?"

## \|\| 17.40 \|\|

*kaścasau mahiṣo nāma kule jātaśca kasya saḥ \|*  
*kaścāsau raktabījākhyo namaraḥ kasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*etadvistaratastāta yathāvad vaktumarhasiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О lord! Who is that Mahisa and how was his family (clan) known? Who is Raktabija and who is the father of Namara? Please, highlight your answer as before on this query.

## \|\| 17.41 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca\|*  
*śrūyatāṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*sarvadā varadā durgā yeyaṃ kātyāyanī mune \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Pulastya said- "I herewith explain the story capable to absolve sons. Please, listen to it. О hermit! Durga the great goddess is Katyayani and not any other.

## \|\| 17.42 \|\|

*purāsuravarau raudrau jagatkṣobhakarāvubhau \|*  
*rambhaścaiva karambhaś ca dvāvāstāṃ sumābalau \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. During the ancient period, there were two dreadful coercive forces to whole world and mighty demon called Rambha and Karambha.

## \|\| 17.43 \|\|

*tāvaputrau ca devarṣe putrārthaṃ tepatustapaḥ \|*  
*bahūn varṣagaṇān daityau sthitau pañcanade jale \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О divine hermit! Those issueless daityas observed penance for several years standing in the water of Pancanada (five rivers) in order to be blessed with a son.

## \|\| 17.44 \|\|

*tatraiko jalamadhyastho dvitīyo 'pyagnipañcamī \|*  
*karambhaścaiva rambhaśca yakṣaṃ mālapaṭaṃ prati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Karambha and Rambha were engrossed in their effort to please Malavata Yaksa. One stood in water while the other was seated amid the fire blazed from fire sides (Pancagni).

## \|\| 17.45 \|\|

*ekaṃ mimagnaṃ salile grāharūpeṇa vāsavaḥ \|*  
*caraṇābhyāṃ samādāya nijaghāna yathecchayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Indra came in disguise as a crocodile, pulled the one standing stood in the water by foot and killed him under such plan.

## \|\| 17.46 \|\|

*tato bhrātari naṣṭe ca rambhaḥ kopapariplutaḥ \|*  
*vahnau svaśīrṣaṃ saṃkṣidya hotumaiccan mahābalaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Rambha was filled with anger when he saw that his brother is dead and prepared to cut his head and throw it into fire.

## \|\| 17.47-48 \|\|

*tataḥ pragṛhya keśeṣu khaṅgaṃ ca ravisaprabham \|*  
*chettukāmo nijaṃ śīrṣaṃ vahninā pratiṣedhitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*uktaśca mā daityavara nāśayātmānamātmanā \|*  
*dustarā paravadhyāpi svavadhyāpyatidustarā \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The fire restricted the demon (Rambha) who had caught his hair in one hand and the sword as radiant as the sun in the other lifted to cut his head. Agni said- О great demon! Don’t kill you yourself because suicide is a heinous sin and bigger than killing another person.

## \|\| 17.49 \|\|

*yacca prārthayase vīra taddadāmi yathepsitam \|*  
*mā mriyasva mṛtasyeha naṣṭā bhavati vai kathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. О chivalrous! Ask me what you want. Don’t commit suicide because the man so dead leaves no record/account behind him. I will fulfil your desire.

## \|\| 17.50 \|\|

*tato 'bravīd vaco rambho varaṃ cenme dadāsi hi \|*  
*trailokyavijayī putraḥ syānme tvattejasādhikaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Rambha stopped and requested- "If you really are so pleased as to fulfil my desire, I ask for a son having more valour than you and could conquer the three-worlds.

## \|\| 17.51 \|\|

*ajeyo daivataiḥ sarvaiḥ pubhirdaityaiśca pāvaka \|*  
*mahābalo vāyuriva kāmarūpī kṛtāstravit \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О Pavaka! May he be invincible by all gods, human-beings and daityas. He should be mighty as the wind, industries and expert in the handling of all weapons and arms.

## \|\| 17.52 \|\|

*taṃ provāca kavirbrahman bāñamevaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yasyāṃ cittaṃ samālambi kariṣyasi tataḥ sutaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. О Brahmin! The fire then replied- "very well. This will be as you desired. You will get such a son of particular characteristics from a woman subjected to your intercourse and love.

## \|\| 17.53 \|\|

*ityevamukto devena vahninā dānavo yayau \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ mālavaṭaṃ yakṣaṃ yakṣaiśca parivāritam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. With this assurance of fire god, Rambha went to see Malavata Yaksa surrounded by the Yaksas.

## \|\| 17.54 \|\|

*teṣāṃ padmanidhistatra vasate nānyacetanaḥ \|*  
*gajaśca mahiṣāścāśvā gāvo 'jāvipariplutāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Nidhi of those Yaksas was called Padma and he used to live there with concentration of mind. There were goats, sheep, horses, buffaloes, elephants and cows in abundance.

## \|\| 17.55 \|\|

*tān dṛṣṭvaiva tadā cakre bhāvaṃ dānavapārthivaḥ \|*  
*mahiṣyāṃ rūpayuktāyāṃ trihāyaṇyāṃ tapodhana \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О great austere man! The demon king was attracted to the beauty of a three year old feminine buffalo (viz. he became sensuous to do intercourse).

## \|\| 17.56 \|\|

*sā samāgācca daityaindraṃ kāmayantī tarasvinī \|*  
*sa cāpi gamanaṃ cakre bhavitavyapracoditaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. That feminine buffalo was also filled with appeal and immediately came to the demon. As preponderance is always attached with the future events, Rambha did intercourse with that buffalo.

## \|\| 17.57 \|\|

*tasyāṃ samabhavad garbhastāṃ pragṛhyātha dānavaḥ \|*  
*pātālaṃ praviveśātha tataḥ svabhavanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. That feminine buffalo became pregnant. He took her, entered into the nether world and then reached his residence.

## \|\| 17.58 \|\|

*dṛṣṭaśca dānavaiḥ sarvaiḥ parityaktaśca bandhubhiḥ \|*  
*akāryakāraketyevaṃ bhṛyo mālavaṭaṃ gataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. His siblings and other kith and kin declared him as corrupt and he was then ousted. He, therefore, went again to the Yaksa Malavata.

## \|\| 17.59 \|\|

*sāpi tenaiva patinā mahiṣī cārudarśanā \|*  
*samaṃ jagāma tat puṇyaṃ yakṣamaṇḍalamuttamam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. That beautiful buffalo too went with her husband at that sacred and best commune of Yaksa.

## \|\| 17.60 \|\|

*tatastu vasatastasya śyāmā sā suṣuve mune \|*  
*ajījanat sutaṃ śubhraṃ mahiṣaṃ kāmarūpiṇam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. О hermit! During shelter there, that buffalo had delivered a baby-buffalo competent to change his body features at will.

## \|\| 17.61 \|\|

*etāmṛtumatīṃ jātāṃ mahiṣo 'nyo dadarśa ha \|*  
*sā cābhyagād ditivaraṃ rakṣantī śīlamātmanaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. When that buffalo again got the reproduction time, any other buffalo seeing her rushed to her for intercourse. She anyhow defended her chastity and care to the demon.

## \|\| 17.62 \|\|

*tamunnāmitanāsaṃ ca mahiṣaṃ vīkṣya dānavaḥ \|*  
*khaṅga niṣkṛṣya tarasā mahiṣaṃ samupādravat \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. When that demon saw another buffalo chasing his beloved by lifting up his nose, he took out a sword and blew it hard on him.

## \|\| 17.63 \|\|

*tenāpi daityastīkṣṇābhyāṃ śṛṅgābhyāṃ hṛdi tāḍitaḥ \|*  
*nirbhinnahṛdayo bhūmau nipapāta mamāra ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. That buffalo too hit at the heart of demon by his pointed horns. It pierced the heart of demon and he fell down dead.

## \|\| 17.64 \|\|

*mṛte bhartari sā śyāmā yakṣāṇāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatā \|*  
*rakṣitā guhyakaiḥ sādhvī nivārya mahiṣaṃ tataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. That buffalo (she) on the death of her husband sheltered herself under Yaksas for protection. Guhyakas at last drove that buffalo away and defended that chaste feminine buffalo.

## \|\| 17.65 \|\|

*tato nivārito yakṣairhayārirmadanāturaḥ \|*  
*nipapāta saro divyaṃ tato daityai'bhavanmṛtaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The buffalo (so sensuous) fell down in a divine reservoir when Yaksas gave him sharp blows. On his death, there appeared a daitya from his body.

## \|\| 17.66 \|\|

*namaro nāma vikhyāto mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*yakṣānāśritya tasthau sa kālayan śvāpadān mun \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О hermit! That daitya began to live with Yaksas and he used to kill the wild animals. This mighty and valorous daitya was later known as Namara.

## \|\| 17.67 \|\|

*sa ca daityeśvaro yakṣairmālavaṭapurassaraiḥ \|*  
*citāmāropitaḥ sā ca śyāmā taṃ cāruhat patim \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Malavata etc. Yaksas then put that demon king on pyre for funeral. The feminine buffalo too sat on pyre with her husband and thus, both of them were burnt into ashes.

## \|\| 17.68 \|\|

*tato 'gnimadhyāduttasthau puruṣo raudradarśanaḥ \|*  
*vyadrāvayat sa tān yakṣān khaṅgapāṇirbhayaṅkaraḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. No sooner there appeared a dreadful and huge Purusa from the pyre so blazed. He drove all Yaksas.

## \|\| 17.69 \|\|

*tato hatāstu mahiṣāḥ sarva eva mahātmanā \|*  
*ṛte saṃrakṣitāraṃ hi mahiṣaṃ rambhanandanam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. He then killed all buffaloes except the son of Rambha (who was also a buffalo in physic).

## \|\| 17.70 \|\|

*sa nāmataḥ smṛto daityo raktabījo mahāmun \|*  
*yo 'jayat sarvato devān sendrarudrārkamārutān \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. О great hermit! That demon became famous as Raktabija later on. He subjugated all gods including Indra, Rudra, sun and Maruta etc.

## \|\| 17.71 \|\|

*evaṃ prabhāvā danupuṅgavāste tejo 'dhikastatra babhau hayāriḥ \|*  
*rājye 'bhiṣiktaśca mahāsurendrairvinirjitaiḥ śambaratārakādyaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. All those demons were so influential yet Hayari (buffalo) was the supreme, valorous. He subjugated Sambara, Тaгака etc. chivalrous monsters. They all then enthroned him.

## \|\| 17.72 \|\|

*aśaknuvadbhiḥ sahitaiśca devaiḥ salokapālaiḥ sahutāśabhāskaraiḥ \|*  
*sthānāni tyaktāni śaśīndrabhāskarairdharmaśca dūre pratiyojitaśca \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. When he could not be defeated by joint efforts of fire, sun etc. gods including lokapalas, the moon and sun had vacated their respective orbits and the religion (dharma) was also thrown away from his territory.

## Chapter 18. Description of Greatness of Goddess

## \|\| 18.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tatastu devā mahiṣema nirjitāḥ sthānāni saṃtyajya savāhanāyudhāḥ \|*  
*jagmuḥ puraskṛtya ricāmahaṃ te draṣṭuṃ tadā cakradharaṃ śriyaḥ patim \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Pulastya said- The gods defeated by Mahisa left their respective places and appeared before Laksmipati (Sri Visnu) under lead of lord Brahma with their respective carriers (vahanas) and weapons.

## \|\| 18.2 \|\|

*gatvā tvapaśyaṃśca mithaḥ surottamau sthitau khagendrāsanaśaṅkarau hi \|*  
*dṛṣṭāvā praṇamyaiva ca siddisādhakau nyavedayaṃstanmahiṣādiceṣṭitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. They saw there lord Visnu and Sankara seated together. They saluted them and described the heinous acts being committed by Mahisa etc. demons.

## \|\| 18.3 \|\|

*prabho 'śvisūryendvanilāgnivedhasāṃ jaleśaśakrādiṣu cādhikārān \|*  
*ākramya nākāttu nirākṛtā vayaṃ kṛtāvanisthā mahiṣāsureṇa \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. (They said) О sovereign gods! The demon Mahisa has confiscated the rights of Asvinikumaras, sun, moon, wind, fire, Brahma, Varuna, Indra etc. gods and expelled us all from the heaven. We are all compelled to live on the earth.

## \|\| 18.4 \|\|

*etad bhavantau śaraṇāgatānāṃ śrutvā vaco brūta hitaṃ surāṇām \|*  
*na ced vrajāmo 'dya rasātalaṃ hi saṃkālyamānā yudhi dānavena \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. We request you both for delivering a suitable suggestion as we are now sheltered by you and reported the matter completely. In case you give no care to us, we all cruelly beaten in battle by that demon will descend to the nether world immediately and just today itself.

## \|\| 18.5 \|\|

*itthaṃ murāriḥ saha śaṅkareṇa śrutvā vaco viplutacetasastān \|*  
*dṛṣṭvātha cakre sahasaiva kopaṃ kālāgnikalpo hariravyayātmā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Murari with Sankara heard their report and the determination and saw that they were very anxious and in gloom. Avyayatma Hari then was filled with anger. His face was blazing like Kalagni.

## \|\| 18.6 \|\|

*tato 'nukopānmadhusūdanasya saśaṅkarasyāpi pitāmahasya \|*  
*tathaiva śakrādiṣu daivateṣu maharddhi tejo vadanād viniḥsutam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. As a result of anger built up in the minds of Madhusudana, Sankara, Pitamaha and Indra etc. gods, rays came out from their mouths.

## \|\| 18.7 \|\|

*taccaikatāṃ parvatakūṭasannibhaṃ jagāma tejaḥ pravarāśram mune \|*  
*kātyāyanasyāpratimasya tena maharṣiṇā teja upākṛtaṃ ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О hermit! That splendour (ray) was crystallised like the ridge of a mountain in the asrama of Katyayana hermit. That hermit processed (upabrhana) that splendour.

## \|\| 18.8 \|\|

*tenārṣisṛṣṭena ca teja-sā vṛtaṃ jvalatprakāśārkasahasratulyam \|*  
*tasmācca jātā taralāyatākṣī kātyāyanī yogaviśuddhadehā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The crystallised splendour of all gods and duly processed start glowing like several thousand suns. Such combination of splendour gave birth to caprice and to a huge-eyed and purified body, a goddess called Katyayani.

## \|\| 18.9 \|\|

*māheśvarād vaktramatho babhūva netratrayaṃ pāvakatejasā ca \|*  
*yāmyena keśā haritejasā ca bhujāstathāṣṭādaśa saṃpjajñire \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The furious splendour of Mahesvara framed her mouth, the splendour of fire fixed her three eyes, the splendour of Yama originated her hair and the splendour of Hari originated her eighteen arms.

## \|\| 18.10 \|\|

*saumyena yugmaṃ stanayoḥ susaṃhataṃ madhyaṃ tathaindreṇa ca tejasābhavat \|*  
*ūraba cajaṅghe ca nitambasaṃyute jāte jaleśasya tu tejasā hi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The splendour of moon originated her compact breast, the splendour of Indra originated her loin and the splendour of Varuna originated her thighs, pubic regions and legs.

## \|\| 18.11 \|\|

*pādo ca lokaprapitāmahasya padmābhikośapratimau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*divākarāṇamapi tejasāṅgulīḥ karāṅgulīśca vasutejasaiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The splendour of Brahma (lokapitamaha) originated her two feet analogous to lotus petals, toes on feet by the splendour of Aditya and hand fingers originated by the splendour of Vasus.

## \|\| 18.12 \|\|

*prajāpatīnāṃ daśanāśca tejasā yākṣeṇa nāsā śravaṇau ca mārutāt \|*  
*sādhyena ca bhrayugalaṃ sukāntimat kandarpabāṇāsanasannibhaṃ babhau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Her teeth were originated by the splendour of Prajapati, nose by the splendour of Yaksas, both ears by the splendour of the wind and both her brows like the Kamadeva's bow were originated by the splendour of Sadhya.

## \|\| 18.13 \|\|

*tarthārṣitejottamamuttamaṃ mahannāmnā pṛthivyāmabhavat prasiddham \|*  
*kātyāyanītyeva tadā babhau sā nāmnā ca tenaiva jagatprasiddhā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The great and supreme splendour of hermit was popularly known as Katyayani and the goddess so originated became famous in this universe with the same name viz. Katyayani.

## \|\| 18.14 \|\|

*dadau triśūlaṃ varadastriśūlī cakraṃ murārirvaruṇaśca śaṅkham \|*  
*śaktiṃ hutāśaḥ śvasanaśca cāpaṃ tūṇau tathākṣyyaśarau vivasvān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Trisuli gave her a trident, Murari gave a discus, Varuna gave a conch, fire gave a sakti, wind gave a bow and surya gave two arrow- stands (tunira) with the undepleting stock of arrows.

## \|\| 18.15 \|\|

*vajraṃ tathendraḥ saha ghaṇṭayā ca yamo 'tha daṇḍaṃ dhanado gadāṃ ca \|*  
*brahma'kṣamālāṃ sakamaṇḍaluṃ ca kālo 'simugraṃ saha carmaṇā ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Indra gave a thunderbolt with a gong, Yama gave a danda, Kubera gave a mace, Brahma gave a kamandala with basil garland and Kala a gave shield with a sharp edged sword.

## \|\| 18.16 \|\|

*hāraṃ ca somaḥ saha cāmareṇa mālaṃ samudro himavān mṛgendram \|*  
*cūḍāmaṇiṃ kuṇḍalamarddhacandraṃ prādāt kuṭhāraṃ vasuśilpakarttā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The moon gave a garland with camara, the ocean gave a garland, Himalaya gave a lion, Visvakarma gave a cudamani, kundala and an axe.

## \|\| 18.17 \|\|

*gandharvarājo rajatānuliptaṃ pānasya pūrṇaṃ sadṛśaṃ ca bhājanam \|*  
*bhujaṅgahāraṃ bhujageśvaro 'pi amlānapuṣpāmṛtavaḥ srajaṃ ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The king of Gandharva gave a silver vessel used for liquor sipping, the king of serpent gave a garland of serpents and the seasons gave an unfading flower garland.

## \|\| 18.18 \|\|

*tadātituṣṭā surasttamānāṃ aṭṭāṭṭahāsaṃ mumuce trinetrā \|*  
*tāṃ tuṣṭuvurdevavarāḥ sahendrāḥ saviṣṇurudrendvanilāgnibhāskarāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The three eyed (Katyayani) then was pleased with the gods and made a peal of laughter. The prominent gods like Indra, Visnu, Rudra, moon, wind, fire and sun etc. began to pray to her.

## \|\| 18.19-20 \|\|

*namo 'stu daivyai surapūjitāyai yā saṃsthitā yogaviśuddhadehā \|*  
*nidrāsvarūpeṇa mahīṃ vitatya tṛṣṇā trapā kṣud bhayadātha kāntiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śraddhā smṛtiḥ puṣṭiratho kṣamā ca chāyā ca śaktiḥ kamalālayā ca \|*  
*vṛttirdayā bhrānti ratheha māyā namo 'stu daivyai bhavarūpikāyai \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Salute to the goddess having a pure body with a combination (yoga). She is present everywhere on the earth in the form of sleep. She is temptation, trapa, hunger, fear, gleam, obeisance, memory, health, forgiveness, shade, power, wealth, profession, kindness, illusion and fallacy. Such a goddess in the form of universe is saluted.

## \|\| 18.21 \|\|

*tataḥ stutāḥ devavarairmṛgendramāruhya devī pragatāvanīdhram \|*  
*vindhyaṃ mahāparvatamuccaśṛṅgaṃ cakāra yaṃ nimnataraṃ tvagastyaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The goddess so prayed to gods then rode on a lion and went to the Vindhya mountain having highest peaks which once was restricted from ascending more.

## \|\| 18.22 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kirmathamadriṃ bhagavānagastyastaṃ nimnaśṛṅgaṃ kṛtavān maharṣiḥ \|*  
*kasmai kṛte kena ca kāraṇena etad vadasvāmalasattvavṛtte \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Narada asked- О sacrosanct soul! Please tell us for what reason and purpose hermit Agastya had restricted the ascending peaks of that mountain?

## \|\| 18.23 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*purā hi vindhyena divākarasya gatirniruddhā gaganecarasya \|*  
*ravistataḥ kumabhabhavaṃ sametya homāvasāne vacanaṃ babhāṣe \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Pulastya said- The Vindhya had created a hurdle for the usual movement of sun god long-long ago. This became the cause of pain for sun and he went before the renowned hermit Agastya, saluted him and then requested.

## \|\| 18.24 \|\|

*samāgato 'haṃ dvija dūratastvāṃ kuruṣva māmuddharaṇaṃ munīndra \|*  
*dadasva dānaṃ mama yanmanīṣinaṃ carāmi yena tridiveṣu nirvṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О Dvija! I have come to you from a distant place. О king of hermits! rescue me. Endow me with the desired thing so that I could move in the sky without the least worry.

## \|\| 18.25 \|\|

*itthaṃ divākaravaco guṇasaṃprayogi śrutvā tadā kalaśajo vacanaṃ babhāṣe \|*  
*dānaṃ dadāmi tava yanmanasastvabhīṣṭaṃ nārthi prayāti vimukho mama kaścideva \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Having heard this cryptic/witty request, Agastya said- "I will endow you with the desired thing as no donor returns empty handed from me."

## \|\| 18.26 \|\|

*śrutvā vaco 'mṛtamayaṃ kalaśodbhavasya prāha prabhuḥ karatale vinidhāya mūrdhni \|*  
*eṣo 'dya me girivaraḥ praruṇāddhi mārgaṃ vindhyasya nimnakaraṇe bhagavan yatasva \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This nectar-pouring assurance made the sun happy and he said with folded hand- "This mountain is restricting my route today. Hence, О lord! Do try to curtail the height of Vindhya."

## \|\| 18.27 \|\|

*iti ravivacanādathāha kumbhajanmā kutamiti viddhi mayā hi nīcaśṛṅgam \|*  
*tava kiraṇajito bhaviṣyate mahīdhro mama caraṇasamśritasya kā vyathā te \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Agastya, the pitcher-bom sage replied- "Deem that this mountain has gone down by me. It will be defeated by virtue of your rays. How can any pain pinch one who sheltered me?

## \|\| 18.28 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā kalaśodbhāvastu sūryaṃ hi saṃstūya vinamya bhaktyā \|*  
*jagāma saṃtyajya hi daṇḍakaṃ hi vindhyācalaṃ vṛddhvapurmaharṣiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. With these words the old Agastya worshipped god sun humbly and then set out to see Vindhya.

## \|\| 18.29 \|\|

*gatvā vacaḥ prāha munirmahīdhraṃ yāsye mahātīrthavaraṃ supuṇyam \|*  
*vṛddhosmayaśaktaśca tavādhiroḍhuṃ tasmād bhavān nīcataro 'stu sadyaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The hermit said to the mountain- "I am now going to see a holy place. I am unable to climb on your so high body due to old age. Hence, shrink your body down immediately for which I urge you.

## \|\| 18.30 \|\|

*ityevamukto munisttamena sa nīcaśṛṅgastvabhavanmahīdhraḥ \|*  
*samākramaccāpi maharṣimukyaḥ prollaṅghya vindhyaṃ tvidamāha śailam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The mountain accepted the prayer and contracted his body, his peaks lost height and the hermit then easily crossed it to go to the other side. He then said to the mountain.

## \|\| 18.31 \|\|

*yāvanna bhūyo nijamāvrajāmi mahāśramaṃ dhautavapuḥ sutīrthāt \|*  
*tvayā na tāvattviha vardhitavyaṃ no ced viśapsye 'hamavajñayā te \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Until I return from that holy place after a bath safely to my asrama, remain as you are this time. In case my instruction is violated, I will curse you for dare consequences.

## \|\| 18.32 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā bhagavāñjagāma diśaṃ sa yāmyāṃ sahasāntarikṣam \|*  
*ākramya tasthau sa hi tāṃ tadāśāṃ kāle vrajāmyatra yadā munīndraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. With these words, lord Agastya moved to the south in space immediately and he stopped there by saying- "I will come again at an appropriate time."

## \|\| 18.33 \|\|

## \|\| 20.13 \|\|

*samāgamya ca vegena devyāḥ śaktiṃ mumoca ha \|*  
*triśulamapi siṃhāya prāhiṇod dānavo raṇe \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The demon then gave a hard blow of sakti on goddess and tlirew a trident to finish the lion.

## \|\| 20.14 \|\|

*tāvāpatantau devyā tu huṅkāreṇātha bhasmasāt \|*  
*kṛtāvatha gajendreṇa gṛhīto madhyato hariḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The goddess made a loud voice, vomited fire from her mouth and burnt both the weapons immediately. The elephant than caught the lion just at his loin.

## \|\| 20.15 \|\|

*athotpatya ca vegena talenāhtaya dānavam \|*  
*gatāsuḥ suñjaraskandhāt kṣipya daivyai niveditaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. (The lion) leapt up suddenly, slapped the demon with his paw, dragged him down from the back of the elephant and put before the goddess his dead body.

## \|\| 20.16 \|\|

*gṛhītvā dānavaṃ madhye brahman kātyāyanī ruṣā \|*  
*savyena pāṇinā bhrāmya vādayat pahaṃ yathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Brahmin! The furious goddess caught the body of that demon from loin, started revolving round with her left hand and began beating him like a drum.

## \|\| 20.17 \|\|

*tato 'ṭṭahāsaṃ mumuce tādṛśe vādyatāṃ gate \|*  
*hāsyāt samudbhavaṃstasyā bhūtā nānāvidhādbhutāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. With the sound coming out by the beating, the goddess made a peal of laughter. Her fierce laugh originated a number of strange ghosts.

## \|\| 20.18 \|\|

*kecid vyāghramukhā raudrā vṛkākārāstathā pare \|*  
*hayāsyā mahiṣāsyāśca varāhavadanāḥ pare \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Some among them had tiger-like mouths, the complexion of some other was Vrka like, some had horse-like face, some other had buffalo like faces while the rest has pig like faces.

## \|\| 20.19 \|\|

*ākhukukkuṭavaktrāśca go 'jāvikamukhāstathā \|*  
*nānāvaktrākṣicaraṇā nānāyudhadharāstathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Some had faces of mouse, some other had faces of cock, cow, goat or sheep like. All of them had different faces, eyes and feet and equipped with numerous weapons.

## \|\| 20.20 \|\|

*gāyantyanye hasantyanye pamantyanye tu saṃghaśaḥ \|*  
*vādayantyapare tatra stuvantyanye tathāmbikām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A certain number of them began singing in groups, some others started laughing, some began moving in pleasure, some started playing musical instruments and some began praying to the goddess.

## \|\| 20.21 \|\|

*sā tairbhūtagaṇairdevī sārddha taddānavaṃ balam \|*  
*śātayāmāsa cākramya yathā sasyaṃ mahāśaniḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The goddess in the company of those ghosts made sharp attacks on the demon's army and killed it all as the thunderbolt destroys the entire crop.

## \|\| 20.22 \|\|

*senāgre nihate tasmin tathā senāgragāmini \|*  
*cikṣuraḥ sainyapālastu yodhayāmāsa devatāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When the front army and its commander were killed, another commander Ciksura began to fight against gods.

## \|\| 20.23 \|\|

*kārmukaṃ dṛḍhamākarṇamākṛṣya rathināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*vavarṣa śarajālāni yathā megho vasundharām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The best demon among the warriors rode on chariots, gave tension up to the ear to his bow and threw a volley of arrows the same way as the clouds rain on the earth.

## \|\| 20.24 \|\|

*tān durgā svaśaraiśchittvā śarasaṃghān suparvabhiḥ \|*  
*sauvarṇapuṅkhānaparāñśarān jagrāha ṣoḍaśa \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The goddess Durga cut-off that volley of arrows so thrown by her arrows with fantastic nodes and put another sixteen arrows having gold wings on her bow.

## \|\| 20.25 \|\|

*tataścaturbhiścaturasturaṅganapi bhāminī \|*  
*hatvā sārathimekena dhvajamekena cicchide \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Goddess Durga killed his four horses by throwing four arrows, his charioteer by an arrow and cut-off the flag by shooting another arrow.

## \|\| 20.26 \|\|

*tatastu saśaraṃ cāpaṃ cicchedaikeṣuṇāmbikā \|*  
*chinne dhanuṣu khaṅgaṃ ca carma cādattavān balī \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When the commander of the army was so dead, a dreadful monster Ugrasya and a demon Karalasya rushed to attack the goddess.

## \|\| 20.27 \|\|

*taṃ khaṅga carmaṇā sārdha daityasyādhunvato balāt \|*  
*śaraiścaturbhiściccheda tataḥ śūlaṃ samādade \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The demons Baskala, Uddhata, Ugrasya, Ugrakarmuka, Durdhara, Durmukha and Vidalanayana and several others then attacked simultaneously the goddess. All of them were well equipped with weapons and had well built bodies.

## \|\| 20.28 \|\|

*samudbhrāmya mahacchūlaṃ saṃprādravadathāmbikām \|*  
*kroṣṭuko mudito 'raṇye mṛgarājavadhūṃ yathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Ambika then cut-off his bow with arrow through an arrow. The chivalrous Ciksura picked up his sword and shield immediately when the bow and arrow were so cut-off.

## \|\| 20.29 \|\|

*tasyābhipatataḥ pādau karau śīrṣa ca pañcabhiḥ \|*  
*śaraiścicchada saṃkruddhā nyapatinnihato 'suraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The goddess threw four arrows and cut-off his sword with shield which he was waving to and fro. He then picked up Sula.

## \|\| 20.30 \|\|

*tasmin senāpatau kṣuṇṇe tadogrāsyo mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*samādravata vegena karālāsyaśca dānavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He rushed to Ambika by waving his Sula so lifted up. His movement appeared as if the fox runs a race toward the lioness when it feels exaggeratedly happy himself.

## \|\| 20.31-32 \|\|

*bāṣkalaścoddhataścaiva udagrākhyograkārmukaḥ \|*  
*durddharo durmukhaścaiva biḍālanayano 'paraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ete 'nye ca mahātmāno dānavā balināṃ varāḥ \|*  
*kātyāyanīmādravanta nānāśastrāstrapāṇayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. The goddess filled with anger, threw five arrows on that aggressor (demon), cut-off both his arms, feet and head from the body and (hus he fell down dead.

## \|\| 20.33 \|\|

*tān dṛṣṭvā līlayā durgā vīṇāṃ jagrāha pāṇinā \|*  
*vādayāmāsa hasatī tathā ḍamarukaṃ varam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Goddess Durga laughed at them when see saw them advancing took a lyre and damaru in her hands and began playing with them.

## \|\| 20.34 \|\|

*yathā yathā vādayate devī vādyāni tāni tu \|*  
*tathā tathā bhūtagaṇā nṛtyanti ca hasnti ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. With the sound of those musical instruments played by goddess Katyayani, the ghosts (Bhutaganas) in her company began dancing and merry-making.

## \|\| 20.35 \|\|

*tato 'surāḥ śastradharāḥ samabhyetya sarasvatīm \|*  
*abhyaghnaṃstāṃś ca jagrāha keśeṣu parameśvarī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The demons so equipped with weapons then started throwing them on Sarasvati when they reached nearer to her. The goddess caught them by the hair.

## \|\| 20.36 \|\|

*prahṛhya keśeṣu mahāsurāṃstān utpatya siṃhāttu nagasya sānum \|*  
*nanarta vīṇāṃ parivādayantī papau ca pānaṃ jagato janitrī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Having caught them by the hair, Katyayani jumped down from her lion, took them at a ridge of that mountain, piped the lyre and began sucking their blood.

## \|\| 20.37-38 \|\|

*tatastu devyā balino mahāsurā dordaṇḍanirdhūtaviśīrmadarpāḥ \|*  
*visrastavastrā vyasavaśca jātāḥ tatastu tān vīkṣya mahāsurendrān \|\| 37 \|\|*

*devyā mahaujā mahiṣāsurastu vyadrāvayad bhūtagaṇān khurāgraiḥ \|*  
*tuṇḍena pucchena tathorasānyān niḥśvāsavātena ca bhūtasaṃghān \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. The mighty and proud demons thus, lost both their apparels and lives. When Mahisasura saw such a dreadful end of his mighty commanders, he drove all ghosts away by hitting them with legs, horns, tail, chest and dreadful expiration through the nose.

## \|\| 20.39 \|\|

*nādena caivāśanisannibhena viṣāṇākoṭyā tvaparān pramathya \|*  
*dudrāva siṃhaṃ yudhi hantukāmaḥ tato 'mbakā krodhavaśaṃ jagāma \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He made a dreadful noise like a thunderbolt, hit hard with his horns the other soldiers (gods) fighting for goddess and rushed fast to kill the lion. This made Ambika more furious.

## \|\| 20.40 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kopādatha tīkṣṇaśṛṅgaḥ kṣipraṃ girīn bhūmimaśīrṇayacca \|*  
*saṃkṣobhayayayaṃstoyanidhīn ghanāṃś ca vidhvaṃsayan prādvatātha gurgām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Mahisa then began destroying the mountain and earth with his sharp horns as he was fiercely in furiated. He polluted even the water of the ocean and covered the clouds with the dust so blown. Thus, he immediately rushed towards goddess Durga.

## \|\| 20.41 \|\|

*sā cātha pāśena babandha duṣṭaṃ sa cāpyabhūt klinnakaṭaḥ karīndraḥ \|*  
*karaṃ praciccheda ca hastino 'graṃ sa cāpi bhṛyo mahiṣo 'bhijātaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He then fastened that wicked demon with Pasa. The demon by virtue of his supernatural powers then turned into an intoxicated elephant, dreadful in look and attack. The goddess immediately cut-off the fore portion of his trunk. He then turned into a buffalo again.

## \|\| 20.42 \|\|

*tato 'sya śūlaṃ vyasṛjanyamṛḍānī sa śīrṇamūlo nyapatat pṛthivyām \|*  
*śaktiṃ pracikṣepa hutāśadattāṃ sā kuṇṭhitāgrā nyapatanamārṣe \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О great hermit! Mrdani then threw Sula on him but it was split in parts and fell down on the ground. She then shot the sakti given by the fire god but that too lost its edge (viz. it could not act on the body of that demon).

## \|\| 20.43 \|\|

*cakraṃ harerdānapacakrahantuḥ kṣiptaṃ tvacakratvamupāgataṃ hi \|*  
*gadāṃ samāvidhya dhaneśvarasya kṣiptātu bhagnā nyapatat pṛthivyām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then the discus given by Hari was shot but it also proved null and void in spite of its magnificent power to kill all demons as it was seen earlier. The mace given by Kubera too was split and fell down on the ground when thrown at the monster.

## \|\| 20.44 \|\|

*jaleśapāśo 'pi mahāsureṇa viṣāṇatuṇḍāgrakhurapraṇunnaḥ \|*  
*nirasya tatkopitayā ca mukto daṇḍastu yāmyo bahukhaṇḍatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. That fierce monster made futile the attack made through Pasa given by Varuna by crushing it under feet, the fore limbs, teeth etc. The danda given by Yama was also split in several parts when it was used for the attack.

## \|\| 20.45 \|\|

*vajraṃ surendrasya ca vigrahe 'sya muktaṃ susūkṣmatvamupājagāma \|*  
*saṃtyajya siṃhaṃ mahiṣāsurasya durgādhirūḍhā sahasaiva pṛṣṭham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The thunderbolt given by Indra was also used in order to give a hard blow but was also split in several micro parts merely when it touched the body of Mahisasura. Durga then suddenly jumped down from the back of the lion and rode on the back of that monster.

## \|\| 20.46 \|\|

*pṛṣṭhasthitāyāṃ mahiṣāsuro 'pi poplūyate vīryamadānmṛḍānyām \|*  
*sā cāpi padbhyāṃ mṛdukomalābhyāṃ mamarda taṃ klinnamivājinaṃ hi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Mahisasura began to leap up frequently on account of having been proud of his power (virya) She also began churning his wet body with her delicate feet.

## \|\| 20.47 \|\|

*sa mṛdyamāno dharaṇīdharābho devyā balī hīnabalo babhūva \|*  
*tato 'sya śūlena bibeda kaṇṭhaṃ tasmāt pumān khaṅgadharo vinirgataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The giant body of that monster (Mahisasura) lost power soon as a result of so churning from feet by the goddess. At the same time, the goddess beheaded him with a blow made by Sula. A man with a sword in hand then appeared immediately from the beheaded body of that monster.

## \|\| 20.48 \|\|

*niṣkrāntamātraṃ hṛdaye padā tam āhatya saṃgṛhya kaceṣu kopāt \|*  
*śiraḥ praciccheda varāsināsya hāhākṛtaṃ daityabalaṃ tadābhūt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. No sooner had he appeared, than the goddess kicked at his chest region, caught his hair in grip and cut-off his head, immediately. The demon army began wailing on watching such a fierce scene.

## \|\| 20.49 \|\|

*sacaṇḍamuṇḍāḥ samayāḥ satārāḥ sahāsilomnā bhayakātarākṣāḥ \|*  
*saṃtāḍyamānāḥ pramathairbhavānyāḥ pātalamevāviviśurbhayārtāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Canda, Munda, Maya, Tara and Asiloma etc. mighty monsters were frightened badly and entered immediately into the nether world so as to save themselves from more thrashing by the goddess.

## \|\| 20.50 \|\|

*devyā jayaṃ devāgaṇā vilokya stuvanti devīṃ stutibhirmaharṣe \|*  
*nārāyaṇīṃ sarvajagatpratiṣṭhāṃ kātyāyanīṃ ghoramukhīṃ surūpām \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. О great hermit! The gods on seeing such a grand victory of goddess Katyayani, the fierce face, enchanting complexion, Narayani, sole cause for creation of entire universe, began praying to her with several hymns.

## \|\| 20.51 \|\|

*saṃstūyamānā surasiddhasaṃghairnniṣaṇṇabhūtā harapādamule \|*  
*bhūyo bhaviṣyāmyamarārthamevamuktvā surāṃstān praviveśa durgā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Goddess Durga who sits at the feet of lord 6iva, worshipped by gods and siddhas declared- "I will again appear for the cause of gods." With these words in declaration, that Durga suddenly vanished from there.

## Chapter 21. The story of the birth of Uma

## \|\| 21.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*pulastya kathyatāṃ tāvad devyā bhūyaḥ samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*mahatkautūhalaṃ me 'dya vistarād brahmavittama \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said- О great Pulastya, you are the best among the sages known to Brahma. Please, again tell me in detail about the origin of goddess today. I am curious enough to listen.

## \|\| 21.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ kathayiṣyāmi bhūyo 'syāḥ saṃbhavaṃ mune \|*  
*śumbhāsuravadhārthāya lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Pulastya said- О hermit! Listen to carefully to the re-appearance of goddess for the cause of killing Kumbha monster in order to maintain peace in the world. I am now going to explain it.

## \|\| 21.3 \|\|

*yā sā himavataḥ putrī bhavenoḍhā tapodhanā \|*  
*umā nāmnā ca tasyāḥ sā kośāñjātā tukauśikī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. That goddess Kausiki got her birth from the Kosa (by virtue of penance) of goddess Uma, daughter of Himalaya married to lord Sankara.

## \|\| 21.4 \|\|

*saṃbhīya vindhyaṃ gatvā ca bhṛyo bhūtagaṇairvṛtā \|*  
*śumbhaṃ caiva niśumbhaṃ ca vadhiṣyati varāyudhaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She would go after birth again to the mountain Vindhya in the company of her ghosts (bhutaganas) and slaughter Sumbha and Nisumbha by exercising her acute and sharp weapons.

## \|\| 21.5 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*brahmaṃstvayā samākhyātā mṛtā dakṣatmajā satī \|*  
*sā jātā himavatputrītyevaṃ me vaktumarhasi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Narada said- О Brahmin! You yourself had said that Sati, the daughter of Daksa was dead; then how come she again became the daughter of Himalaya? Please, give a detailed account of that event.

## \|\| 21.6-8 \|\|

*yathā ca pārvatīkośāt samuddhabhūtā hi kauśikī \|*  
*yathā hatavatī śumbhaṃ nisumbhaṃ ca mahāsuram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kasya cemau sutau vīrau khyātau śumbhaniśumbhakau \|*  
*etad vistarataḥ sarvaṃ yathāvad vaktumarhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhagavaṃstvatapsadena devyācaritamuttamam \|*  
*śrutaṃ vistarato barūhi pārvatyāḥ saṃbhavaṃ mune\|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Again please, tell that how Kausiki appeared from the Kosa of goddess Parvati and how she slaughtered the mighty and indomitable monsters Sumbha and Nisumbha? Again tell in detail that who was the father of Sumbha and Nisumbha? By your grace, I listened such excellent character of goddess Durga, now recite me in detail about the story of goddess Parvati and her birth.

## \|\| 21.9 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*etatte kathayiṣyāmi pārvatyāḥ saṃbhavaṃ mune \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā skandotpattiṃ ca śāśvatīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Pulastya said- О hermit! I describe the origin of Kausiki from Parvati. Listen carefully to the episode on the origin of immortal Skanda.

## \|\| 21.10 \|\|

*rudraḥ satyāṃ praṇaṣṭāyāṃ brahmacārivrate stitaḥ \|*  
*nirāśrayatvamāpannastapastaptuṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Rudra began to engross himself in austerity by observing celibacy strongly when Sati set her body on fire.

## \|\| 21.11 \|\|

*sa cāsīd devasenānīrdaityadarphavināśanaḥ \|*  
*śivarūtvamāsthāya saināpatyaṃ samutsṛjat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was the commander of divine army and destroyed the monsters by virtue of his being chivalrous and skilled in war-craft. He had then shifted to peace and became Siva. Thus, he resigned from commanding the divine army.

## \|\| 21.12 \|\|

*tato nirākṛtā devāḥ senānāthena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*dānavendreṇa vikramya mahiṣeṇa parājitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The demon king Mahisa defeated all gods under forcible attack when he saw that Sambhu is no more commanding the divine army.

## \|\| 21.13 \|\|

*tato jagmuḥ mureśānaṃ draṣṭuṃ cakragadādharam \|*  
*śvetdavīpe mahāhaṃsaṃ prapannāḥ śaraṇaṃ harim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The gods so defeated went to see Cakragadadhara (lord Visnu) at £vetadvipa and sheltered by him. Lord Visnu is the sole ruler of gods and called Mahahansa (supreme soul).

## \|\| 21.14 \|\|

*tānāgatān surān dṛṣṭvā tataḥ śakrapurogamān \|*  
*vihasya meghagambhīraṃ provāca puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lord Visnu (Purusottama) saw gods, he smiled and said in a tone serious as the clouds.

## \|\| 21.15 \|\|

*kiṃ jitāstvasurendreṇa mahiṣeṇa durātmanā \|*  
*yena sarve sametyaivaṃ mama pārśvamupāgatāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Why have you been defeated by the demon king the barbarous Mahisa? why has and the case finally come to me.

## \|\| 21.16 \|\|

*tad yuṣmākaṃ hitārthāya yad vadāmi surottamāḥ \|*  
*tatkurudhvaṃ jayo yena samāśritya bhaveddhi vaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О great gods! Do as I say in the interest of you all and worth enabling you to conquer demons.

## \|\| 21.17 \|\|

*ya ete pitaro divyāstvagniṣvātteti viśrutāḥ \|*  
*amīṣāṃ mānasī kanyā menā nāmnāsti devatāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О gods! The divine Pitara known as Agnisvatta has a virgin (Minasi) called Mena.

## \|\| 21.18 \|\|

*tāmārādhya mahātithyāṃ śraddhayā parayāmarāḥ \|*  
*prārthayadhvaṃ satīṃ menāṃ prāleyādrerihārthataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О gods! Do worship of Sati Mena on Mahatithi (Amavasya) with keen obeisance and request her to marry Himalaya (viz. accept to be wife of Himalaya).

## \|\| 21.19 \|\|

*tasyāṃ sā rūpasaṃyuktā bhaviṣyati tapasvinī \|*  
*dakṣakopād yayā muktaṃ malavajjīvitaṃ priyam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. That usterious virgin who once had abandoned her dear life like night-soil (rubbish) on account of neglect made by Daksa (her father) will get birth from the womb of Mena.

## \|\| 21.20 \|\|

*sā śaṅkarāt svatejoṃ'śaṃ janayiṣyati yaṃ sutam \|*  
*sa haniṣyati daityendraṃ mahiṣaṃ sapadānugam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The son bom as a result of consummation with Sankara of that virgin shall kill the demon king Mahisa with his army and all attendants.

## \|\| 21.21 \|\|

*tasmād gacchata puṇyaṃ tat kurukṣetraṃ mahāphalam \|*  
*tatra pṛthūdake tīrthe pūjyantāṃ pitaro 'vyayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Hence, I suggest you to go at Kuruksetra, the blessed place and do worship of imperishable ancestors at the holy place of Prthudaka.

## \|\| 21.22 \|\|

*mahātithyāṃ mahāpuṇye yadi śatruparābhavam \|*  
*jihāsatātmanaḥ sarve itthaṃ vai kriyatāmiti \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Perform this rite at that most sacred place on Mahatithi if you all wish to give defeat to your enemy.

## \|\| 21.23 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā vāsudevena devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhūtvā papracchuḥ paramśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Pulastya said- Indra etc. gods asked that supreme god with folded hands when this was suggested by him.

## \|\| 21.24 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ko 'yaṃ kurukṣetra iti yatra puṇyaṃ pṛthūdakam \|*  
*udbhavaṃ tasya tīrthasya bhagavān prabravītu naḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The gods asked- Where is Kuruksetra that has the holy place Prthudaka? Explain the origin of that holy place.

## \|\| 21.25 \|\|

*keyaṃ proktā mahāpuṇyā tithīnāmuttamā tithiḥ \|*  
*yasyāṃ hi pitaro divyāḥ pūjyāsmābhiḥ prayantataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Explain again the best day (tithi) most sacrosanct on which we should worship the divine ancestors.

## \|\| 21.26 \|\|

*tataḥ surāṇāṃ vacanānmurāriḥ kaiṭabhārdanaḥ \|*  
*kurukṣetrodbhavaṃ puṇyaṃ proktavāṃstāṃ tithīmapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Murari, who once had killed the monster Kaitabha then began explaining the origin of sacred Kuruksetra and that holiest the day (tithi).

## \|\| 21.27 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*somavaṃśodbhavo rājā ṛkṣo nāma mahābalaḥ \|*  
*kṛsyādau samabhavadṛkṣāt saṃvaraṇo 'vat \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Lord said- During the beginning of Kita era, a mighty king Rbha was bom in the Soma dynasty. Samvarana was originated by Rksa.

## \|\| 21.28 \|\|

*sa ca pitrā nije rājye bāla evābhiṣecitaḥ \|*  
*bālye 'pi dharmanirato madbhaktaśca sadābhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. His father Rksa enthroned him when he was merely a child. He was religion abiding and my devotee since childhood.

## \|\| 21.29 \|\|

*purohitastu tasyāsīd vasiṣṭho varuṇātmajaḥ \|*  
*sa cāsyādhyāpayāmāsa sāṅgān vedānudāradhīḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Vasistha, the son of Varuna, was his priest (Purohita). He taught him the Vedas with their ahgas (parts).

## \|\| 21.30 \|\|

*tato jagāma cāraṇyaṃ tvanadhyāye nṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*sarvakarmasu nikṣipya vasiṣṭhaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. That prince went to the forest when his study was completed by duly assigning the affairs of the state to the austere Vasistha.

## \|\| 21.31 \|\|

*tato mṛgayāvyākṣepād ekākī vijanaṃ vanam \|*  
*vaibhrājaṃ sa jagāmātha athonmādanamabhyayāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Attached with haunting, he then reached alone a deserted forest Vaibhraja and intoxicated there (viz. engrossed himself in pleasure so deep as to forget other liabilities).

## \|\| 21.32 \|\|

*tatastu kautukāviṣṭaḥ sarvatukusume vane \|*  
*avitṛpataḥ sugandhasya samantād vyacarad vanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He saw a forest where all seasonal flowers simultaneously blossomed. It geared up his curiosity to see entire forest as the fragrant atmosphere rendered him with extreme pleasure.

## \|\| 21.33 \|\|

*sa vanantaṃ ca dadṛśe phullakokanadāvṛtam \|*  
*kahlārapadmakumudaiḥ kamalendīvarairapi \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He saw the forest covered everywhere with phulla, kokanada, kalhara, padma, lily, lotus and Indivara flowers.

## \|\| 21.34 \|\|

*tatra krīḍanti satatamapsaro 'marakanyakāḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ madhye dadarśātha kanyāṃ saṃvaraṇo 'dhikām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The divine damsels and nymphs were playing there regularly. Sariwarana saw a most beautiful virgin among them.

## \|\| 21.35 \|\|

*darśanādeva sa nṛpaḥ kāmamārgaṇapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*jātaḥ sā ca tamīkṣyaiva kāmabāṇāturābhavat \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. With meeting the eyes with each other the prince as also that virgin simultaneously fell a prey to sensuous feelings.

## \|\| 21.36 \|\|

*ubhau tau pīḍitau mohaṃ jagmatuḥ kāmamārgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*rājā calāsano bhūmyāṃ nipapāta turaṅgamāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Both of them lost consciousness on account of feeling excessive appeal for sex. The king lost control on the horse back and he fell down on the ground immediately.

## \|\| 21.37 \|\|

*tamabhyetya mahātmāno gandharvāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*siṣicurvāriṇābhyetya labdhasaṃjño 'bhavat kṣaṇāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Gandharvas having power to change their complexion voluntarily soon got him and sprinkled water on his face. Thus, he regained conscious.

## \|\| 21.38 \|\|

*sā cāpsarobhirutpātya nītā pitṛkulaṃ nijam \|*  
*tābhirāśvāsitā cāpi madhurairvacanāmbubhiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The nymphs on the other side lifted up that unconscious virgin and brought to her father's home. They revived her by sprinkling water in the form of their sweet words of assurance.

## \|\| 21.39 \|\|

*sa cāpyaruhya turagaṃ pratiṣṭhānaṃ purottamam \|*  
*gatastu meruśikharaṃ kāmacārī yathāmaraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. That king too rode on his horse and returned to Pratisthana pura as the sensuous gods visit the peak of Meru mountain.

## \|\| 21.40 \|\|

*yadāprabhṛti sā dṛṣṭā ārkṣiṇā tapatī girau \|*  
*tadāprabhṛti nāśnāti divā svapiti no niśi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Since the day Samvarapa, the son of Rksa saw Tapati, the divine damsel there, he was so deeply enchanted as he left the day meal and sleep at night.

## \|\| 21.41-42 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvavidavyagroviditvā varuṇātmajaḥ \|*  
*tapatītāpitaṃ vīraṃ pārthivaṃ tapasāṃ nidhiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*samutpatya mahāyogī gaganaṃ ravimaṇḍalam \|*  
*viveśa devaṃ tigmāṃśu dadarśa syandane sthitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. When Vasistha, the son of Varuna saw that chivalrous king so anxious for Tapati by virtue of his intuition and Yoga; he ascended to the sky, entered within sun orbit and saw lord sun seated on his chariot.

## \|\| 21.43 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāskaraṃ devaṃ praṇamad dvijasattamaḥ \|*  
*pratipraṇamitaścāsau bhāskareṇāviśad rathe \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The great Dvija Vasistha saluted god sun and rode on his chariot when it was reciprocated by him.

## \|\| 21.44 \|\|

*jvalajjaṭākalāpo 'sau divākarasamīpagaḥ \|*  
*śobhate vāruṇiḥ śrīmān dvitīya iva bhāskaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Vasistha looked like a second sun with aura shining and matted hair when he took a seat beside the sun.

## \|\| 21.45 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjitor'ghārbhāskareṇa tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭaścāgamane hetuṃ pratyuvāca divākaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. God sun honoured him by offering Argha etc. and asked about the purpose of his visit. Vasistha replied-

## \|\| 21.46 \|\|

*samāyāto 'smi deveśa yācituṃ tvāṃ mahādyute \|*  
*sutāṃ saṃvaraṇasyārthe tasya tvaṃ dātumarhasi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О most radiant god! I have come to ask for the hand of your daughter to Samvarana. Please, fulfil my demand.

## \|\| 21.47 \|\|

*tato vasiṣṭhāya divākareṇa niveditā sā tapatī tanūjā \|*  
*gṛhāgatāya dvijapuṅgavāya rājñor'thataḥ saṃvaraṇasya devāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О gods! lord sun then replied in the affirmative and offered that virgin Tapati for the king Samvarana to Vasistha so came with demand to him.

## \|\| 21.48 \|\|

*sāvitrimādāya tato vasiṣṭhaḥ svamāśramaṃ puṇyamupājagāma \|*  
*sā cāpi saṃsmṛtya nṛpātmajaṃ taṃ kṛtāñjalirvāruṇimāha devī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Vasistha then returned to his asrama with the daughter of sun. That virgin too remembered the prince and said to Vasistha with folded hands.

## \|\| 21.49 \|\|

*tapatyuvāca \|*  
*brahman mayā khedamupetya yo hi sahāpsarobhiḥ paricārikābhiḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭo hyaraṇye 'maragarbhatulyo nṛpātmajo lakṣaṇato 'bhijāne \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Tapati said- О Brahmin! I know the characteristics of the prince I saw in that forest when I was in the company of attendant nymphs and lost my consciousness due to over attraction for him.

## \|\| 21.50 \|\|

*pādau śubhau cakragadāsicihnau jaṅghe tathorū karihastatulyau \|*  
*kaṭistathā siṃhakaṭiryathaiva kṣāmaṃ ca madhyaṃ tribalīnibaddham \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Both this feet are with the marks of discus, mace and axe, his legs and thighs are like an elephant's trunk, his loin is like that of a lion's loin and the middle portion of his body is very thin with three lines drawn thereupon.

## \|\| 21.51 \|\|

*grīvāsya śaṅkhākṛtimādadhāti bhujau ca pīnau kaṭhanausudīrghau \|*  
*hastau tathā padmadalodbhavāṅkau chatrākṛtistasya śiro vibhāti \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. His neck is like a conch, both arms sturdy, solid and long, marks of lotus flower on his palms and his head is like an umbrella.

## \|\| 21.52 \|\|
