*pulastya uvāca tato murāribhuvanaṃ samabhyetya surāstataḥ \|*  
*ūcurdevaṃ namaskṛtya jagatsaṃkṣubdhikāraṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Pulastya said- All gods then visited at Visnu, bowed their heads in however and asked him the reason for sudden excitement of the universe.

## \|\| 62.2 \|\|

*tacchrutvā bhagavāngrāha gacchāmo haramandiram \|*  
*sa vetsyati mahājñānī jagatkṣubdhaṃ carācaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. God Murari heard the curiosity and said- Let us go to Siva. That great scholar definitely would know the reason for the anxiety of the movable and immovable world.

## \|\| 62.3 \|\|

*tathoktā vāsudevena devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*janārdanaṃ puraskṛtya prajagmurmandaraṃ girim \|*  
*na tatra devaṃ vṛṣaṃ na devīṃ na ca nandinam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Indra etc. gods followed god Vasudeva and reached at the mountain Mandar. They did not see Mahadeva, the bull, goddess Parvati and Nandi there.

## \|\| 62.4-5 \|\|

*śūnyaṃ girimapaśyanta ajñānatimirāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*tān mūḍhadṛṣṭīn saṃprekṣya devo viṣṇurmahādyutiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*provāca kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ maheśaṃ purataḥ sthitam \|*  
*tamūcurnaiva deveśaṃ paśyāmo girijāpatim \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. On account of being gripped Witn ignorance, these people saw that mountain void. God Visnu when saw the gods so sinking in ignorance, addressed them- "Whatever you people not seeing Mahadeva just front of you all? They replied we are not seeing the husband of mountain's daughter.

## \|\| 62.6 \|\|

*na vidmaḥ kāraṇaṃ tacca yena hṛṣṭirhatā hi naḥ \|*  
*tānuvāca jaganmūrttiryūyaṃ devasya sāgasaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. We do not know the reason why our vision has been destroyed. God Visnu (Jaganmurtti) said- You are offender of god Siva.

## \|\| 62.7 \|\|

*pāpiṣṭhā garbhahantāro mṛḍānyāḥ svārthatatparāḥ \|*  
*tena jñānaviveko vai hato devena śūlinā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You people have struck to heinous offence as you had destroyed the womb of Mrdani. God Sulapani had therefore, seized your discretion and conscious both.

## \|\| 62.8-9 \|\|

*yenāgrataḥ sthitamapi paśyanto'pi na paśyatha \|*  
*tasmāt kāyaviśuddhyarthaṃ devadṛṣṭyarthamādarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*taptakṛcchreṇa saṃśuddhāḥ kurudhvaṃ snānamīśvare \|*  
*kṣīrasnāne prayuñjīta sārddha kumbhaśataṃ purā \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. This is the reason, Sankara is before you still you are unable to see him. Hence, all people should purify your mind and soul by observing Tapta-krcchra in order to see god and take bath with sheer reverence. О gods! Arrange one hundred fifty pitchers of milk in order to give bath to the god.

## \|\| 62.10 \|\|

*dadhisnāne catuḥṣaṣṭirdvātriṃśaddhaviṣo'rhaṇe \|*  
*pañcagavyasya śuddhasya kummāḥ ṣoḍaśa kīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. (Then for his bath) a provision of sixty four pitchers full of curd, thirty two pitchers ghee and sixteen pitcher pure Pancagavya has been made.

## \|\| 62.11-13 \|\|

*madhuno'ṣṭau jalasyoktāḥ sarve te dviguṇāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*tato rocanayā devamaṣṭottaraśatena hi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*anulimpet kuṅkumena candanena ca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*bilvapatraiḥ sakamalaiḥ dhattūrasuracandanaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mandāraiḥ pārijātaiśca atimuktaisthā'rcayet \|*  
*aguruṃ saha kāleyaṃ candanenāpi dhūpayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. О gods! A bath with eight pitcher full of honey and bath with water just double in number of pitchers has been stated. One should then smear gorocana, kuiiikuifta and sandal as much as one hundred eight times. Then worship with bilvapatra, lotus, horn fruit (dhattura), sura-candana, Mandara, Parijata and Atimukta flowers should be made.

## \|\| 62.14 \|\|

*japtavyaṃ śatarudrīyaṃ ṛgvedokta padakramaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte tu deveśaṃ paśyadhvaṃ netareṇa hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. You should then do japa on Satarudriya in serial to padas laid down in Rgveda. By doing this, you will be able to see the god of gods. There is no other measure to see him.

## \|\| 62.15 \|\|

*ityuktvā vāsudevena devāḥ keśavamabruvan \|*  
*vidhānaṃ taptakṛcchrasya kathyatāṃ madhusūdana \|*  
*yasmiścīrṇe kāyaśuddhirbhavate sārvakālikī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The gods said Kesava- О Madhusudana! Please, tell us the provision of Tapta-krcchra that renders physical purity every time.

## \|\| 62.16 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca tryahamuṣṇāḥ pibedāpa tryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pibet \|*  
*tryahamuṣṇaṃ pibetsarpirvāyubhakṣo dinatrayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Vasudeva said- One should sip hot water for three days, three day then hot milk, three days, in hot ghee and live on air for another three days.

## \|\| 62.17 \|\|

*palā dvādaśa toyasya palāṣṭau payasaḥ surāḥ \|*  
*ṣaṭpalaṃ sarpiṣaḥ proktā divase divase pibet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О gods! One should sip twelve pala water, eight pala milk and six pala ghee during the above-said days.

## \|\| 62.18 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca ityevamukte vacane surāḥ kāyaviśuddhaye \|*  
*taptakṛcchrarahasyaṃ vai cakruḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Pulastya said- Indra etc. gods then observe Tapta-krcchra fast for bringing in purity to the body.

## \|\| 62.19 \|\|

*tato vrate surāścīrṇa vimuktāḥ pāpato'bhavan \|*  
*vimuktapāpā deveśaṃ vāsudevamathābruvan \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The gods absolved from sins when that fast was observed. The gods so absolved from sins said to Vasudeva-

## \|\| 62.20 \|\|

*kvāsau vada jagannātha śaṃbhustiṣṭhati keśava \|*  
*yaṃ kṣīrādyabhiṣekeṇa snāpayāmo vidhānataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О Jagannatha! О Kesava! Please, tell that where is Sambhu existed? See that we can give bath to him with milk etc. only when we could see Mahadeva.

## \|\| 62.21 \|\|

*athovāca surānviṣṇureṣa tiṣṭhati śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*maddehe kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ yogaṃścāyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. God Visnu said to gods- God Sankara is existed in my body. Whether you all are still unable to see?

## \|\| 62.22 \|\|

*tamūcurnaiva paśyāmastvatto vai tripurāntakam \|*  
*satyaṃ vada sureśāna maheśānaḥ kva tiṣṭhati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Those people said to him- We people are not seeing god Sankara in you too. О Suresana! Tell us in fact that where is Mahesa existed?

## \|\| 62.23 \|\|

*tato'vyayātmā sa hariḥ svahṛtpaṅkajaśāyinam \|*  
*darśayāmāsa devānāṃ murārirliṅgamaiśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Avyaya soul Murari Hari then showed the divine linga sleeping in his heart lotus to all gods.

## \|\| 62.24 \|\|

*tataḥ surāḥ krameṇaiva kṣīrādibhiranantaram \|*  
*snāpayāṃcakrire liṅgaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvamavyayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The gods then gave bath to that everlasting, stable and immortal linga with milk etc. in a systematic manner.

## \|\| 62.25 \|\|

*gorocanayāā tvālipya candanena sugandhinā \|*  
*bilvapatrāmbujairdevaṃ pūjayāmāsurañjasā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. They worshipped thereafter that god by smearing gorocana, the fragrant sandal and by offering bilvapatra and lotus flowers.

## \|\| 62.26 \|\|

*pradhūpyāguruṇā bhaktyā nivedya paramauṣadhīḥ \|*  
*japtvā'ṣṭaśatanāmānaṃ praṇāmaṃ cakrire tataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The gods then offered the supreme medicines with lighting Dhupa etc. They chanted one hundred eight names of Sankara and saluted.

## \|\| 62.27 \|\|

*nārada uvāca ityevaṃ cintayantaśca devadetau harīśvarau \|*  
*kathaṃ yogatvamāpannau sattvānyatamasodbhavau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All gods began to think that how integration has been established between Hari, bom with sattva while Sankara bom with Tamas?

## \|\| 62.28 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca surāṇāṃ cintitaṃ jñātvā viśvamūrtirabhūdvibhuḥ \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaḥ sarvāyudhadha ro'vyayaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When Hari came to know the doubt looming in the minds of gods, he turned him into Avyaya, Vibhu, Visvamurti with all characteristics and weapons in his hands.

## \|\| 62.29-31 \|\|

*sārddha trinetraṃ kanakāhikuṇḍalaṃ jaṭāguḍākeśa khagarvabhadhvajam \|*  
*samādhavaṃ hārabhujaṅgayakṣasaṃ pītājinācchannakaṭipradeśam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*cakrāsihastaṃ halaśārṅgapāṇiṃ pinākaśūlājagavānvitaṃ ca \|*  
*kaparchakhaṭvāṅgakapālaghaṇṭā- saśaṅkhaṭaṅkāraravaṃ maharṣe \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭva devā hariśaṃkaraṃ taṃ namo'stu te sarvagatāvyayeti \|*  
*proktapraṇamāḥ kamalāsanādyā- ścakrurmati caikatarāṃ niyujya \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. О hermit! The gods saw with surprise Visnu comprising simultaneously and in a single body serpent earrings, matted hair, bull, garland of serpent, Pinaka, Sula, Ajagava bow, Kaparda, Mahadeva with Khatvahga, gong, stag hide, three eyes, Pitambara, Cakra, Asi, plough, Sarnga bow, conch, kamala kundala, gudakesa, eagle, garland. Brahma etc. gods said- "salute to omniscient avyaya" and thus introduced with the integrated form of Hari and Sankara.

## \|\| 62.32 \|\|

*tānekacittān vijñāya devān devapatirhariḥ \|*  
*pragṛhyābhyadravattūrṇaṃ kurukṣetraṃ svamāśramam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. When Visnu saw that the gods are known properly the integration we took them to his asrama at Kuruksetra.

## \|\| 62.33 \|\|

*tato'paśyanta deveśaṃ sthāṇubhūtaṃ jale śūcim \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā namaḥ sthāṇaveti proktvā sarve'hyupāviśan \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Those all gods then saw the god of gods Sthanu immersed into water. They spoke unanimously- "Salute to Sthanu" and seated there.

## \|\| 62.34 \|\|

*tato'bravīt surapatireohi dīyatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*kṣubdhaṃ jagajjagannātha unmajjasva priyātithe \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Indra then said- О Jagannatha! О Priyatithi! “This entire world has been agitated.” Come to us and bestow a boon.

## \|\| 62.35 \|\|

*tatastāṃ madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śuśrāva vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*śrutvottasthau ca vegena sarvavyāpī nirañjanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Mahadeva, the bull rider then heard that melodious speech. The omnipresent Niranjana then stood up on the water.

## \|\| 62.36 \|\|

*namo'stu sarvadevebhyaḥ provāca prahasanharaḥ \|*  
*sa cāgataḥ suraiḥ sendraiḥ praṇato vinayānvitaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He said smiling- "Salute to all gods. Indra etc. gods saluted humbly to god Sankara so came there.

## \|\| 62.37 \|\|

*tamūcurdevatāḥ sarvāstyajyatāṃ śaṃkara drutam \|*  
*mahāvrataṃ trayo lokāḥ kṣubdhāstvattejasāvṛtāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. All gods said to him- "O Sankara! Give up this great resolution immediately. Three worlds have been excited due to the splendour so increased by virtue of penance made by you.

## \|\| 62.38 \|\|

*athovāca mahādevo mayā tyakto mahāvrataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ surā divaṃ jagmurhaṣṭāḥ prayatamānasāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. God Mahadeva then said- "I abandon just this Mahavrata. The gods then returned to heaven with all satisfaction and balanced mind.

## \|\| 62.39 \|\|

*tato'pi kampate pṛthvī sābdhidvīpācalā mune \|*  
*tato'bhicintayaduduḥ kimartha kṣubhitā mahī \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О sage! The sea, island and mountains on the earth were shivering. Rudra then thought why is the earth so trembling?

## \|\| 62.40 \|\|

*tataḥ paryacaracchūlī kurukṣetraṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*dadarśodhavatītīre uśanarsa taponidhim \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Sankara, the holder of trident then began to walk around Kuruksetra. He saw ascetic Usana on the bank of Oghavati.

## \|\| 62.41 \|\|

*tato'bravītsurapatiḥ kimarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ \|*  
*jagatkṣobhakaraṃ vipra tacchīghraṃ kathyatāṃ mama \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. God Sankara said to him- О Brahmin! Tell me that why are you doing penance to the extent that this entire world is excited.

## \|\| 62.42 \|\|

*uśanā uvāca tavārādhanakāmārthaṃ tapyate hi mahattapaḥ \|*  
*saṃjīvinīṃ śubhā vidyāṃ jñātumicche trilocana \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Usana said- "I am observing the great penance with a desire to worship you. О three eyed god! I want to know the benevolent Sanjivani learning.

## \|\| 62.43 \|\|

*hara uvāca tapasā parituṣṭo'smi sutaptena tapodhana \|*  
*tasmāt saṃjīvinīṃ vidyā bhavān jñāsyati tattvataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Mahadeva said- О ascetic! I am happy to see the penance so properly observed by you. Hence, you will know Sanjivani learning with its original and real form.

## \|\| 62.44 \|\|

*varaṃ labdhvā tataḥ śukrastapasaḥ saṃnyavarttata \|*  
*tathāpi calate pṛthvī sābdhibhūbhṛntragāvṛtā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Sukra then did over his penance. The earth consisting of sea, mountain, tree etc. was still shivering.

## \|\| 62.45 \|\|

*tato'gamanmahādevaḥ saptasārasvataṃ śuci \|*  
*dadarśa nṛtyamānaṃ ca ṛṣiṃ maṅkaṇasaṃjñitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then the sacrosanct Mahadeva went to Saptasarasvata. He saw there Mankana, a hermit dancing.

## \|\| 62.46 \|\|

*bhāvena poplūyati bālavat sa bhujau prasāryaiva nanartta vegāt \|*  
*tasyaiva vegena samāhatā tu cacāla bhūrbhūmidharaiḥ sahaiva \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He was dancing like a child innocently and forgetting everything. His hands were spread wide and he was jumping on heels. The rhythm of dance was so splendid that the earth was shivering with mountains.

## \|\| 62.47 \|\|

*taṃ śaṃkaro'bhyetya kare nigṛhya provāca vākyaṃ prahasan maharṣe \|*  
*kiṃ bhāvito nṛtyasi kena hetunā vadasva māmetya kimatra tuṣṭiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Sankara accessed to him, caught his hand and said with smile on lips- О hermit! Why and for what purpose are you dancing? Please, tell me that why are you so happy?

## \|\| 62.48 \|\|

*sa brāhmaṇaḥ prāha mamādya tuṣṭi- yeneha jātā śṛṇu taddvijendra \|*  
*bahūn gaṇān vai mama tapyatastapaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ kāyaviśoṣaṇārtham \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. That Brahmin said- О great Dvija! Listen to all that pleases me. A number of years passed to the penance I observed in order to bring down my body.

## \|\| 62.49 \|\|

*tato'nu paśyāmi karāt kṣatotthaṃ nirgacchate śākarasaṃ mameha \|*  
*tenādya tuṣṭo'smi bhṛśaṃ dvijendra yenāsmi nṛtyāmi subhāvitātmā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I see now that the injured part of my hand is pouring with vegetable juice. This has pleased me and it is the sole reason for my intoxicated dance in exhilaration.

## \|\| 62.50 \|\|

*taṃ prāha śaṃbhurdvija paśya mahāṃ bhasma pravṛtto'ṅgulito'tiśuklam \|*  
*saṃtāḍanādeva na ca praharṣo mamāsti nūnaṃ hi bhavānpramattaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Sambhu said to him- О Dvija! Look at me. A white ash is coming out from my finger when I hit here. Yet I am not so happy. You have definitely become mad.

## \|\| 62.51 \|\|

*śrutvā'tha vākyaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajasya matvā munirmaṅkaṇako maharṣe \|*  
*nṛtyaṃ parityajya suvismito'tha vavanda pādau vinayāvanamraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О great hermit! Маnkanка stopped dancing when he heard Sankara. He surprised enough and bowed to his feet very humbly.

## \|\| 62.52 \|\|

*tamāha śaṃbhurdvija gaccha lokaṃ taṃ brahmaṇo durgamamavyayasya \|*  
*idaṃ ca tīrthaṃ pravaraṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthūdakasyāstu samaṃ phalena \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Sambhu said to him- О Dvija! Go to the inaccessible abode of Brahma. This holiest place will pour with the fruits analogous to Prthudaka.

## \|\| 62.53 \|\|

*sāṃnidhyamatraiva surāsurāṇāṃ gandharvavidyādharakiṃnarāṇām \|*  
*sadā'stu dharmasya nidhānamagryaṃ sārasvataṃ pāpamalāpahāri \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The gods, demons, gandharva, vidyadhara and kinnaras shall always be present here. This holiest sarasvata will always be an abode of religion and absolving the evils and sins.

## \|\| 62.54-55 \|\|

*suprabhā kāñcanākṣī ca suveṇurvimalodakā \|*  
*mahodarā caughavatī viśālā ca sarasvatī \|\| 54 \|\|*

*etāḥ sapta sarasvatyo nivasiṣyanti nityaśaḥ \|*  
*somapānaphalaṃ sarvāḥ prayacchanti supuṇyadāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Seven rivers- Suprabha, Kancanaksi, Suvenu, Vimalodaka, Manohara, Oghavati, Visala Sarasvati will flow here. All these rivers give the fruit equal to had on soma sipping.

## \|\| 62.56 \|\|

*bhavānapi kurukṣetraṃ mūrti sthāpya garīyasīm \|*  
*gamiṣyati mahāpuṇyaṃ brahmalokaṃ sudurgamam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. You too will go to most sacrosanct and inaccessible abode of Brahma by installing a best icon at Kuruksetra.

## \|\| 62.57 \|\|

*ityevamukto devena śaṃkareṇa tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*mūrtti sthāpya kurukṣetre brahmalokamagādvaśī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On being said by Mahadeva, the austere Mankanaka installed an icon at Kuruksetra and went to, abode of Brahma.

## \|\| 62.58 \|\|

*gate maṅkaṇake pṛthvī niścalā samajāyata \|*  
*athāgānmandaraṃ śaṃbhurnirjanāvasathaṃ śuci \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The earth got stability when the hermit Маnkanка went to the abode of Brahma. Mahadeva too returned at his sacred residence on Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 62.59 \|\|

*evaṃ tavoktaṃ dvija śaṃkarastu gatastadāsīt tapase'tha śaile \|*  
*śūnye'bhyayādraṣṭumatirhi devyā saṃyodhito yena hi kāraṇena \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. О Dvija! I here told you that Sankara had gone for penance and at that interval of his absence, Andhaka fought against the goddess.

## Chapter 63. The story of king Dangaka

## \|\| 63.1 \|\|

*gato'dhakastu pātāle kimaceṣṭata dānavaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkaro mandarastho'pi yacakāra taducyatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said- What did Andhaka, the monster do in nether? Further tell that what did Mahadeva do while living on Mandara mountain?

## \|\| 63.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca pātāla stho'ndhako brahman bādhyate madanāgninā \|*  
*saṃtaptavigrahaḥ sarvān dānavānidamabravīt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Pulastya said- О Brahmana! Andhaka felt excess lust while he was living at nether world. His body was excited. He said to all monsters.

## \|\| 63.3 \|\|

*sa me suhṛtsa me bandhuḥ sa bhrātā sa pitā mama \|*  
*yastāmadrisutāṃ śīghraṃ mamāntikamupānayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He is my true friend, sibling, brother and father who will bring that mountain's daughter to me.

## \|\| 63.4 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvati daityendre andhake madanānyake \|*  
*meghagambhīranirghoṣaṃ prahlādo vākyamabravīt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the monster said these words, Prahlada became serious and said-

## \|\| 63.5 \|\|

*yeyaṃ girisutā vīra sā mātā dharmatastava \|*  
*pitā trinayano devaḥ śrūyatāmatra kāraṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О warrior! The daughter of mountain is your mother by religion and three-eyed Sankara is your father. Listen to the reason for this

## \|\| 63.6 \|\|

*tava pitrā hyaputreṇa dharmanityena dānava \|*  
*ārādhito mahādevaḥ putrārthāya purā kila \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О monster! Your father was religion abiding but issueless. He therefore, did a firm penance long ago for the pleasure of god Siva.

## \|\| 63.7 \|\|

*tasmai trilocanenāsīddatto'nyo'pyeva dānavaḥ \|*  
*putrakaḥ putrakāmasya proktvetyaṃ vacanaṃ vibho \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О monster! The three eyed god gave him a blind son and said-

## \|\| 63.8 \|\|

*netratrayaṃ hiraṇyākṣa narmārthamumayā mama \|*  
*pihitaṃ yogasaṃsthasya tato'dhvamabhavattamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О Hiranyaksa! One day UmS had closed my three eyes just for merriment when I was in meditation. It originated Tama in the form

## \|\| 63.9 \|\|

*tasmādya tamaso jāto bhūto nīlaghanasvanaḥ \|*  
*tadidaṃ gṛhyatāṃ daitya tavaupayikamātmajam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. An organism thundering like cloud was bom from that darkness. His complexion too was blue like cloud. О monster! Receive it. It is an appropriate son for you.

## \|\| 63.10-11 \|\|

*yadā tu lokavidviṣṭaṃ duṣṭaṃ karma kariṣyati \|*  
*trailokyajananīṃ cāpi abhivāñchiṣyate'dhamaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ghātayiṣyati vā vipraṃ yadā prakṣipya cāsurān \|*  
*tadā'sya svayamevāhaṃ kariṣye kāyaśodhanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. When this mean-child will do wicked activities, fall in affection for Parvatl or kill the Brahmins by sending monsters, I myself will do purification of his body.

## \|\| 63.12 \|\|

*evamuktvā gataḥ śaṃbhuḥ svasthānaṃ mandarācalam \|*  
*tvatpitā'pi samabhyāgāttvāmādāya rasātalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Sambhu went to Mandaracala with these words and your father also came to netherland with you.

## \|\| 63.13 \|\|

*etena kāraṇenāmbā śaileyī bhavitā tava \|*  
*sarvasyāpīha jagato guruḥ śaṃbhuḥ pitā dhruvam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hence, mountain's daughter is your mother and Sambhu, the preceptor to entire world is your father.

## \|\| 63.14 \|\|

*bhavānapi tapoyuktaḥ śāstravettā guṇāplutaḥ \|*  
*nedṛśe pāpasaṃkalpe matiṃ kuryādbhavadvidhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. You are acetic, known to Sastras and enriched with a number of strange qualities. Hence, the man like you should not indulge your mind in such evil some acts.

## \|\| 63.15 \|\|

*trailokyaprabhuravyakto bhavaḥ sarvairnamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*ajeyastasya bhāryeyaṃ na tvamardo'marārdana \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О enemy of gods! In expressive Siva is the ruler of three worlds. You should not even think of any affection for his life.

## \|\| 63.16 \|\|

*na cāpi śaktaḥ prāptuṃ tā bhavāśailanṛpātmajām \|*  
*ajitvā sagaṇaṃ rudraṃ sa ca kāmo'tha durlabhaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. You cannot receive that mountain's daughter without giving defeat to Sankara including his ganas. Hence, your such desire is rare and impossible.

## \|\| 63.17 \|\|

*yastaretsāgaraṃ dorthyāṃ pātayeddhavi bhāskaram \|*  
*merumutpāṭayedvāpi sa jayecchūlapāṇinam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Only a man capable to cross the sea by swimming or knock down sun on the ground or root out the Meru mountain can conquer Sankara.

## \|\| 63.18 \|\|

*utāhosvidimāṃ śakyāḥ kriyāṃ kartuṃ narairbalāt \|*  
*na ca śakyo haro jetuṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ mayoditam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Or the above-said works can be done with manpower but Sankara still is undefeated. I have said this all solemnly.

## \|\| 63.19 \|\|

*kiṃ tvayā na śrutaṃ daitya yathā daṇḍo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*parastrīkāmavān mūḍhaḥ sarāṣṭro nāśamāptavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О monster! Have you not listen that the idiot king Danda was ruined with his state as he once wished to do courtship with other's wife?

## \|\| 63.20 \|\|

*āsīddaṇḍo nāma nṛpaḥ prabhūtabalavāhanaḥ \|*  
*sa ca vavre mahātejāḥ paurohityāya bhārgavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A king, danda had a large army and carriers (vahanas). He appointed Sukracarya as his priest (Purohita).

## \|\| 63.21 \|\|

*īje ca vividhairyajñairnṛpatiḥ śukrapālitaḥ \|*  
*śukrasyāsīgha duhitā arajā nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The king performed a number of yajnas under super vision of Sukracarya. Sukracarya had a daughter Araja.

## \|\| 63.22 \|\|

*śukraḥ kadācidagamad vṛṣaparvāṇamāsuram \|*  
*tenārcitaściraṃ tatra tasthau bhārgavasattamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Sukracarya once had gone to Vfsaparva. Bhargava stayed there for several period there when he required so to him.

## \|\| 63.23 \|\|

*arajāḥ svagṛhe vahiṃ śuśrūvantī mahāsura \|*  
*atiṣṭhata sucārvaṅgī tato'bhyāgānnarādhipaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О great monster! The beautiful Araja was at her home serving the fire. Once that king visited there.

## \|\| 63.24 \|\|

*sa papraccha kva śukroti tamūcuḥ paricārikāḥ \|*  
*gataḥ sa bhagavān śukro yājanāya danoḥ sutam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He asked- where is Sukracarya? The home- maids replied- he had gone to arrange yajna at Danunandana.

## \|\| 63.25 \|\|

*papraccha nṛpatiḥ kā tu tiṣṭhate bhārgavāśrame \|*  
*tāstamūcurguroḥ putrī saṃtiṣṭhatyarajā nṛpa \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The king asked- whether any female is in the asrama of Bhargava? They replied- О king! Araja, the daughter of preceptor is there.

## \|\| 63.26 \|\|

*tāmāśrame śukrasutāṃ draṣṭumikṣva \|*  
*kunandanaḥ \|*  
*praviveśa mahābāhurdadarśārajasaṃ tataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The chivalrous Iksvaku's son entered into asrama to see that daughter and saw Araja.

## \|\| 63.27 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmasaṃtaptastatkṣaṇādeva pārthivaḥ \|*  
*saṃjāto'ndhaka daṇḍastu kṛtāntabalacoditaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О Andhaka! On account of the shadow of event, the king motivated and become passionate to see her.

## \|\| 63.28 \|\|

*tato visarjayāmāsa bhṛtyān bhrātṛn suhṛttamān \|*  
*śukraśiṣyānapi balī ekākī pṛṣṭha āvrajat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The mighty king removed all maids, brothers, intimate friends and the disciples of Sukracarya from there and entered lonely at her room.

## \|\| 63.29 \|\|

*tamāgataṃ śukrasutā pratyutyāya yaśasvinī \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭā bhrātṛbhāvena dānava \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The illustrious daughter of Sukra honoured that king as her brother happily.

## \|\| 63.30 \|\|

*tatastāmāha nṛpatirbāle kāmāgnitāpitam \|*  
*māṃ samāhlādayasvādya svapariṣvaṅgavāriṇā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The king said to her- О virgin! I am badly burning in the fire of lust. Satiate me with water of embrace today.

## \|\| 63.31 \|\|

*nītā deśaṃ mahāpuṇya kośalaṃ sādhubhiryutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The river Hiranvati took with her waves Nandayanti to holiest Kosala country inhabited by saints and gentlemen.

## \|\| 64.20 \|\|

*gacchantī sā ca rudatī dadṛśe vaṭapādam \|*  
*prarohaprāvṛtatanuṃ jaṭādharamiveśvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. She was weeping bitterly as she strolled about, and then saw a banyan tree. That banyan was with a number of airy roots like Mahesvara’s matted hair.

## \|\| 64.21 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vipulacchāyaṃ viśaśrāma varānanā \|*  
*upaviṣṭā śilāpaṭṭe tato vācaṃ praśuśrave \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That beautiful virgin sat on a stone lying under the dense shadow of that tree. She then heard a speech.

## \|\| 64.22 \|\|

*na so'sti puruṣaḥ kaścidyastaṃ brūyāttapodhanam \|*  
*yathā satanayastubhyamudbaddho vaṭapādape \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. ’Alas’ there is any person here who can report Rtadhvaja that his son is fastened with this banyan tree.

## \|\| 64.23 \|\|

*sā śrutvā tāṃ tadā vāṇīṃ vispaṣṭākṣarasaṃyutām \|*  
*tiryagūrdhvamadhaścaiva samantādavalokayan \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. She looked here and there all around to find the man so explaining because that voice was clear and precise.

## \|\| 64.24 \|\|

*dadṛśe vṛkṣaśikhare śiśuṃ pañcābdikaṃ sthitam \|*  
*piṅgalābhirjaṭābhisatu udbaddhaṃ yatnataḥ śubhe \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О virtuous lady! she saw a five year old child at the top of that tree. He was duly fastened by the aerial roots of banyan.

## \|\| 64.25 \|\|

*taṃ vibruvantaṃ dṛṣṭaiva nandayantī suduḥkhitā \|*  
*prāha kenāsi baddhastvaṃ pāpinā vada bālaka \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Nandyanati became sad and addressed that speaker- "O child! Tell me that who is the sinner of fastening you in this manner?

## \|\| 64.26 \|\|

*satāmāha mahābhāge baddho'smi kapinā vaṭe \|*  
*jaṭāsvevaṃ suduṣṭena jīvāmi tapaso balāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. That infant replied- О great lady! A wicked monkey has fastened me with aerial roots here. I am living on the power of my penance.

## \|\| 64.27 \|\|

*puron mattapuretyeva tatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatrāsti tapaso rāśiḥ pitā mama ṛtadhvajaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. During long past, god Mahesvara dwelled at a place called Puronmattapura. My father Rtadhvaja used to be there. He was austere.

## \|\| 64.28 \|\|

*tasyāsmi japamānasya mahāyogaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*jāto'livṛndasaṃyuktaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When that exhalted self was contemplating a deep meditation, I was bom, proficient in all the scriptures and attended by a row of bees.

## \|\| 64.29 \|\|

*tato māmabravīttāto nāmakṛtvā śubhānane \|*  
*jābālīti parikhyāya tacchṛṇuṣva śubhānane \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O good complexion virgin! My father addressed me as Jabali and listen to what he was said to me.

## \|\| 64.30 \|\|

*pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi bāla eva bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi kumāratve cariṣyasi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He said- you shall remain a boy for five thousand years and Kumara (youth) for ten thousand years thereafter.

## \|\| 64.31 \|\|

*viṃśati yauvanasthāyī vīryeṇa dvigāṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pañcavarṣaśatān bālo bhokṣyase bandhanaṃ dṛḍham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. You will enjoy manhood for twenty thousand years and shall pass old age just double to that period. Five hundred years of your childhood shall pass in firm bondage.

## \|\| 64.32 \|\|

*daśavarṣaśatānyeva kaumāre kāyapīḍanam \|*  
*yauvane paramān bhogāndvisahattrasamāstathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You shall suffer from physical pains during teenage upto ten thousand years and you will enjoy the supreme pleasures upto two thousand years during manhood.

## \|\| 64.33 \|\|

*catvāriṃśacchatānyeva vārdhake kleśamuttamam \|*  
*lapphsyase bhūmiśacyāḍhyaṃ kadannāśanabhojanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. During forty thousand years of old age, you shall have to suffer severe pains. You shall be compelled to lie on ground and eat coarse food.

## \|\| 64.34 \|\|

*ityevamuktaḥ pitrā'haṃ bālaḥ pañcābdadeśikaḥ \|*  
*vicarāmi mahīpṛṣṭhaṃ gacchan snātuṃ hiraṇvatīm \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When the statement of my father was over, I was at the age of five years walking on earth to see and bath at the river Hiranvati.

## \|\| 64.35 \|\|

*tato'paśyaṃ kapivaraṃ so'vadanmāṃ kva yāsyasi \|*  
*imāṃ devavatīṃ gṛhya mūḍha nyastāṃ mahāśrame \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. I saw a monkey on the way. He said to me- O foolish fellow! “Where are you going with Devavati, kept by me in this great asrama?”

## \|\| 64.36 \|\|

*tato'sau māṃ samādāya visphurantaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*vaṭāgre'sminnudbhabandha jaṭābhirapi sundari \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then, О beautiful lady! He caught me and tied me to the top of this banyan tree by my matted hair. I was shivering that time with

## \|\| 64.37 \|\|

*tathā ca rakṣā kapinā kṛtā bhīru nirantaraiḥ \|*  
*latāpāśairmahāyantramadhstād duṣṭabuddhinā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. О delicate lady! That wicked monkey made a cage by using several creepers as cord, kept me beneath and restrained me continuously.

## \|\| 64.38 \|\|

*abhedyo'yamanākramya upariṣṭāttathāpyadhaḥ \|*  
*diśāṃ mukheṣu sarveṣu kṛtaṃ yantraṃ latāmayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. That cage made up of creepers was very strong from four sides and cannot be pierced even from up or down side.

## \|\| 64.39 \|\|

*saṃyamya māṃ kapivaraḥ prayāto'maraparvatam \|*  
*yathecchyā mayā dṛṣṭametatte gaditaṃ śubhe \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. That monkey thereafter voluntarily went at Amara mountain and I am here so fastened. О lady! I have told all that seen by me.

## \|\| 64.40 \|\|

*bhavatī kā mahāraṇye lalanā parivarjitā \|*  
*samāyātā sucārvaṅgī kena sārthena māṃ vada \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О beautiful virgin! Tell me that who are you and have come with whom in this dreadful forest?

## \|\| 64.41 \|\|

*sā'bravīdañjano nāma guhyakendraḥ pitā mama \|*  
*nandayantīti me nāma pramlocāgarbhasaṃbhavā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. She replied! "Anjana, the lord of Yaksas is my father. My name is Nandayanti. My mother is Pramloca.

## \|\| 64.42 \|\|

*tatra me jātake proktamṛṣiṇā mudgalena hi \|*  
*iyaṃ narendramahiṣī bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Mudgala, a great sage had predicted that this girl shall undoubtedly become a queen.

## \|\| 64.43 \|\|

*tadvākyasamakālaṃ ca vyanadad devadundubhiḥ \|*  
*śivā cāśivanirghoṣā tato bhūyo'bravīnmuniḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Celestial drums in heaven were piped just then and auspicious as well as inauspicious sonds were reported simultaneously. The sage again had declared:

## \|\| 64.44 \|\|

*na saṃdeho narapatermahārājñī bhaviṣyati \|*  
*mahāntaṃ saṃśayaṃ ghoraṃ kanyābhāve gamiṣyasi \|*  
*\|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. There is no scope of doubt that this virgin will become the queen of a king. However, she will remain in a precarius condition during her maidenhood. The sage left that place with such wonderful statement.

## \|\| 64.45 \|\|

*tato jagāma sa ṛṣirevamuktvā vaco'dbhutam \|*  
*pitā māmapi cādāya samāgantumathaicchata \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. My father then wished once to visit at holy place with me. When we were on the way, a monkey sprang up from the bank of Hiranvati.

## \|\| 64.46 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ tato hiraṇvatyāstīrāt kapirathotpatat \|*  
*tadbhayācca mayā hyātmā kṣiptaḥ sāgaragājale \|*  
*tayā'smi deśamānītā imaṃ mānuṣavarjitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Due to fear I rushed but suddenly fell into the river. The river has carried me to this deserted land.

## \|\| 64.47 \|\|

*śrutvā jābāliratha tadvacanaṃ vai tayoditam \|*  
*prāha sundari gacchasva śrīkaṇṭhaṃ yamunātaṭe \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Jabali heard this report and said- О nice lady! Go at Srikantha situated on the bank of Yamuna river.

## \|\| 64.48 \|\|

*tatrāgacchati madhyāhne matpitā śivamarthitum \|*  
*tasmai nivedadyātmānaṃ tataḥ śreyo'dhilapsyase \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. My father comes there to worship Sankara exactly at noon. Report to him about you. You shall definitely receive bliss from him.

## \|\| 64.49 \|\|

*tatastu tvaritā kāle nandayantī taponidhim \|*  
*paritrāṇārthamagamaddhimādreryamunāṃ nadīm \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Nandayanti then speedily started for a holy hermitage and reached at Rtadhvaja, a holy place situated on the bank of Yamuna river in the Himadri for her defence.

## \|\| 64.50 \|\|

*sātvadīrgheṇa kālena kandamūlaphalāśanā \|*  
*saṃprāptā śaṃkarasthānaṃ yatrāgacchati tāpasaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. She took the wild fruits and roots on the way and reached at that place of Sankara where the ascetics used to visit daily in the noontime.

## \|\| 64.51 \|\|

*tataḥ sā devadeveśaṃ śrīkaṇṭhaṃ lokavanditam \|*  
*prativandha tato'paśyadakṣarāṃstānmahāmune \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О great sage! She then worshipped the god of gods Srikantha and looked at the words inscribed there.

## \|\| 64.52 \|\|

*teṣāmarthaṃ hi vijñāya sā tadā cāruhāsinī \|*  
*tañjābālyuditaṃ ślokamalikhaccānyamātmanaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Having understood the meaning of that hymn, that virgin inscribed the words spoken by Jabali and one more hymn relating to her.

## \|\| 64.53 \|\|

*mudgalenāsmi gaditā rājapatnī bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sā cāvasthāmimāṃ prāptā kaścinmāṃ trātumīśvaraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The hermit Mudgala had once declared that I will become queen. But I am passing these days in such piteous condition. Whether there is any lord who could defend me?

## \|\| 64.54 \|\|

*ityullikhya śilāpaṭṭe gatā snātuṃ yamasvasām \|*  
*dadṛśe cāśramavaraṃ mattakokilanāditam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. She wrote this on a slab of stone and then descended in Yamuna for bath. She discovered there an attractive hermitage resonant with the sweet songs of cuckoo.

## \|\| 64.55 \|\|

*tato'manyata sātrarṣirnūnaṃ tiṣṭhati sattamaḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ cintayantī sā saṃpraviṣṭā mahāśramam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. She then fencied that the hermit definitely lives here. Guessing this in mind, she entered in that sacred asrama.

## \|\| 64.56 \|\|

*tato dadarśa devābhāṃ sthitāṃ devavatīṃ śubhām \|*  
*saṃśuṣkāsyāṃ calannetrāṃ tu pariglānāmivābjinīm \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. She then saw the virtuous Devavati of divine lustre, with face emaciated and eyes moving like a withered lotus.

## \|\| 64.57 \|\|

*sā cāpatantīṃ dadṛśe yakṣajāṃ daityanandinī \|*  
*keyamityeva saṃcintya samutthāya sthitā'bhavat \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Devavati saw the Yaksa's daughter approaching her. She stood up thinking that "who is she."

## \|\| 64.58 \|\|

*tato'nyonyaṃ samāliṅgya gāḍhaṃ gāḍhaṃ suhṛttayā \|*  
*papracchatustathānyo'nyaṃ kathayāmāsatustadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then both of them embrace one another friendly and began enquiring and talking each other.

## \|\| 64.59 \|\|

*te parijñātatattvārthe anyonyaṃ lalanottame \|*  
*samāsīne kathābhiste nānārūpābhirādarāt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Both these virgins transacted the true events which took place in their lives and began to say stories in order to get recreation.

## \|\| 64.60 \|\|

*etasminnantare prāptaḥ śrīkaṇṭha strātumādarāt \|*  
*sa tattvajño muniśreṣṭho akṣarāṇyavalokayan \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In the intervening time, that learned sage came near Srikantha for bath and saw the words inscribed on a the slab.

## \|\| 64.61 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā vācayitvā ca tadarthamadhigamya ca \|*  
*muhūrta dhyānamāsthāya vyajānādya taponidhiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He watched, read and understood the meaning. A concentration for second, gave him the exact knowledge on the matter.

## \|\| 64.62 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ tvarayā sa ṛtadhvajaḥ \|*  
*ayodhyā magamatkṣipraṃ draṣṭumiṣkṣvākumīśvaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The hermit Rtadhvaja then worshipped the god of gods and went Ayodhya to see the king Iksvaku.

## \|\| 64.63 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpatiśreṣṭhaṃ tāpaso vākyamabravīt \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ naraśārdūla vijñaptirmama pārthiva \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The ascetic met to the chief of kings and said- О king!, the bravest of men, listen to my report.

## \|\| 64.64 \|\|

*mama putro guṇairyuktaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*udbaddhaḥ kapinā rājan viṣayānte tavaiva hi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. О king! A monkey has tied up my meritorious and learned son in the border of your realm.

## \|\| 64.65 \|\|

*taṃ hi mocayituṃ nānyaḥ śaktastvattanayādṛte \|*  
*śakunirnāma rājendra sa hāstravidhipāragaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О king! Nobody else but only your expert archer son Sakuni can make him free from the ties.

## \|\| 64.66 \|\|

*tanmunervākyamākarṇya pitā mama kṛśodari \|*  
*ādideśa priyaṃ putraṃ śakuniṃ tāpasānvaye \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О slender-waisted one, hearing those words of the hermit, my father asked his dear son Sakuni to go in company with the ascetic.

## \|\| 64.67 \|\|

*tataḥ sa prahitaḥ pitrā bhrātā mama mahābhujaḥ \|\` saṃprāpto bandhanoddeśaṃ samaṃ hi paramarṣiṇā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. My brother in compliance with the order of his father then reached at the place where the son of sage was fastened in his company.

## \|\| 64.68 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā nyagrodhamatyucaṃ prarohāstṛtadiṅmukham \|*  
*dadarśa vṛkṣaśikhare udbaddhamṛṣiputrakam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He observed the son of sage tied at the top of that huge and tall banyan tree. It was covered with the dense aerial roots from all sides.

## \|\| 64.69-70 \|\|

*tāṃśca sarvāllatāpāśān dṛṣṭavānsa samantataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sa muniputraṃ taṃ svajaṭāsaṃyataṃ vaṭe \|\| 69 \|\|*

*dhanurādāya balavānadhijyaṃ sa cakāra ha \|*  
*lāghavādṛṣiputraṃ taṃ rakṣaścicchedamārgaṇaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. He inspected properly those creepers from all sides, the position of sage's son tied by the roots, picked up the bow and began to cut the root very aptly so that the child could escape of blows.

## \|\| 64.71 \|\|

*kapinā yatkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ latāpāśaṃ caturdiśam \|*  
*pañcavarvaśate kāle gate śaktastadā śaraiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The grip of creepers made by that monkey could finally cut-off when as much as five hundred years passed.

## \|\| 64.72-73 \|\|

*latācchannaṃ tatastūrṇamāruroha munirvaṭam \|*  
*prāptaṃ svapitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā jābāliḥ saṃyato'pi san \|\| 72 \|\|*

*ādarāt pitaraṃ mūrdhvā vavandata vidhānataḥ \|*  
*saṃpariṣvajya su munirmūrdhyāghrāya sutaṃ tataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. The sage Rtadhvaja then climbed up that huge tree surrounded by creepers. Jabali bowed his head for father in his honour inspite of his being tied. That sage smelt his forehead and embraced him.

## \|\| 64.74-75 \|\|

*unmocayitumārabdho na śaśāka susaṃyatam \|*  
*tatastūrṇaṃ dhanurjyasya bāṇāṃśca śakunirbalī \|\| 74 \|\|*

*āruroha vaṭaṃ tūrṇaṃ jaṭā mocayituṃ tadā \|*  
*na ca śaknoti saṃcchantraṃ dṛḍhaṃ kapivareṇa hi \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. He then started opening the ties but being these very strong, he failed. Mighty Sakuni then kept his bow and arrow on the ground and climbed up on banyan tree to open those knots. He himself failed to open those knots made by the monkey.

## \|\| 64.76 \|\|

*yadā na śakitā stena saṃpramocayituṃ jaṭāḥ \|*  
*tadā'vatīrṇaḥ śakuniḥ sahitaḥ paramarṣiṇā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. When he was not able to disentangle the boy from his matted locks, sakuni and the great sage together descended down on the earth.

## \|\| 64.77 \|\|

*jagrāha ca dhanurbāṇāṃśakāra śaramaṇḍapam \|*  
*lāghavādarddhacandraistāṃ śākhāṃ ciccheda sa tridhā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. He then picked up bow and arrows and made a bower of arrows. Then he used half crescent arrows to cut that branch into three segments.

## \|\| 64.78 \|\|

*śākhayā kṛttayā cāsau bhāravāhī tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*śarasopānamārgeṇa avatīrṇo'tha pādapāt \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The child (Jabali) came down from tree with the branch of tree so cut-off through the leaders made by Sakuni from his arrows.

## \|\| 64.79 \|\|

*tasmistadā sve tanaye ṛtadhvaja- strāto narendrasya sutena dhanvinā \|*  
*jābālinā bhāravahena saṃyutaḥ samājagāmātha nadīṃ sa sūryajām \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. When his son was so liberated by the valorous son of the king, he took Jabali at the bank, of the river Yamuna with him.

## Chapter 65. Marriage of Citragada

## \|\| 65.1 \|\|

*daṇḍaka uvāca etasminnantare bāle yakṣāsura sute mune \|*  
*samāgate haraṃ draṣṭuṃ śrīkaṇṭhaṃ yogināṃ varam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Dandaka said- During such intervening period, the daughter of Yaksa and the Asura both came to see Srikantha Mahadeva.

## \|\| 65.2 \|\|

*dadṛśāte parimlānasaṃśuṣkakusumaṃ vibhum \|*  
*bahunirmālyasaṃyuktaṃ gate tasmin ṛtadhvaje \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Rtadhvaja having departed from the temple till then, both these virgins foune the lord among faded and dried flowers and strewn over with many remains of offerings of garlands.

## \|\| 65.3 \|\|

*tatastaṃ vīkṣya deveśaṃ te ubhe api kanyake \|*  
*snāpayete vidhānena pūjayetāmaharniśam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When they saw Srikantha, both the maidens washed him according to prescriptions and worshipped him day and night.

## \|\| 65.4 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ sthitābhyāṃ tatraiva ṛṣiradhyāgamanam \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ śrīkaṇṭhamavyaktaṃ gālavo nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When they were living there, a sage named Galava came to see inscrutable Srikantha in that forest.

## \|\| 65.5-6 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā kanyakāyugmaṃ kasyedamiti cintayan \|*  
*praviveśaṃ śuciḥ snātvā kālindyā vimale jale \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tato'nupūjayāmāsa śrīkaṇṭhaṃ gālavo muniḥ \|*  
*gāyete susvaraṃ gītaṃ yakṣāsurasute tataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. When he saw two virgins, a thought came in his mind as whose daughter they might be? He took bath in the pure water of Yamuna, gained purity in heart and soul and then worshipped Mahadeva Srikantha. The daughter of Yaksa and monster then began singing in melodious voice.

## \|\| 65.7 \|\|

*tataḥ svaraṃ samākarṇya gālavaste ajānata \|*  
*gandharvakanyake caite saṃdeho nātra vidyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hearing their voice, Galava guessed of them as daughters of any Gandharva because only they were so expert in singing.

## \|\| 65.8 \|\|

*saṃpūjya devamīśānaṃ gālavastu vidhānataḥ \|*  
*kṛtajapyaḥ samavyāste kanyābhyāmabhivāditaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Having done worship, Galava did Japa of Srikantha. Both maidens saluted him and he then seated there.

## \|\| 65.9 \|\|

*tataḥ papraccha sa muniḥ kanyake kasya kathyatām \|*  
*kulālaṅkārakaraṇe bhaktiyukte bhavasya hi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. That sage asked- “Tell me that who is your father?” You are meritorious and devotee to god Sankara.

## \|\| 65.10 \|\|

*tamūcaturmuniśreṣṭhaṃ yāthātathyaṃ śubhānane \|*  
*jāto viditavṛttānto gālavastapatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then two pretty-faced maidens reported the real facts before Galava and thus, he could knew all about them.

## \|\| 65.11 \|\|

*samuṣya tatra rajanīṃ tābhyāṃ saṃpūjito muniḥ \|*  
*prātarutthāya gaurīśaṃ saṃpūjya ca vidhānataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The sage honoured by both virgins stayed that at night. In next morning, he worshipped Sankara, the husband of Gauri according to the injunctions.

## \|\| 65.12 \|\|

*te upetyābravīdyāsye puṣkarāraṇyamuttamam \|*  
*āmantrayāmi vāṃ kanye samanujñātumarhathaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He then went to them and said-I shall go to excellent Puskara forest. So, I want to ask your permission to my mission. Please, give your consent.

## \|\| 65.13 \|\|

*tataste ūcaturbrahmandurlabhaṃ darśanaṃ tava \|*  
*kimarthaṃ puṣkarāraṇyaṃ bhavānyāsyatyathādarāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Both maidens asked him- О Brahmana! your meeting is rare. Why are you visiting Puskara forest with such reverence?

## \|\| 65.14 \|\|

*te uvāca mahātejā mahatkāryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*kārtikī puṇyadā bhāvimāsānte puṣkareṣu hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The most learned and noblest sage said to them- "The full moon night of Kartika (November) month is approaching nearer. It gives rare boons as a result of bath in Puskara.

## \|\| 65.15 \|\|

*te ūcaturvayaṃ yāmo bhavānyatra gamiṣyati \|*  
*na tvayā sma vinā brahmanniha sthātuṃ hi śaknuvaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Both of them replied- We will follow you everywhere you go. О Brahmin! We cannot remain here without you.

## \|\| 65.16 \|\|

*bāḍhamāha muniśreṣṭhastato natvā maheśvaram \|*  
*gate ca ṛṣiṇā sārddhaṃ puṣkarāraṇyamādarāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The hermit said- "It's very well." They, saluted Mahesvara and went to Puskara forest with the hermit.

## \|\| 65.17 \|\|

*tathā'nye ṛṣayastatra samāyātāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*pārthivā jānapadyāśca muktvaikaṃ tamṛtadhvajam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Barring Rtadhvaja, there were gathered several thousand hermits, the kings and the citizens of the Janapadas (district).

## \|\| 65.18 \|\|

*tataḥ snātāśca kārttikyāmṛṣayaḥ puṣkareṣvatha \|*  
*rājānaśca mahābhāgā nābhāgeṣṭvā kusaṃyutāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The hermits, the illustrious kings including Nabhaga and Iksvaku etc. took bath in Puskara, the holy place on the day of Kartika Purnima.

## \|\| 65.19 \|\|

*gālavo'pi samaṃ tābhyāṃ kanyakābhyāmavātarat \|*  
*snātuṃ sa puṣkare tīrthe madhyame dhanuṣākṛtau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Galava too descended to take bath in Puskara, the holy place in the shape of bow with those two maidens.

## \|\| 65.20 \|\|

*nimagnaścāpi dadṛśe mahāmatsyaṃ jaleśayam \|*  
*bahvībhirmatsyakanyābhiḥ prīyamāṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When he took dip in depth, a huge size fish was seen there being frequently gratified by many female fish again and again.

## \|\| 65.21 \|\|

*sa tāścāha timirmugdhāḥ yūyaṃ dharma na jānatha \|*  
*janāpavādaṃ ghoraṃ hi na śaktaḥ soḍhumulvaṇam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That fish said to them “You are infatuated, do not know what is morality?” I cannot bear excessive and dreadful public censure.

## \|\| 65.22 \|\|

*tāstāmūcurmahāmatsyaṃ kiṃ na paśyasi gālavam \|*  
*tāpasaṃ kanyakābhyāṃ vai vicarantaṃ yathecchayā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Those female fish said to the great fish- “Whether you are not seeing an ascetic Galava moving freely in company of two virgins.”

## \|\| 65.23 \|\|

*yadyasāvapi dharmātmā na bibheti tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*janāpavādāttatkiṃ tvaṃ bibheṣi jalamadhyagaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “When this virtuous-souled ascetic is not afraid of public blame, why do you, dwelling inside water as you are, fear any reproach?”

## \|\| 65.24 \|\|

*tatastācāha sa timinaiṣa vetti tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*rāgāndho nāpi ca bhayaṃ vijānāti subāliśaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. That great fish replied- “This ascetic is blind of affection and does not know the morality. He is blind with lust and has no fear of the blame that pierces later-on.”

## \|\| 65.25 \|\|

*tacchrutvā matsyavacanaṃ gālavo vrīḍayā yutaḥ \|*  
*nottatāra nimagno'pi tasthau sa vijitendriyaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Galava ashamed of listening to such remark. He did not came up and by virtue of his extreme powers remained at the bottom of river for a longer period.

## \|\| 65.26 \|\|

*snātvā te api rambhorū samuttīrya taṭe sthite \|*  
*pratīkṣantyau munivaraṃ taddarśanasamutsuke \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Both those virgins came out from the river after bath, stood up at the bank and waited curiously for that sage.

## \|\| 65.27 \|\|

*vṛttā ca puṣkare yātrā gatā lokā yathāgatam \|*  
*ṛṣayaḥ pārthivāścānye nānā jānapadāstadā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All sages, the kings and citizen returned back to their respective place when this journey to Puskara was completed.

## \|\| 65.28 \|\|

*tatra sthitaikā sudatī viśvakarmatanūruhā \|*  
*citrāṅgadā sucārvaṅgī vīkṣantī tanumadhyame \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. There was left only Citrangada, a beautiful lady with attractive teeth. That daughter of Visvakarma was stood there and gazing at those two virgins.

## \|\| 65.29 \|\|

*te sthite cāpi vīkṣantyau pratīkṣantyau ca gālavam \|*  
*saṃsthite nirjane tīrthe gālavo'ntarjale tathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Both of them too stood in that deserted place for long as they were waiting for Galava. However, Galava had determined not to come up from water, so he remained there.

## \|\| 65.30 \|\|

*tato'bhyagādvedavatī nāmnā gandharvakanyakā \|*  
*parjanyatanayā sādhvī ghṛtācīgarbhasaṃbhavā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then there came Vedavati, the virtuous Gandharva maiden. Her mother was Ghrtaci and father was Parjanya, a Gandharva.

## \|\| 65.31 \|\|

*sā cābhyetya jale puṇye snātvā madhyamapuṣkare \|*  
*dadarśa kanyātritayamubhayostaṭayoḥ sthitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. She took bath in the holy water of the middle tank in Puskara and saw the three maidens stood on either side of the river.

## \|\| 65.32 \|\|

*citrāṅgadāmathābhyetya paryapṛcchadaniṣṭhuram \|*  
*kāsi kena ca kāryeṇa nirjane sthitavatyasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. She first came to Citrangada and asked politely- "Who are you? Tell me the purpose for which you are here in this deserted place."

## \|\| 65.33 \|\|

*sā tāmuvāca putrīṃ māṃ vindasva suravardhakeḥ \|*  
*citrāṅgadeti suśroṇi vikhyātāṃ viśvakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Citrangada replied- О you of lovely hips! Know me as Citrangada, the daughter of Visvakarma, the divine artisan.

## \|\| 65.34 \|\|

*sāhamabhyāgatā bhadre snātuṃ puṇyāṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*naimiṣe kāñcanākṣīṃ tu vikhyātāṃ dharmamātaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О good virgin! I had gone to take bath in Kancanaksi, the sacred river in Naimisa, the place known as the mother of religion.

## \|\| 65.35 \|\|

*tatrāgatātha rājñā'haṃ dṛṣṭā vaidarbhakeṇa hi \|*  
*surathena sa kāmārto māmeva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The king Suratha of Vidarbha dynasty saw me there and surrendered himself unto me as he was encited to my beauty.

## \|\| 65.36 \|\|

*mayātmā tasya dattaśca sakhībhirvāryamāṇayā \|*  
*tataḥ śaptā'smi tātena viyuktā'smi ca bhūbhujā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. My companions resisted me, yet I surrendered myself for him. My father then cursed me and it separated me from the king.

## \|\| 65.37 \|\|

*martuṃ kṛtamatirbhadre vāritā guhyakena ca \|*  
*śrīkaṇṭhamagamaṃ draṣṭuṃ tato godāvaraṃ jalam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O nice maiden! I thought of suicide but Guhyaka resisted me. I then went to visit Srikantha and then accessed to Godavari.

## \|\| 65.38 \|\|

*tasmādimaṃ samāyātā tīrthapravaramuttam \|*  
*na cāpi dṛṣṭaḥ surathaḥ sa manohlādanaḥ patiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I came from there in this best holy place. But I still unable to see my heart-ravishing husband Suratha.

## \|\| 65.39 \|\|

*bhavatī cātra kā bāle vṛtte yātrāphale'dhunā \|*  
*samāgatā hi tacchaṃse mama satyena bhāmini \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O young lady! You have come here when the auspicious day has over. Please, tell me who are you? О spinster! Tell me everything correctly.

## \|\| 65.40 \|\|

*sābadrīcchūyatāṃ yā'smi mandabhāgyā kṛśodarī \|*  
*yathā yātrāphale vṛtte samāyātā'smi puṣkaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. She replied- О slender-waisted one! Listen to my introduction and the reason for arrival in Puskara when the auspicious time is over.

## \|\| 65.41 \|\|

*parjanyasya ghṛtācyāṃ tu jātā vedavatīti hi \|*  
*ramamāṇā vanoddeśe dṛṣṭā'smi kapinā sakhi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I am Vedavati. My mother is Ghrtaci and father is Parjanya. О friend! I was strolling around a forest when a monkey saw me.

## \|\| 65.42 \|\|

*sa cābhyetyābravīnta kā tvaṃ yāsi devavatīti hi \|*  
*ānītāsyāśramātkena bhṛpṛṣṭhānmeruparvatam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He came to me and asked- "Who are you? Where are you going?" You definitely are Devavati. Who has picked you up from an asrama on the earth to this mountain Meru?

## \|\| 65.43 \|\|

*tato mayokto naivāsmi kape devavatītyaham \|*  
*nāmnā vedavatītyevaṃ merorapi kṛtāśrayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. I replied- О monkey! I am not Devavati and my name is Vedavati. I always live on the mountain Meru.

## \|\| 65.44 \|\|

*tatastenātiduṣṭena vānareṇa hyabhidrutā \|*  
*samārūḍhāsmi sahasā bandhujīvaṃ nagottamam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. That wicked monkey then attacked me. I suddenly climbed on the tree of Bandhujiva.

## \|\| 65.45 \|\|

*tenāpi vṛkṣastarasā pādākrāntastvabhajyata \|*  
*tatosya vipulāṃ śākhāṃ samāliṅgaya sthitā tvaham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The monkey hit hard by kicks and collapsed that tree. I remained hugged to a large branch of that tree.

## \|\| 65.46 \|\|

*tataḥ plavaṅgamo vṛkṣa prākṣipat sāgarāmbhasi \|*  
*saha tenaiva vṛkṣeṇa patitāsmyahamākulā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The monkey then threw that tree in sea. I was frightened badly and fell into the see along with that tree.

## \|\| 65.47 \|\|

*tatombaratalād vṛkṣaṃ nipatantaṃ yadṛcchayā \|*  
*dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. All movable and immovable beings saw the scene of that tree falling down from the sky of its own accord.

## \|\| 65.48-49 \|\|

*tato hāhākṛtaṃ lokairmā patantīṃ nirīkṣya hi \|*  
*ūcuśca siddhagandharvāḥ kaṣṭaṃ seyaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*indradyumnasya mahiṣī gaditā brahmaṇā svayam \|*  
*manoḥ putrasya vīrasya sahasrakratuyājinaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. All those cried with grief when they saw me falling down along with the tree. The Siddhas and Gandharvas said- “Oh! It is piteous scene.” Brahma had declared himself that this maiden will become the queen of high-souled Indradyumna, the son of Manu, the Karta of several thousand sacrifices.

## \|\| 65.50 \|\|

*tāṃ vāṇīṃ madhurāṃ śrutvā mohamaspyāgatā tataḥ \|*  
*na ca jāne sa kenāpi vṛkṣaśchinnaḥ sahasrathā \|*  
*\|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Having heard that sweet voice, I fell unconscious. I do not know who had cut-off that tree in several thousand pieces.

## \|\| 65.51 \|\|

*tatto'smi vegāt balinā itānalasakhena hi \|*  
*samānītāsmyahamimaṃ tvaṃ dṛṣṭā cādya sundari \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The mighty wind, the friend of fire has then brought me here with its strong waves. О pretty lady! I could now see you here.

## \|\| 65.52 \|\|

*taduttiṣṭhasva gacchāvaḥ pṛcchāvaḥ ka ime sthite \|*  
*kanyake anupaśye hi puṣkarasyottare taṭe \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. So, stand up please. Let us move from here and see that who are the girls standing at the northern bank of this Puskara river, we should enquire them.

## \|\| 65.53 \|\|

*evamuktvā varāṅgī sā tayā sutanukanyayā \|*  
*jagāma kanyake draṣṭha praṣṭuṃ kāryasamutsukā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. With these words that curious virgin took her and reached at the place where two girls were stood. They wanted to identify them.

## \|\| 65.54 \|\|

*tato gatvā paryapṛcchat ūcaturume api \|*  
*yātātathyaṃ tayostābhyāṃ svamātmānaṃ niveditam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then both of them approached the two girls and questioned them. They too in their turn narrated the true facts and expressed themselves clearly.

## \|\| 65.55 \|\|

*tatastaṣṭhaturopīha saptagodāvaraṃ jalam \|*  
*saṃprāpya tīre tiṣṭhanti arcantyo hāṭakeśvaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. These four maidens then began to live in that holy place near the confluence of seven Godavari waters and engaged themselves in the worship of god Sankara.

## \|\| 65.56 \|\|

*tato bahūn varṣagaṇān babhramuste janāstrayaḥ \|*  
*tāsāmarthāya śakunirjābāliḥ saṛtadhvajaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. When one thousand years passed, the fatigued load-bearer Jabali left the hope and returned with his father at the district of Sakala.

## \|\| 65.57 \|\|

*bhāravāhī tato khinno daśābdaśatike gate \|*  
*kāle jagāma nirvedātsamaṃ pitrā tu śākalam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. 1. Performer.

## \|\| 65.58 \|\|

*tasminnarapatiḥ śrīmānindradyumno manoḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*samadhyāste sa vijñāya sārdhapātro viniryayau \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The king Indradyumna, son of Manu was residing there. He came out from palace with Arghya in his hand when he learned of their presence.

## \|\| 65.59 \|\|

*samyaksaṃpūjitastena sajābāliṛtavvajaḥ \|*  
*sa cekṣvākusuto dhīmān śakunirdhātṛjo'rcitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. He worshipped with reverence Jabali and Rtadhvaja and honoured the talented nephew Sakuni who was the son of Iksvaku.

## \|\| 65.60 \|\|

*tato vākyaṃ muniḥ prāha indradyumnaṃ ṛtavvajaḥ \|*  
*rājantraṣṭā'balā'smākaṃ nandayantīti viśrutā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Rtadhvaja sage then said to Indradyumna- “O king! Our frail maiden Nandayanti has been missing.”

## \|\| 65.61 \|\|

*tasyārthe caiva vasudhā asmābhiraṭitā nṛpa \|*  
*tasmāduttiṣṭha mārgasva sāhāyyaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O king! All of us have traversed the entire earth in search of her. Hence, please take it in your notice, do search of her and thus, cooperate us in the mission.

## \|\| 65.62 \|\|

*athovāca nṛpo brahman mamāpi lalanottamā \|*  
*naṣṭā kṛtaśramasyāpi kasyāhaṃ kathayāmi tām \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The king then said- О Brahmana! a maiden of mine too is missing. I have done enormous labour to search her. To whom should I say about her?

## \|\| 65.63 \|\|

*ākāśāt parvatākāraḥ patamāno nagottamaḥ \|*  
*siddhānāṃ vākyamākarṇya bāṇaiśchinnaḥ sahasradhā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. I had cut a mountain-like tree failing from the sky into several thousand pieces in compliance with the words of Siddhas.

## \|\| 65.64 \|\|

*na caiva sā varārohā vibhinnā lāghavānmayā \|*  
*na ca jānāmi sā kutra tasmādgacchāmi mārgitum \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. I very aptly defended that beautiful virgin from injury. But I don't know where is she. I am therefore, ready to go with you in search of her.

## \|\| 65.65 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā sa nṛpaḥ samutthāya tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*syandanāni dvijābhyāṃ sa bhrātṛputrāya cārpayat \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. That king immediately stood-up and gave chariots to both Brahmins and his nephew too.

## \|\| 65.66-67 \|\|

*te'dhirūhya rathāṃstūrṇa mārgante vasudhāṃ kramāt \|*  
*badaryāśramamāsādya dadṛśustapasāṃ nidhim \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tapasā karśitaṃ dīnaṃ malapaṅkajaṭādharam \|*  
*niḥśvāsāyāsaparamaṃ prathame vayasi sthitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. They began to investigate on the earth in systematic manner on the chariots. They saw an eminent ascetic seated on penance when they reached at Badari asrama. The young hermit was found to be emaciated by austerities, miserable, bearing matted locks, besmeared with dirt and mud and he was breathing hard.

## \|\| 65.68-69 \|\|

*tamupetyābravīdrājā indudyumno mahābhujaḥ \|*  
*tapasvin yauvane ghoramāsthito'si suduścaram \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tapaḥ kimarthaṃ tacchaṃsa kimabhipretamucyatām \|*  
*so'bravītko bhavānbrūhi mamātmānaṃ suhṛttayā \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. The king Indradyumna went to him and said- О ascetic! Tell me that why are you seated on such strict penance at this early stage? Further, please, tell us that what is your mission? He enquired- “Please, tell me first that who are you and why are you so anxious to ask me, a hermit lean and afflicted with grief?”

## \|\| 65.70-71 \|\|

*paripṛcchasi śokārta parikhinnaṃ taponvitam \|*  
*sa prāha rājā'smi vibho tapasvinśākale pure \|\| 70 \|\|*

*manoḥ putraḥ priyo bhrātā ikṣvākoḥ kathitaṃ tava \|*  
*sa cāsmai pūrvacaritaṃ sarvaṃ kathitavānnṛpaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. He replied- О ascetic! О sovereign! I am the son of Manu, brother of Iksvaku and king of Sakalapura. The ascetic also narrated all his previous life.

## \|\| 65.72 \|\|

*śrutvā provāca rājarṣirmā muñcasva kalevaram \|*  
*āgaccha yāmi tanvaṅgī vicetuṃ bhrātṛjo'si me \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The pious king then said- “Don't abandon your life.” You are my nephew come, we should go in search of that slender-bodied lady.

## \|\| 65.73 \|\|

*ityuktvā saṃpariṣvajya nṛpaṃ dhamanisaṃtatam \|*  
*samāropya rathaṃ tūrṇa tāpasābhyāṃ nyavedayat \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. With these words, he embraced the weak prince. He rode him on a chariot and presented him before both ascetics.

## \|\| 65.74 \|\|

*ṛtadhvajaḥ saputrastu taṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛthivīpatim \|*  
*provāca rājanneohi kariṣyāmi tava priyam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. When Rtadhvaja saw that prince, he along with his son said- О prince! “Come, come here. I will do good for you.”

## \|\| 65.75 \|\|

*yā'sau citrāṅgadā nāma tvayā dṛṣṭā hi naimiṣe \|*  
*saptagodāvare tīrtha sā mayaiva visarjitā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. I have left by myself Citrangada who was beheld by you in Naimisa in the holy confluence of seven Godavaris.

## \|\| 65.76 \|\|

*tadāgacchatha gacchāmaḥ saudevasyaiva kāraṇāt \|*  
*tatrāsmākaṃ sameṣyanti kanyāstistrastathāparāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Hence, come with us. Let us all go there for the son of Sudeva. We shll see three more maidens there.

## \|\| 65.77-78 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā sa ṛṣiḥ samāśvāsya sudevajām \|*  
*śakuni purataḥ kṛtvā sendradyumnaḥ saputrakaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*syandanenāśvayuktena gantuṃ samupacakrame \|*  
*saptagodāvaraṃ tīrthaṃ yatra tāḥ kanyakā gatāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. That hermit consoled the son of Sudeva, accompanied by Indradyumna and his own son, they began to move towards Saptagodavara on the chariot under lead of Sakuni where those maidens had gone.

## \|\| 65.79 \|\|

*etasminnantare tanvī ghṛtācī śokasaṃyutā \|*  
*vicacārodayagiriṃ vicinvantī sutāṃ nijām \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. In the meantime, Ghrtaci, the slenderbodied girl afflicted with grief was strolling on the Udayagiri in search of her daughter.

## \|\| 65.80 \|\|

*tamāsasāda ca kapiṃ paryapṛcchat tathāpsarāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ bālā na tvayā dṛṣṭā kape satyaṃ vadasva māṃ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The Apsaras got that monkey there. She asked him- “O monkey! Tell me the truth if you have seen my daughter anywhere?”

## \|\| 65.81-82 \|\|

*tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa kapiḥ prāha bālikām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā devavatī nāmnā mā nyastā mahāśrame \|\| 81 \|\|*

*kālindyā vimale tīrthe mṛgapakṣisamanvite \|*  
*śrīkaṇṭhāyatanasyāgre mayā satyaṃ tavoditam \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. That monkey replied- “I have seen a maiden named Devavati and kept her at a great as'rama near Srikantha temple at the bank of Kalindi river where birds and deers are found abundantly.” I have reported this fact to you truely.

## \|\| 65.83 \|\|

*sā prāha vānarapate nāmnā vedavatīti sā \|*  
*na hi devavatī khyātā tadāgaccha vrajāvahe \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Ghrtaci said- О chief of monkeys! She is Vedavati and not Devavati. Hence, come with me arid we should go there together.

## \|\| 65.84 \|\|

*ghṛtācyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā vānarastvaritakramaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhato'syāḥ samāgacchannadīmanveva kauśikīm \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The monkey was agreed to Ghrtaci and went jumpingly in company of her towards Kausiki river.

## \|\| 65.85 \|\|

*te cāpi kauśikīṃ prāptā rājarṣipravarāstrayaḥ \|*  
*- dvitayaṃ tāpasābhyāṃ ca rathaiḥ paramavegibhiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Those three great princely sages too reached near Kausiki river with Jabali and Rtadhvaja on the speedy chariots.

## \|\| 65.86 \|\|

*avatīrya rathebhyaste snātumabhyāgamannadīm \|*  
*ghṛtācyapi nadīṃ snātuṃ supuṇyamājagāma ha \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. They alighted from the chariot and came near to the river for bath. Ghrtaci too came for bath in that river.

## \|\| 65.87 \|\|

*tāmanveva kapiḥ prāyādṛṣṭo jābālinā tathā \|*  
*dṛṣṭaiva pitaraṃ prāha pārthivaṃ ca mahābalam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The monkey too came behind her and Jabali saw him. He immediately reported his father and the mighty king about monkey’s appearance there.

## \|\| 65.88 \|\|

*sa eva punarāyāti vānarastāta vegavān \|*  
*pūrvaṃ jaṭāsveva balādyena baddho'smi pādape \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. О father! That powerful monkey is coming again. It is the same monkey who once forcibly tied me with the aerial roots of banyan tree with my matted locks.

## \|\| 65.89 \|\|

*tajjābālivacaḥ śrutvā śakuniḥ krobasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*saśaraṃ dhanurādāya idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Having heard Jabali, Sakuni became furious, picked up his bow fitted with arrow and said-

## \|\| 65.90 \|\|

*brahmanpradīyatāṃ mahāmājñā tāta vadasva mām \|*  
*bāvadenaṃ nihanmyadya śareṇaikena vānaram \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. О Brahmin! О father! Give me permission. Tell me that should I kill this monkey at once with a single arrow?

## \|\| 65.91 \|\|

*ityevamukte vacane sarvabhūtahite rataḥ \|*  
*maharṣiḥ śakuniḥ prāha hetuyuktaṃ vaco mahat \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The great hermit engaged in doing good to all beings then said to Sakuni:

## \|\| 65.92 \|\|

*na kaścittāta kenāpi badhyate hanyate'pi vā \|*  
*vadhabanyau pūrvakarmavaśyau nṛpatinandana \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. О prince! “None can be killed or fettered by another.” О son of a king! “Slaughter and imprisonment are governed by past deeds”.

## \|\| 65.93 \|\|

*ityevamuktatvā śakunibhṛṣirvānaramabravīt \|*  
*ehyehi vānarāsmākaṃ sāhāyyaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The sage then said to the monkey- “O monkey! Come up. It is proper for you ta help us.”

## \|\| 65.94 \|\|

*ityevamukto muninā bāle sa kapikuñjaraḥ \|*  
*kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā praṇipatyedamabravīt \|*  
*mamājñā dīyatāṃ brahmanśādhi kiṃ karavāṇyaham \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. O young lady, thus addressed by the hermit, the great monkey saluted the sage with folded hands and said- “O Brahmin! Instruct me that what should I do at this moment?”

## \|\| 65.95 \|\|

*ityukte prāha sa munistaṃ vānarapatiṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*mama putrasvayodvaddho jaṭāsu vaṭapādape \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. The sage then said to the lord of monkeys- “You had tied my son with his matted hair with the banyan tree.”

## \|\| 65.96 \|\|

*na cenmocayituṃ vṛkṣācchaknuyāmo'pi yatnataḥ \|*  
*tadanena narendreṇa tridhā kṛtvā tu śākhinaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. In spite of our best efforts, we could not make him finally free from that tree. Hence, this king had cut that tree into three pieces.

## \|\| 65.97 \|\|

*śākhāṃ vahati matsūnuḥ śirasā tāṃ vimocaya \|*  
*daśavarṣaśatānyasya śākhāṃ vai vahato'gamanḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. My son is still bearing the burden of the branch of that tree. Please, make him free how. He had now completed ten centuries since he has been carrying the branch.

## \|\| 65.98-99 \|\|

*na ca so'sti pumān kaścidyo hyunmocayituṃ kṣamaḥ \|*  
*sa ṛṣervākyamākarṇya kapirjābālino jaṭāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*śanairunmocayāmāsa kṣaṇādunmocitāca tāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prīto muniśreṣṭho varadobhūdṛtadhvajaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. There is no person who could make him free. That monkey gradually untied the matted locks of Jabali and those were quickly unleased. The sage Rtadhvaja was then pleased and wished to give him a boon.

## \|\| 65.100-102 \|\|

*kapi prāha vṛṇīṣva tvaṃ varaṃ yanmanasepsitam \|*  
*ṛtdhvajavacaḥ śrutvā imaṃ varamayācata \|\| 100 \|\|*

*viśvakarmā mahātejāḥ kapitve pratisaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*brahmanbhavānvaraṃ mahāṃ yadi dātumihecchati \|\| 101 \|\|*

*tatsvadatto mahāghoro mama śāpo nivartyatām \|*  
*citrāṅgadāyāḥ pitaraṃ māṃ tvaṣṭāraṃ tapodhana \|\| 102 \|\|*

100-102. He said to monkey- “Ask whatever you desire.” Visvakarma in the form of that monkey begged this boon from Rtadhvaja- “O Brahmana! if you really are intended to give me a boon, please, remove the impact of curse once thundered on me by youself.” О ascetic, “Recognise me as Tvasta,” the father of Citrangada.

## \|\| 65.103-105 \|\|

*abhijānīhi bhavataḥ śāpādvānaratāṃ gatam \|*  
*subahūni ca pāpāni mayā yāni kṛtāni hi \|\| 103 \|\|*

*kapicāpalyadoṣeṇa tāni me yāntu saṃkṣayam \|*  
*tato ṛtadhvajaḥ prāha śāpasyānto bhaviṣyati \|\| 104 \|\|*

*yadā ghṛtācyāṃ tanayaṃ janiṣyasi mahābalam \|*  
*ityevamuktaḥ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sa tathā kapikuñjaraḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

103-105. I have become monkey due to your curse. Whatever sins I have committed in this monkey form, please destroy them by your blessing. Rtadhvaja said- “the curse shall be effaced when you will give birth to a mighty son from the womb of Ghrtaci.” That monkey became happy with the blessings of Rtadhvaja.

## \|\| 65.106-107 \|\|

*snātuṃ tūrṇaṃ mahānadyāmavatīrṇaḥ kṛśodari \|*  
*tatastu sarve kramaśaḥ snātvā'rcya pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*jagmurhaṣṭā rathebhyaste ghṛtācī divamutpatat \|*  
*tāmanveva mahāvegaḥ sa kapiḥ plavatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

106-107. О slender-waisted lady, the eminent monkey descended immediately for bath in the river. Thereafter, they all took bath and doing (Tarpana of ancestors) and gods and returned by their chariots, while Ghrtaci proceeded to the heaven. That monkey chased her very fast.

## \|\| 65.108-110 \|\|

*dadṛśe rūpasaṃpannāṃ vṛtācīṃ ca plavaṅgamaḥ \|*  
*sāpi taṃ balināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭva kapikuñjaram \|\| 108 \|\|*

*jñātvā'tha viśvakarmāṇaṃ kāmayāmāsa kāminī \|*  
*tato'nuparvataśreṣṭhaṭhe khyāte kolāhale kapiḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*ramayāmāsa tāṃ tanvīṃ sā ca taṃ vānarottamam \|*  
*evaṃ ramantau suciraṃ prāptau tau vindhyaparvatam \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. The monkey beheld the beautiful Ghrtaci. That lady wished courtship with him when she saw him and knowing him to be Visvakarma. That monkey then enjoyed courtship with that lady on the mountain Kolahala. They enjoyed sporting prolong and arrived at the Vindhya mountain.

## \|\| 65.111 \|\|

*rathaiḥ pañcāpi tattīrthaṃ saṃprāptāste narottamāḥ \|*  
*madhyāhnasamaye prītāḥ saptagodāvaraṃ jalaṃ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Those five persons (Rtadhvaja and other) too reached at noon at the holy place of Saptagodavara.

## \|\| 65.112 \|\|

*prāpya viśrāmahetvarthamavaterustvarānvitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sārathayaścāśvān snātvā pītodakāplutān \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. They alighted from the chariots to relax there. Their charioteers also took bath, offered water for horses and then left them for gazing in the attractive forest region.

## \|\| 65.113-115 \|\|

*ramaṇīye vanoddeśe pracārārthe samutsṛjan \|*  
*śāḍvalāḍhyeṣu deśeṣu muhūrtādava vājinaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*tṛptāḥ samādravansarve devāyatanamuttamam \|*  
*turaṅgakhuranirghoṣaṃ śrutvā tā yoṣitāṃ varāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*kimetaditi coktvaiva prajagmurhāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*āruhya balabhauṃ tāstu samudaikṣanta sarvaśaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

113-115. Those horses satisfied within a moment because there was grass abundantly grown. Those horses then began speding near the temple. Having heard the sound coming from hoofs of horses, those maidens went at the temple of Hatakesvara with curiosity to see what is it and looked around getting up on the attic.

## \|\| 65.116 \|\|

*apaśyaṃstīrthasalile strāyamānān narottamān \|*  
*tataścitrāṅgadā dṛṣṭvā jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam \|*  
*surathaṃ hasatī prāha saṃrohatpulakā sakhīm \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. From there, they saw the exalted being bathing in the river. Citrangada saw the king Suratha with matted hair. She became very happy to see him and informed her maiden companion about it.

## \|\| 65.117 \|\|

*yo'sau yuvā nauladhanaprakāśaḥ saṃlakṣyate dīrghabhujaḥ surūpaḥ \|*  
*sa eva nūnaṃ naradevasūnu- vṛto mayā pūrvapataraṃ patiryaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Look at the young-chap with long arms and complexion like blue cloud, I had surrounded before that king on that day.

## \|\| 65.118 \|\|

*yaścaiṣa jāmbūnadatulyavarṇaḥ śvetaṃ jaṭābhāramadhārayiṣyat \|*  
*sa eṣa nūnaṃ tapatāṃ variṣṭho ṛtadhvajo nātra vicāramasti \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. It need not to stress much on mind that the man of golden complexion with white matted hair is definitely the best ascetic Rtadhvaja.

## \|\| 65.119 \|\|

*tatobravīdayo hṛṣṭā nandayantī sakhījanam \|*  
*eṣo'paro'syaiva suto jābālirnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Then Nandayanti said happily to the other mates that the other person undoubtedly is Jabali, the son of Rtadhvaja.

## \|\| 65.120 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ balabhyā avatīrya ca \|*  
*samāsatāgrataḥ śaṃbhorgāyantayo gītikāṃ śubhām \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. With this chat, they sat before the icon of god Sankara and began singing all benevolent song-

## \|\| 65.121 \|\|

*namo'stu śarva śaṃbho trinetra cārugātra trailokyanātha umāpate dakṣayajñavidhvaṃsakara kāmāṅganāśana ghorapāpapraṇāśana mahāpuruṣa mahogramūrte sarvasattvakṣayaṃkara śubhaṃkara maheśvara triśūladhārin smarāre guhāvāsin digvāsaḥ mahācandraśekhara jaṭādhara kapālamālāvibhūṣitaśarīra vāmacakṣuḥ vāmadeva \|*  
*prajādhyakṣa bhagākṣṇoḥ kṣayaṃkara bhīmasena mahāsenanātha paśupate kāmāṅgadahana catvaravāsin śiva mahādeva īśāna śaṃkara bhīma bhava vṛṣabhadhvaja jaṭila prauḍha mahānāṭyeśvara bhūriratna avimuktaka rudra rudreśvara sthāṇo ekaliṅga kālindīpriya śrīkaṇṭha nīlakaṇṭha aparājita ripubhayaṃkara saṃtoṣapate vāmadeva aghora tatpuruṣa mahāghora aghoramūrte śānta sarasvatīkānta konāṭa sahastramūrta mahodbhava vibho kālāgnirudra rudra hara mahīdharapriya sarvatīrthādhivāsa haṃsa kāmeśvara kedārādhipate pūripūrṇa mucukunda madhunivāsin kṛpāṇapāṇe bhayaṃkara vidyārāja somarāja kāmarāja rañjaka añjanarājakanyā-hṛdacalavasate samudraśāyin gajamukha ghaṇṭeśvara gokarṇa brahmayone sahasravakrākṣicaraṇa hāṭakeśvara namaste'stu te \|*  
*etasminnantare prāptāḥ sarva evarṣipārthivāḥ \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ trailokyakartāraṃ tryambakaṃ hāṭakeśvaram \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. We salute to Sarva, Sambhu, Trinetra (three-eyed), Carugatra, Trailokyanatha, Umapati, destroyer of Daksa's yajna, killer of Kama (sex god), Papa-pranasana, Maha- purusa, Mahogramurtti, destroyer of all beings, creator of weal, Mahesvara, trident bearer, enemy of cupid, resident of caves, naked, Mahasankha Sekhara, holder of matted hair, holder of skull garland, Vamacaksu, Vamadeva, Prajadhyaksa, killer of the eyes of Bhaga, of the terrible army, lord of Mahasena, Pasupati, Kamangadhana, Catvaravasini, Siva, Mahadeva, Isana, Sankara, Bhima, Bhava, Vrsabhadhvaja, Jatila, Praudha, Mahanatyesvara, Bhuriratna, Avimuktaka, Rudra, Rudresvara, Sthanu, Ekalitiga, fond of Kalindi, Srikantha, Nilakantha, Aparajita, Ripubhayankara, Santosapati, Vamadeva, Aghora, Tatpurusa, Mahaghora, Aghoramurtti, Santa, Sarasvatikanta, Konata, Sahastramurtti, Mahodbhava, sovereign, Kalagnirudra, Rudra, Hara, Mahidharapriya, Sarvatirthadhivasa, Hamsa, Kamesvara, Kedaradhipati, Paripurna, Mucukunda, Madhunivasin, Krpanapani, Bhayankara, Vidyaraja, Somaraja, Kamaraja, Ranjaka, permanent dweller in the heart of the princess Anjana king, Samudrasayin, Gajamukha, Ghantesvara, Gokarna, Brahmayoni, Sahastravaktraksicarana and Hatakesvara. At the same time, all sages and kings reached there to visit Tryambaka, Hatakesvara, the creator of the three-worlds.

## \|\| 65.122 \|\|

*samārūḍhāśca susnātā dadṛśuryoṣitaśca tāḥ \|*  
*sthitāstu puratastasya gāyantyo geyamuttamam \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. After taking bath, they beheld those women singing excellent songs before the icon of god.

## \|\| 65.123 \|\|

*tataḥ sudevatanayo viśvakarmasutāṃ priyām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā hṛṣitacittastu saṃrohatpulako babhau \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. The son of Sudeva then exhilarated to see her beloved, the daughter of Visvakarma.

## \|\| 65.124 \|\|

*ṛtadhvajo'pi tanvaṅgīṃ dṛṣṭvā citrāṅgadāṃ sthitām \|*  
*pratyabhijñāya yogātmā babhau muditamānasaḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Yogi Rtadhvaja too recognised slenderbodied Citrangada and became highly delighted.

## \|\| 65.125 \|\|

*tatastu sahasā'bhyetya deveśaṃ hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*saṃpūjayantastryakṣa te stuvantaḥ saṃsthitāḥ kramātḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Then all people went to the god of gods Hatakesvara. They worshipped three eyed god, stood up and chanted prayers.

## \|\| 65.126 \|\|

*citrāṅgadāpi tāndṛṣṭvā ṛtadhvajapurogamān \|*  
*samaṃ tābhiḥ kṛśāṅgībhirabhyutthāyābhyavādayat \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Citrangada too stood up with those virgins when saw Rtadhvaja etc. and saluted them.

## \|\| 65.127 \|\|

*sa ca tāḥ pratinandyaiva samaṃ putreṇa tāpasaḥ \|*  
*samaṃ nṛpatibhirhaṣṭaḥ saṃviveśa yathāsukham \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. That ascetic with his son congratulated them and seated there comfortably with kings.

## \|\| 65.128 \|\|

*tataḥ kapivaraḥ prāpto ghṛtācyā saha sundari \|*  
*snātvā godāvarītīrthe didṛkṣurhāṭakeśvaram \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. О beautiful lady! The monkey with Ghrtaci also attended them after taking bath in the holy Godavari. He was also desirous of visiting Hatakesvara.

## \|\| 65.129 \|\|

*tato'paśyat sutāṃ tanvīṃ ghṛtācī śubhadarśanām \|*  
*sā'pi tāṃ mātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭā'bhūdvaravarṇinī \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Ghrtaci then saw her slim-bodied daughter there. She too exhilarated on seeing her mother.

## \|\| 65.130 \|\|

*tato ghṛtācī svāṃ putrīṃ pariṣvajya nyapīḍayat \|*  
*snehāt sabāṣpanayanā muhustāṃ parijighnatī \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Ghrtaci embraced boldly her daughter. She began smelling the weeping daughter on the head again and again.

## \|\| 65.131 \|\|

*tato ṛtabvajaḥ śrīmānkapiṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*gacchānetuṃ guhyakaṃ tvamañjanādrau mahāñjanam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. The ascetic Rtadhvaja then instructed the monkey- "Go at the mountain Anjana to bring Guhyaka (Yaksa) here."

## \|\| 65.132 \|\|

*pātālādapi daityeśaṃ vīraṃ kandaramālinam \|*  
*svargādgandharvarājānaṃ parjanyaṃ śīghramānaya \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Bring here the demon king Kandaramali from the nether world and king of Gandharva Parjanya from the heaven.

## \|\| 65.133 \|\|

*ityevamukte muninā prāha devavatī kapim \|*  
*gālavaṃ vānaraśreṣṭha ihānetuṃ tvamarhasi \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. The ascetic having said this, Devavati said to the monkey- “O great monkey! Please, bring Galava also here.”

## \|\| 65.134 \|\|

*ityevamukte vacane kapirmāstavikramaḥ \|*  
*gatvā'ñjanaṃ samāmantrya jagāmāmaraparvatam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. The monkey with rapid speed went on the mountain Anjana, invited Guhyaka from there and proceeded to the mountain of gods thereafter.

## \|\| 65.135 \|\|

*parjanyaṃ tatra cāmantrya preṣayitvā mahāśrame \|*  
*saptagodāvare tīrthe pātālamagamat kapiḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. He invited Parjanya there, suggested him the route to the great hermitage situated in Saptagodavara and then went to the nelherland.

## \|\| 65.136 \|\|

*tatrāmantrya mahāvīrya kapiḥ kandaramālinam \|*  
*pātālādabhiniṣkramya mahīṃ paryacarajjavī \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Не invited Kandaramali there, came up then on earth and began strolling there.

## \|\| 65.137 \|\|

*gālavaṃ tapaso yoniṃ dṛṣṭvā māhiṣmatīmanu \|*  
*samutpatyānayacchīghraṃ saptagodāvaraṃ jalam \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. He leapt rapidly when he saw Galava near Mahismati and brought him immediately near the holy place Saptagodavara.

## \|\| 65.138 \|\|

*tatra snātvā vidhānena saṃprāpto hāṭakeśvaram \|*  
*dadṛśe nandayantīṃ caṃ sthitāṃ devavatīmapi \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. He reached near Hatakesvara, taking bath there, he saw Nandayanti and Devavati staying there.

## \|\| 65.139-140 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā gālavaṃ caiva samutthāyābhyavādayan \|*  
*sa cārcivyanmahādevaṃ maharṣīnabhyavādayat \|*  
*te cāpi nṛpatiśreṣṭhāstaṃ saṃpūjya tapodhanam \|\| 139 \|\|*

*praharvamatulaṃ gatvā upaviṣṭā yathāsukham \|*  
*teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu tadā vānaropanimantritāḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

139-140. All were stood up to honour Galava when they saw him approaching near. They too worshipped Mahadeva and saluted the hermits. Those great kings also honoured the ascetic and deriving immense pleasure, sat down comfortably. Yaksa, Gandharva and demon all greatmen then came there.

## \|\| 65.141-143 \|\|

*samāyātā mahātmāno yakṣagandharvadānavāḥ \|*  
*tānāgatān samīkṣyaiva putryastāḥ pṛthulocanāḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

*snehārdranayanāḥ sarvāstadā sasvajire pitṛn \|*  
*nandayantyādikā dṛṣṭvā sapitṛkā varānanā \|\| 142 \|\|*

*sabāṣpanayanā jātā viśvakarmasutā tadā \|*  
*atha tāmāha sa muniḥ satyaṃ satyadhvajo vacaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

141-143. The daughters when saw their fathers, their huge eyes filled with tears of joy. They all embraced their fathers. When Citrangada saw her other mates meeting their fathers, she also started weeping. Then Rtadhvaja sage narrated her the fact.

## \|\| 65.144 \|\|

*mā viṣādaṃ kṛthāḥ putri pitā'yaṃ tava vānaraḥ \|*  
*sā tadvacanamākarṇya vrīḍopahatacetanā \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. “O daughter! Don't be dejected. This monkey is your father.” She ashamed of listening these words.

## \|\| 65.145 \|\|

*kathaṃ tu viśvakarmā'sau vānaratvaṃ gato'dhunā \|*  
*duṣṭutryāṃ mayi jātāyāṃ tasmāttyakṣe kalevaram \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. How could Visvakarma, my father becomes a monkey? Perhaps it has been due to the birth of an inauspicious daughter as I am. Therefore, I shall give up my body.

## \|\| 65.146-147 \|\|

*iti saṃcintya manasā ṛtadhvajamuvāca ha \|*  
*paritrāyasva māṃ brahman pāpopahatacetanām \|\| 146 \|\|*

*pitṛchanī martumicchāmi tadanujñātumarhasi \|*  
*athovāca munistanvī mā viṣādaṃ kṛthādhunā \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. She made up her mind to suicide and said to Rtadhvaja- О Brahmana! please, absolve all sins committed by me. I am the sole cause for this state of my father. I therefore, desire to die soon. Please, allow me. Then the sage consoled her and said- "Don't weep any more in this matter."

## \|\| 65.148-149 \|\|

*bhāvyasya naiva nāśo'sti tanmā tyākṣīḥ kalevaram \|*  
*bhaviṣyati pitā tubhyaṃ bhūyo'pyamaravarddhakiḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

*jāto'patye ghṛtācyāṃ tu nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*ityevamukte vacane muninā bhāvitātmanā \|\| 149 \|\|*

148-149. The future events cannot be ceased by death. Hence, don't abandon your body. Your father shall again become a celestial artisan when Ghrtaci gives birth to a son. “There is no scope of doubt in this regard,” narrated by the hermit, whose soul was purified by meditation.

## \|\| 65.150-151 \|\|
